The old fallbacks (potion, rest) remain under the floor and with `--fight-stamina-full 0`.

The floors (`ManaOrder.ManaFloorOf`, `StaminaFloorOf`; `FightScenario.ComputeFloors`, logged as "mana: D88 floors: ..."): the mana floor is the bolt's own try floor plus the least mana at which a Stamina to Mana press lands at least a quarter of the time, plus the same for one Revitalize Self press, each never under 5. The stamina floor is the least stamina at which a landed transfer gives at least the transfer's base plus the Revitalize's base. For a level-80 mage (Mana Conversion 258, stamina 275; Stamina to Mana Self VI base 60 power 250, Revitalize Self VI base 70 power 250, Flame Bolt VI base 30 power 250, from the dat's spell table) the mana floor is 15 (5 + 5 + 5) and the stamina floor 174 of 275 (a landing gives 130 = 60 + 70). A landing takes 1.5 presses at 15 mana, 2.8 at 5 and 10.2 at 1 (`RefillFloorsDatTests`).

**The drain when health runs low (D88's health rule, F7).** With no Melee Defense the mage takes the damage, so the fight holds two health lines, both options and Lifestone's own numbers: `--fight-drain-under` (default 50, the health share under which the rule starts) and `--fight-drain-until` (default 75, the safe line at which the bolts begin again; never under the first). Between them the rule holds, a hysteresis. Under the first line, with a living target in line and range, the fight casts Drain Health Other instead of the bolt. With no target in reach it casts Heal Self at the highest level the pack's scarabs pay (the keeper's heal). Before F7 the fight did nothing about its own health: it bolted whatever it was, the vitals keeper healed between fights (VitalsKeeper, VitalsMeans), and HarmHealScript is only the gate's test script. The upkeep line sits under it: the drain starts under 50%, and the upkeep stops the fight under 30% (`AutopilotOptions.HealthFloorPercent`: 50 with the drain rule off, `--fight-drain-under=0`; otherwise 60% of `--fight-drain-under` and at most 30, `AutopilotScenario.HealthFloorWithDrainPercent`).

Drain Health Other is a Life Magic transfer: ids 1237 to 1242 (I to VI, powers 38, 88, 138, 188, 238, 288, base mana 10 to 60), 2328 (VII, Vitality Siphon, power 325, base mana 60), and 4643 (the incantation, power 400, base mana 68; it has no transfer row in the pinned world SQL, so the picker does not offer it, `TODO(m5-drain-viii-row)`). The level-80 pack pays VI with the Pyreal Scarab and the level-126 pack pays VII with the Platinum Scarab (`LevelFloor` kept). The line is one of `ArenaProfile.Extras` (`ProfileRole.LifeDrain`), so the build learns it with the others. ACE's rule (`WorldObject_Magic.cs` @95ef426d, `HandleCastSpell_Transfer` 697-760): the target loses round(current health x proportion), cut to the transfer cap (721-727); the caster gains round(taken x (1 - loss)) (732), cut to its missing health, and itself cut to the cap (737-749). The rows from the pinned world SQL v0.9.296 (proportion, loss, cap) are I 0.25, -1, 60; II 0.25, -0.6, 80; III 0.25, -0.33, 100; IV 0.25, 0, 100; V 0.3, 0, 120; VI 0.4, 0.25, 150; VII 0.5, 0.5, 180. On a 400-health tusker VI heals 112, VII 90 and V 120, so the highest level is not the best one. The resist is `MagicDefenseCheck` (104-113), the 0.03 logistic of the caster's Life Magic against the target's Magic Defense. The chat proof is "You gain N points of health due to casting <spell> on <name>" (853).

The level is chosen at the moment of casting by `DrainPicker` (`Session/Vitals`, engine-free and allocation-free, so the harm-heal and the death handler can read it later). Every input is read live: the mage's Life Magic (`GearCasts.TryCurrentSkill`, buffs up), its Mana Conversion (`ManaOrder.TryManaConversion`), its health and mana, the target's health (the last health update, timed against the ground profile's max_health) and the distance. The score is the chance times the heal if it lands, cut to the health missing so that overshoot earns nothing, per second of casting. Of the levels within 10% of the best, the cheapest in mana is taken. When even the best expected heal is under 3% of the mage's maximum health, the answer is no drain and the bolt goes (a nearly dead tusker). The chance is the cast chance (`GearCasts.Chance`, 0.07 factor) times the target's pass chance (0.03 logistic). The targets' measures are ground profile values: `black-spawn-den-aluvian.json` gives the Tusker Slave max_health 400 and magic_defence 200, and the Tusker Guard 260 and 225 (the pinned world SQL's `weenie_properties_attribute_2nd` type 1 current_Level and `weenie_properties_skill` type 15 init_Level, without ACE's formula share for the skill: `TODO(m5-drain-magic-defence-formula)`). A target the profile gives none for is assumed large with an even resist, named once (`TODO(m5-drain-target-stats)`). Left named: `TODO(m5-drain-cast-time)` (the cast time is taken as equal across the line). `TODO(m5-drain-resistance-mods)` is closed (M6 14 drain resistance, after three drains of 0 on Armored Tuskers and the climber's death on 2026-11-14): the target kind's `ResistHealthDrain` scales the take before the cap (`DrainSituation.TargetDrainResist`, read by `Vitals/DrainResist.cs`); the caster's boost mod stays 1 (a player with no healing rating). Each pick is one log line, `health: drain pick: <spell>, expected heal, chance, mana, why`, and each drain one line, `health: drain: <spell> on 0x<guid> at health x of y`. The verdict gains `drains= heals= health_min=` (report-only).

The mana floor holds a drain's cost too. Each offered level has the bolt's kind of floor, `min(ceiling, ManaOrder.FloorOf(ceiling, power, ceiling, Mana Conversion read now) + the D88 reserve for one Stamina to Mana press and one Revitalize Self press)`, the ceiling being the level's base mana (VI 60, VII 60; Heal Self VI 70). A level is offered only when the mana held is at or over its floor. With none paid, the fight casts the bolt it would have cast, since its own order has already funded it. The stamina order of D88 runs first (the transfer, then the Revitalize Self refill, then the fight): the drain is a step of `Choose` after `BoltNeedsMana`. Safety: a cast that did not land (not a resist), or 8 casts in a row that did not end the low state, set the rule aside for 30 s, named.

**Self-defence (F4, F15).** A living creature that attacks the player becomes the fight's target at once, before the profile's targets, whatever the profile says of it (avoided, no-go, outside the level band). It stays the target until it is dead, gone from the object table, or has not attacked for `--fight-defend-forget-s` (default 20 s; 0 is off; 0 to 600, Lifestone's own bound). The fight hears the attack on the session bus: the defender and evasion notices (GameEvent 0x01B2 and 0x01B4, the `CombatEvent`s `DefenseHit` and `DefenseEvaded`) and the Magic-typed chat lines a creature's spell writes to the player (ACE @95ef426d `SpellProjectile.cs` 810-845, `WorldObject_Magic.cs` 199 and 1429). Every notice names the attacker and none gives its guid. ACE's CurrentAttacker private update carries the guid and is not decoded (`TODO(m3-autotarget-attacker-id)`), so the attacker is the nearest living creature of that name in the object table (`NearestLivingCreatureNamed`). A name with none is logged once as `TODO(m5-defend-attacker-unseen)`. The pick asks `DefenceStep` first: the nearest attacker in cast range with a clear line is the target, wherever it stands, a no-go cell included. With none, the nearest attacker decides. In a no-go cell the fight holds, since nothing is walked into a no-go cell (logged once: "stands in the no-go cell ... holding"). Otherwise it walks, and the walk phase drops that walk the frame an attacker is in range with a clear line. The walk has no leg toward a given creature, so it is the tour's next leg (`TODO(m5-defend-walk-to)`). The hold has its own bound (F15): `--fight-defend-hold-s` (default 30; 0 to 600; 0 is no bound). After it, the attacker is dropped for the profile's targets, logged once, and not fought back at while it stays in the table. Heal Self comes before a hold and before a walk. Each attacker is logged once: "self-defence: <name> 0x<guid> attacked (<how>); fighting it before the targets". Its kill counts in `kills=` and `target_kills=`, reaches the respawn schedule (`GroundTour.Killed`), and the verdict gains `defended=<n>` after `target_kills=` (report-only). Not covered: the loot step runs before the pick, so an attacker is fought after the corpse in hand is done; a bolt in flight and the mana wait finish first. This closes the first rehearsal's finding, in which a Virindi attacked the mage and the mage kept to the tuskers.

**The one live picker (D90, F10).** The fight's toolbox is one picker, `FightPicker` (engine-free and allocation-free per decision), fed by a snapshot of the fight at that moment (`FightScenario.Picker.cs`: the mage's vitals and skills, the target's health and range, the scarabs in the pack). At each decision with a target picked and the bolt's mana order passed, `Choose` calls `PickerDecide`. D88's drain-health floor comes first (F7's `DrainPicker` picks the level). Then the picker scores the bolt; F9's best war option (`WarSpellPicker.Choose`, scaled by its seconds a kill over the bolt's); Drain Health Other VI or VII as an attack; and every debuff at the plan cap's level, I to VII (VI at 80; M6 item 1 f), each in expected all-in seconds to finish the target. The least wins, and a tie keeps the bolt. A debuff's or a drain's score is the bolt's minus its `FightDebuffs` net seconds. The profile's `opener` names the debuffs a target allows (the hint) and stays the default when the picker cannot score (no bolt row or no target health: `TODO(f10-picker-data)`, named once for each kind of target; M6 item 1 f). F8's `TryBeginOpener` casts the vulnerability the picker chooses. Two measured rates feed the score (`FightRates`), both exponentially weighted means with weight 0.2. The dance's seconds a mana point is seeded at 0.09; then each landed dance adds its seconds plus the Revitalize Self seconds since the last dance, over the net mana. The heal's seconds a health point is seeded at each decision from Drain Health Other VI's yield on the target at the live Life Magic (cast seconds plus its mana at the dance's rate, over the expected heal); then each landed drain or heal adds its seconds plus its mana at the dance's rate, over the health gained. The incoming damage rate is the tally's damage taken over a 20 s time constant, fight-wide (`TODO(f10-incoming-per-attacker)`: the notices name the attacker and the tally sums them).

The log writes one line when the pick changes, never per repeated cast: `pick: <line> <level> on <name> 0x<guid> | all-in <s> s vs bolt <s> s | hit <p>% | mana <m> | why <reason>`. Each debuff that does not win gets one line once: `pick: <spell> never wins: <ACE reason>` for Imperil, Exhaustion, Vulnerability and Defenselessness, and `pick: <spell> does not win here: it saves x s and costs y s (net z s) ...` for the rest. The attribute debuffs carry `TODO(f10-target-attributes)`, since no source gives the fight their attributes. The stamina drain's line reads `pick: Drain Stamina Other VI on <name> 0x<guid> | stamina a a second vs Revitalize Self b | hit p% | mana m | why the stamina floor: the drain refills faster`. The verdict's `picks=` counts the casts per spell the picker chose, as `picks=Flame_Bolt_VI:40,Fire_Vulnerability_Other_VI:12,Drain_Health_Other_VI:3` (spaces as underscores, apostrophes dropped). It sits after `openers=`, in place of F9's shape counts, and is report-only in its first gate.

**The opener, the war spells, the debuffs and the stamina drain (D89, D90; F8, F9, F10, F11).** A target's optional `opener` (in `ArenaProfile.Extras`) names the debuff the fight casts first. The den's Tusker Slave opens with Fire Vulnerability Other, and a Tusker Guard gets bolts only (the owner's choice). ACE multiplies a war bolt's damage by the fire vulnerability (SpellProjectile.cs:526-557, EnchantmentManager.cs:925-939 at 95ef426d): x2.5 at VI (1108) and x2.85 at VII (2170). Imperil does nothing to a bolt. The opener's level is the highest the ground's plan cap, the spellbook, the cast chance and the pack allow (VI at 80, VII at 126 with Platinum). A resisted or fizzled cast is pressed again up to `--fight-opener-tries` (default 3, 0 to 10, Lifestone's own; 0 is off). A target under half its health skips it. The opener burns the same scarab and tapers a Flame Bolt of its level does, about one cast a Slave and up to three on resists. The verdict field `openers=sent:n,landed:n,resisted:n,skipped:n` is report-only in its first gate. The opener's ids are 21, 1104-1108, 2170 (Inferno's Gift) and 4481.

The war spell is chosen live by `WarSpellPicker` (`Session/Mage/WarSpellPicker.cs`; the glue is `FightScenario.WarPick.cs`). For each option it counts the casts the cast target needs at the option's mean hit, each cast costing its gesture, 0.4 s of overhead and 0.09 s a mana point of the dance (registered estimates the rehearsal measures), over the kills the casts make. The least seconds a kill wins, and a tie keeps the bolt. One `war pick:` line is logged when the pick changes, and `picks=` counts the choices. At level 80 the data keeps Flame Bolt VI for a lone full-health Slave or Guard. For a Slave the all-in seconds a kill are 10.1 for the bolt, 14.8 for the streak, 13.1 for the volley, 22.7 for the blast, 10.0 for the arc (with no way to test its lob) and 25.8 for the ring. The picks that pay are two. A streak pays for a target one streak finishes (a hit of about 62 against the hit points left, at any range in reach). Cassius' Ring of Fire pays for three or more tuskers within 3 m of the mage: 9.4 s a kill against 10.1 on three Slaves, 7.1 on four, and 6.3 against 6.8 on three Guards. It never pays for two (13.8 against 10.1). The ring is built in, and its scarabs are carried since F10 (a Diamond Scarab line, keep 6, trip and stop under 2; about one lost every 450 casts). It needs 80 mana in hand. Volleys and blasts never win on the den's numbers. Arcs are left out: a lob does not track a moving target (WorldObject_Magic.cs:1728), and no arc-line sweep exists (`TODO(m5-war-pick-arc-line)`). Walls (Slithering Flames, 1841: 10 projectiles in a line, 80 mana, about 63 a projectile) pay only on tuskers standing in a line in front of the mage. The spell is in no profile line and is not learned, so the walls stay numbers only. The war line's mean hits and mana at War Magic 361 and Mana Conversion 258 are: bolt 146.5 and 6.59 mana, streak 62.2 and 13.10, volley and blast 59.0 a projectile and 7.83, ring 75.5 a projectile and 10.88. The damage rows are ACE world SQL v0.9.296 (table `spell`) and the projectile speeds of the projectile weenies (bolt 15 m/s, streak 45, arc 40, ring 2); no code is ported.

The debuffs are picked by the same scale, and most never win. The data per debuff is for a level-80 mage against a Tusker Slave (Light Weapons 287, Magic Defense 219, health 400, body damage 60), with illustrative rates: the target hitting for 25 a second, a heal of 0.04 s a health point, and the dance at 0.09 s a mana point. The net seconds at VI, where positive pays: Weakness Other -5.5 at 400 health (it cuts the damage taken by 14%, so it pays only in a fight longer than about 20 s, +13.6 at 4000 health). Clumsiness Other -6.8. Light Weapon Ineptitude Other -6.7. Slowness Other -6.2 (the swing takes 0.94 s instead of 0.8 s; `TODO(f11-swing-seconds)`: the swing length is not in the data read, so a 1.2 s stand-in is used and a debuff reports unscored at 0). Bafflement Other, which is the Focus debuff, -6.8. Feeblemind Other, which is the Self debuff, -6.8. Frailty Other -6.0 (a Slave at full health loses 17 of its 400). Magic Yield Other -6.6. Harm Other -4.7 (a third of a bolt's damage for 15.6 mana, against 6.6 for the bolt). Drain Stamina Other -2.5 at 0.05 s a stamina point. Imperil Other, Vulnerability Other (Melee Defense), Defenselessness Other (Missile Defense) and Exhaustion Other have no value at all: ACE's reasons are constant strings in `FightDebuffs`. Imperil lowers an armour level that a war bolt does not read; Vulnerability and Defenselessness act on the target's defence against melee and missiles, which a mage does not roll against; Exhaustion stops only a monster's stamina regeneration. Fire Vulnerability Other pays +3.65 on a 400-health Slave (+3.87 at VII): 10.46 s of fight over a Slave, more the more health is left (1.3 s at 100, 5.2 at 200, 10.5 at 400, 41.8 at 1600). It does not pay on a target a bolt kills anyway, and it breaks even near 260 health. Drain Health Other pays +4.0 (VII +4.2), but only while the mage is hurt: at full health ACE scales the cast to nothing. The picker's verdicts follow: a full-health Slave gets the vulnerability and then bolts (a landed vulnerability makes the next evaluation "already on"); a Guard gets bolts, since its entry names no opener; a mage at 60%, over D88's floor, casts Drain Health Other VI as an attack against a healthy Slave; and the rest never win. The corrected names are these: ACE's Bafflement is the Focus debuff and its Feeblemind the Self debuff, Vulnerability is Melee Defense, Defenselessness is Missile Defense, and Magic Yield is Magic Defense. A debuff's cast is paid under the target's blows, so a debuff that cuts the target's damage needs a long fight, while one that changes the mage's own damage (the vulnerability) does not.

Drain Stamina Other is the refill beside Revitalize Self (F10, F15). When D88's order says Revitalize Self, the target is alive, and it is in the drain's range and in line, the fight casts Drain Stamina Other at it instead, when `FightPicker.StaminaDrainWins`. That is so when the drain's expected stamina over its all-in seconds (the cast, the mana at the dance's rate, and the blows taken while casting at the heal's rate) beats Revitalize Self's (VI: 80 a cast). It is never an attack (F11: -2.5 s). The target's stamina is not in the profile, so it is taken as enough for the cap to bind (`TODO(f10-target-stamina)`). A cast that did not land (not a resist) sets the drain aside for 30 s. The yield is measured (F15): the stamina after the landing minus the stamina before, against the gain expected if it lands. Under `StaminaDrainMinYieldShare` (0.25) the drain is set aside for that target and Revitalize Self takes over; above it, the share scales the drain's score. The line is in `ArenaProfile.Extras` (I to VI 1249 to 1254, VII 2330 Vigor Siphon, the incantation 4645; SpellsToLearn 277 to 285).

**The buffs at 80 (F12).** The cycle casts 24 lines at Level VI (power 250, 2,700 s, which is 45 minutes): the focus and willpower lines, the creature, war, item, life and mana masteries, the four attributes (Strength, Endurance, Coordination and Quickness, which raise burden, health and stamina, and Melee Defense), Arcane Enlightenment, Magic Resistance (Magic Defense), Invulnerability (Melee Defense, which the mage does not train), Impregnability (Missile Defense), Armor Self (armour level +200), Bludgeon Protection (bludgeoning damage taken x0.4), the Regeneration, Rejuvenation and Mana Renewal lines (x1.85), Impenetrability and Bludgeon Bane on the worn armour, Hermetic Link (x1.6) and Defender (+0.15). The order is focus, willpower, the creature mastery, the other masteries, then the rest in profile order, then the upgrade pass. The buffed skills after a cycle are War 364, Life 326, Creature 325 and Item 325, and a cycle costs 1,640 base mana (live: 26 lines in 56 s). Level VII is not cast. It needs a skill of 332 for the owner's 0.9 cast chance, and Creature, Item and Life sit at 325 to 326. The tuskers do bludgeoning damage and carry no spell book, so no element line is added. The recast timing is unchanged. The upkeep checks every 5 s (`UpkeepDue`, `--buff-rebuff-margin-s`, default 300 s); a line lapses only if the time from crossing the margin to its recast exceeds 300 s. The headroom is about 150 s at the model's numbers. The residual risk is named: the health floor is checked before the buff in each 5 s check, so a health crisis lasting longer than that headroom would delay the buff.

**The autopilot's bind and the journey's level (F14).** A fresh mage at level 80 is not bound to a lifestone, so its first recall is refused with 0x049E (YouMustLinkToLifestoneToRecall; ACE `WorldObject_Magic.cs` 1087-1093, `WeenieError.cs` 658). The client cannot read the bind beforehand: ACE's player description carries only the last outside death position, not the Sanctuary or the linked lifestone. So the autopilot reacts to the refusal. A failed `recall-home` whose text carries 0x049E runs the bind station once (log: "autopilot: no lifestone bind: binding at <home town> first"), re-arms the recall-once flag, and classifies the state again. The bind walks from where the mage stands to the profile's home lifestone (`HuntingGround.Home`; any ground, no den constant), and it sets the linked lifestone that Lifestone Recall reads (Lifestone Tie, 2644; `WorldObject_Magic.cs` 966-976). A second refusal stops by name, `failed:travel:no-lifestone-bind`, because a recall cannot cure it. The journey takes `--mage-level` (50 to 126, default 126): `--scenario=journey --journey=mage --mage-level=80` verifies the level-80 traditional build (`MageTemplate.BuildFor`). Another journey refuses the option. This closes `TODO(m5-7-journey-mage-level)`, and the gate's journey at 126 is unchanged.

**The review's fixes (F15).** The fight review's findings were fixed as follows. (1) A kill notice that names the target is held as a pending kill. The target is marked killed, and the tour, the defence count and the loot are told, only when the object table shows it dead (health 0, Dead motion) or gone. A notice the table does not confirm within `FightScenario.KillNoticeSeconds` (2 s) was a neighbour's of the same name: it is logged once ("that creature lives ... it stays the target") and the target stays. The named creature is kept out of the pick while the notice is pending. `target_kills=` still counts by name, as a report-only count. (2) The upkeep's health stop is set as in the vitals paragraph above. (3) `DrainFirst`: with the drain rule on, a drain level known, health wanted by the rule and a target picked, the drain is cast before the stamina refill, and the pre-emptive transfer and the refill branches wait. (4) The stamina drain's yield is measured, as above. (5) Heal Self comes before a Hold and before a Walk of the self-defence, and the hold has its bound. (6) Nits: a Fire Vulnerability pick whose opener is settled re-decides without debuffs, so the war picks are weighed without a direct fall to the bolt; `EndFight` stops and tallies a pending opener and a pending stamina drain; and the dance (Stamina to Mana) and the Revitalize refill respect the plan cap (`FightRefill.Fill(..., maxLevel)`, `FillDanceLevels(..., maxLevel)`, `LevelCapFor`). The cap binds every level the fight casts, so a level-80 mage casts VI whatever scarabs it carries, and D88's "the highest the pack's scarabs pay" is read under the cap. Heal Self and the drain-health levels are unchanged. Still open from the review: the drain does not count toward the refill's in-a-row bound, and a vital update that lags the landing line would read as a zero yield (harmless, since Revitalize runs).

**Buff lines never lapse in a batch (D126 a).** Soak round 12 lost 12 to 15 lines together twice: at 09:43 UTC (about 30 s, 09:43:05 to 09:43:18) and in the 10:28 trip. The lines had been cast together and so came due together. At 09:43 the fight was in a two-minute walk (a 48 m leg that the runner replanned around creatures to 491 m), so no decision point came, and the 30 s hard floor never ran. At 10:27 the sell trip left with the lines due 23 to 48 s later. The fixes are below (`FightScenario.Refresh.cs`, `AutopilotScenario.cs`, `BuffCycle.cs`).

- **The batch.** Every pick sorts the lines by their time left. The k-th soonest line (counting from 1) is due when it has less left than the threshold plus k × 1.5 s (`BatchLineSeconds`; round 12's hard floor recast 13 lines in 19 s). So a batch starts early enough for its last line. At a lull and before a trip, every line due within 60 s (`BatchGapSeconds`) of the last line taken joins the batch. A batch once started is finished, because its end is kept on the clock. The log line carries `(batch: the lines under N s go together)`.
- **The walk.** In the Walk phase, a line under the hard floor (as a batch) drops the walk. The check runs once a second, and the next decision recasts the line (`buff refresh: the walk is dropped: ...`, `WalksDroppedForBuffs`).
- **The trip.** Before the stop for a trip (the counters' trip or the forced trip), the autopilot asks the fight (`IBuffRefreshFight.RequestLeaveRefresh`) to recast every line due within the trip's expected length plus the lookahead margin. The stop then waits for that, for 120 s at most (`buff refresh: leave: ...`). The trip's length is an exponentially weighted mean (weight 0.3) of the trips made, from the trip station's start to its end. It is seeded at 120 s, because round 12's trips took 97, 121 and 119 s. A stop asked before the fight's first pick ends the fight at once (F30) and runs no refresh.
- **The start's pass.** A start's or restart's buff station (`AutopilotScenario.BuffSpec`, `JourneyStations.StartPassArgument`) uses one buff cycle as its margin: `--buff-start-margin-s`, 2,700 s on the autopilot, which is VI's duration. So it recasts every line, and no line left from before falls due on its own in the first fight. The upkeep's station (`UpkeepSpec`) keeps the re-buff margin. Outside the autopilot the option defaults to the re-buff margin, as before.

The known-state after a trip still goes straight to the fight when an enchantment is up (`TODO(m4-journey-buffed)` is unchanged). The trip's refresh covers the lines due inside the trip, and the fight's hard floor covers any line that lapsed.

**The experience planner raises only what this mage gains from (D126 b).** In round 12 the spending rule bought Loyalty 120 → 121 (421,961 XP, 08:12 UTC) and Run 120 → 121 (421,961, 10:29), 843,922 in all. It bought no Salvaging. The level-80 build itself holds 120 ranks (5,470,950 XP) in each of the three. The relay's figure of about 1.6 M is not borne out by round 12's raise lines. Each skill was checked against ACE (ACEmulator/ACE@95ef426d, `Source/ACE.Server`):

- **Loyalty is dropped.** It is read only by the allegiance's pass-up: `AllegianceManager.DoPassXP`, `Managers/AllegianceManager.cs:255-265`, through `Creature_Skills.cs:72` `GetCurrentLoyalty`, an `IPlayer` wrapper "used by the AllegianceManager to handle passup". The pass-up returns at once when the vassal has no patron (`:256-257`). A solo mage is sworn to no one, so Loyalty earns nothing.
- **Salvaging is dropped.** It is read only by the salvage operation (`Player_Crafting.cs:142` `HandleSalvaging`; `:220` the value factor; `:313-327` the amount), and item 7 runs no salvaging (tinkering is later).
- **Run is capped at 81 ranks.** ACE runs a player at `MovementSystem.GetRunRate(burden, Run, 1)` (`Monster_Navigation.cs:346-368`, `Physics/Animation/MovementSystem.cs:20-28`): (loadMod × Run / (Run + 200) × 11 + 4) / 4. The load modifier is 1 under a full burden (`Physics/Common/EncumbranceSystem.cs:32-40`), and the mage carries about half. The client's `Lifestone.Data.Motion.MovementSystem.GetRunRate` is the same formula.
  - The mage's Run is 238 at 121 ranks ("Your base Run skill is now 238!"), plus Quickness Self VI's 35, so 273. The rate is 2.59, and one more point is worth 0.095% of the walking time.
  - Round 12 walked at most 27% of its 4.57 hours: the runner's 274 runs took 3,888 s, and ACE's MoveTo to a corpse took at most 608 s over 677 opens. The kills earned about 5.7 M XP an hour (7,053,567 in 73.6 minutes and 5,695,297 in 59.7 minutes).
  - So one more point brings about 1,465 XP an hour. The 121st rank cost 421,961, which is about 288 hours to pay back.
  - The rule (`RunPayback`, `MageSpendingPlanner.cs`) buys a rank of Run while it pays for itself within one soak (12 hours, D85's window). On the dat's trained list that is 81 ranks, whose last step costs 21,837 for about 1,840 an hour. At rank 120 the payback is 286 hours, at 100 it is 57 hours, and at 50 it is 1.4 hours.

`MageShares.Dance` (the soak mage's shares, every level under 126) sets Loyalty and Salvaging to weight 0 and caps Run. A weight-0 stat is left out of the plan, and the spending rule never raises a stat that is not in the plan. The capped Run moves first in the pool, so what its cap leaves rolls on to the stats after it. At level 80 the plan moves from Run 119 to 81 ranks, with no Loyalty or Salvaging. The freed experience goes to the rest of the pool (Strength 106 → 115, and Endurance and Max Stamina by their weight), and the remainder stays under 1%. The soak mage already holds 121 ranks of Run and 121 of Loyalty, so it raises none of the three again. The level-126 D19 split is unchanged, because it is the owner's decision. Pinned by `MageSpendingD126Tests` and `MageLevelPlanDatTests`.

**The mute check from the run's start (D126 c).** `tools\play.ps1` judges an automated run silent by the game's start-up line `audio service installed ... muted=true`. With `--log-copies=file` it reads that line from the isolated logs folder. A long run rolls `lifestone.log` (`--log-max-mb=16`), so after round 12 the line was in `lifestone.1.log`, and a clean run exited with code 3. The check now reads the start of every `lifestone*.log` written since the game was started (`Get-PlayRunLogHead` in `tools\lib\Play.psm1`), oldest first (the highest N). The previous run's copy, which the game's start makes as `lifestone.1.log` with its old write time, is left out.

**The packs, one job each (D121; `Session/Mage/PackLayout.cs`, `PackSorter.cs`; `PackLayoutTests`).** The main pack holds the loot to sell, the coins and the trade notes, nothing else; the four foci keep their side slots; the three side packs (two Packs and a Sack, 24 items each: ACE weenies 136 and 166, ItemsCapacity 24) take one job each. `PackRules` gives an item its job: money and a note the main pack; a spell component (ItemType 0x1000 or a class of the ground's `components`) the components pack; a stock line that is no component (the Mana Potion), a mana stone (ItemType 0x80000), a healing kit, a spare of a worn or wielded kit line, or a piece the self-equip took off (`PackMemory.Rotation`) the kit pack; a find the keep-aside rule kept (`SaleMemory.KeptAside`) the review pack; everything else the main pack. Gear already in the kit pack and an owner's find already in the review pack stay. `PackLayout.Assign` chooses the packs by a rule, logged: a pack that already holds a job's items keeps that job, and the jobs left go to the packs left in their slot order, so the empty packs of 2026-10-29 become components, kit and review in that order and keep those jobs once filled. Every station that moves an item follows the layout. The loot step's plan (`MageLootRules.Plan(..., layout, packRules)`) counts each kept item against the free slots of its job's pack and falls back to the main pack when that pack is full; the shared looter picks it up into that pack (`LootRules.DestinationOf`, `CorpseLooter`). The death's take-back is `LayoutTakeAll`. The resupply sorts the packs at the start of the visit and again after the buys, since ACE creates a bought ware in the main pack. The sale reads the main pack only (`ShopLeg.PackItems`), so D99's drop of the cheapest comes from the main pack only. The start-up audit's packs check runs `PackSorter` once per audit (`autopilot audit packs: ...`, `packs=<moved>/<planned>` in the summary). The trip's slot trigger still reads the main pack (`LogisticsCounters`, `PackView.MainPackFree`). The lines are `packs: layout (<why>): components='Pack' 0x... (side slot 1); ...; packs main=<free>/<cap> components=<free>/24 kit=... review=...` and one `packs: move '<name>' 0x<guid> main -> <job> pack 0x<pack> (<why>): done` per move. The soak line ends with `free_components= free_kit= free_review= self_equips= stone_refills= stone_captures=`.

**The shoes (D122; `SelfEquipJudge.PickFootwear`).** The mage wears footwear from its own items only while the feet are free. ACE refuses any clothing whose ClothingPriority overlaps a worn piece's (`WieldedLocationIsAvailable` through `GetEquippedClothingArmor`, Creature_Equipment.cs 50-58 and 93-101; "You must remove your X to wield Y", Player_Inventory.cs 1801-1809). The Faran Robe with Hood is worn at 0x7F01, which holds FootWear 0x100, and its ClothingPriority 0x17F00 includes Feet 0x10000, so today the step logs `gear: shoes: feet covered by Faran Robe with Hood ...` and wears nothing. D129 (the owner): the mage keeps the robe and wears no shoes, as retail. The pick stays dormant and acts only if the feet are ever free (then the best armour level among the pieces whose requirements are met, then the lightest). No shoe is ever bought (`TODO(m5-shoes-vendor)` is closed), and looted footwear is loot like anything else.

**The self-equip and the items' mana (D125; `Session/Mage/SelfEquip.cs`, `ItemManaKeeper.cs`, `Scenarios/Journey/ResupplyStation.Gear.cs`; `SelfEquipTests`).** A better caster has a higher war damage factor on the plan's element. The factor is the caster's ElementalDamageMod (float 152), but only when its DamageType (int 45) is the spell's element (WorldObject_Weapon.cs 382-401; Flame Bolt's `e_Type` is 16, fire). On a tie the higher ManaConversionMod (float 144) wins, then more useful cantrips. A wearable, jewellery piece or trinket is worn when it casts a useful cantrip that no worn piece casts and a slot is free (coverage for clothing and armour, the location for jewellery, a ring or a bracelet on the free side). The useful cantrips are the ground's keep-aside list. Both kinds must meet the wield requirements (int 158-160 and 270-272; Skill, RawSkill, Level and Training are read) and the activation requirements (Arcane Lore against ItemDifficulty 109, UseRequiresLevel 369, ItemSkillLevelLimit 115). Any other find goes to the review pack and is never sold. The loot step wears a free-slot wearable at once. A caster swap waits for the home visit's gear phase, in peace, and the old caster goes to the kit pack as rotation gear. The gear phase also keeps the worn items' mana. A charged stone is used on the player when a worn piece is under half its maximum or has under two hours left at its ManaRate (ManaStone.cs 119-190: rationed over every equipped item that needs mana; the stone is destroyed on its ManaStoneDestroyChance, 0.2 for the Greater Mana Stone, else left empty). While fewer than two charged stones are held and something worn uses mana, an empty stone may be used on a junk magic item of the main pack (weighed against its sale since S2b, below). That drains `round(efficiency x mana)` into the stone (2.0 for the Greater Mana Stone) and destroys the item (ManaStone.cs 84-117); a Retained item is refused. The lines are `gear: swap in|wear|review '<name>' 0x<guid>: <why with the numbers>` and `gear mana: refill|capture: ...`. A worn item's "<item> cast <spell> on you" and "Your <item> is low on Mana." reach the log through the chat tap (category `chat`, `type=7`, ACE ChatMessageType.Magic). After a death, and at every start-up audit, the worn set goes back on (S2d, closes `TODO(m5-self-equip-death-rewear)`; `Session/Mage/WornRestorer.cs`, `WornRestorerTests`). While the mage lives, the autopilot takes a snapshot of every worn piece that is no caster, by object id and location, every 5 s (never at 0 health or after a death is seen), and writes it into its checkpoint (`worn`). `WornRestorer` then wears, one action at a time: (1) the remembered pieces at their locations; (2) any clothing or armour held whose coverage no worn piece overlaps, by best armour level, then lightest (with no memory, as at the login of 2026-10-29 after the gate's scripted death, this is how the Shirt and the Wide Breeches went back on); (3) the cantrip wearables; (4) the one best caster held, the review and kit packs included. Each wear and refusal is logged as `gear: restore: ...`; the audit's summary gains `worn_restored=<n>`, and the death handler logs `handler: worn_restored=<n>`.

**A worn item's mana, the drain against the sale, the kit's stones and the requirements (S2b, the owner's addition to D125; `Session/Mage/WornManaWatch.cs`, `ItemManaKeeper.cs`, `SelfEquip.cs`; `ItemManaTests`, `ItemManaDatTests`).** ACE burns a worn item whose spells are on by `-ManaRate x 5` on the player's 5 s heartbeat (Player_Tick.cs 110-116 and 624-660; WorldObject_Tick.cs 44-56). Setting ItemCurMana sends nothing (WorldObject_Properties.cs 2163-2167), so the client learns the mana only from an appraisal, or as a fraction from a one-shot QueryItemMana (0x0263 and 0x0264, Player.cs 440-455, WorldObject.cs 621-637; the client has no verb for it, `TODO(m5-query-item-mana)`). The only lines are "Your X is low on Mana." under 120 s left (Player_Tick.cs 662-679) and "Your X is out of Mana." at 0 (681-699), both F7E0 lines of ChatMessageType.Magic (7); the item's spells drop 2 s later.

The autopilot's `WornManaWatch` therefore re-appraises each worn magic item every 300 s and predicts the mana between reads at its rate. Each read logs `gear mana: read '<name>' 0x<guid> <cur>/<max> (<pct>%), burns <rate>/s while its spells are on: <h> h left; predicted <p> from the read <s> s ago`. The two server lines log `gear mana: ALARM: ...`, and "out" sets the prediction to 0. Round 12's Compass casts Major War Magic Aptitude (spell 2534, base mana 10 in the dat). ACE therefore gives it a ManaRate of -1/120 (`CalculateManaRate`, LootGenerationFactory_Magic.cs 105-112), a point every 2 minutes, and an ItemMaxMana of 120 to 200 at workmanship mod 1 (`RollItemMaxMana`, 67-100: jewellery takes 12 to 20 times the base). That is 4 to 6.7 hours from full to empty, and half after 2 to 3.3 hours. The examine window's "Mana: N / M." is the appraisal's number when the window opened (`GameExaminePanel`, as retail's `Appraisal_ShowMagicInfo`); it changes only when the item is appraised again.

The capture is weighed against the sale. The captured mana is `round(efficiency x ItemCurMana)` (ManaStone.cs 108). The efficiency is PropertyFloat 87, an assessment property, else the world SQL's table: Minor 0.1, Lesser 0.25, Mana Stone 0.6, Moderate 1.2, Greater 2, Major 3. The use's tracker reads ACE's capture line, "The Mana Stone drains N points of mana from the X.\nThe X is destroyed." (ManaStone.cs 110), as the success it is (S2c: the rehearsal of 2026-10-29 read it as "nothing happened"); its N is the efficiency times the appraised mana (2.0 x 2,934 = 5,868). The caster swap is one pick per visit, the best of every caster held with the wielded one included (`SelfEquipJudge.BestCaster`), and a caster off the plan's element never wins a tie (S2c: the rehearsal wielded an Electric Sceptre on its mana conversion and never sent the better Fire Sceptre's swap, because only the first swap of the item-by-item loop was sent). The captured mana is valued at 1.8 pyreals a point (the Titan Mana Charge's Value 9,000 for 5,000 points) and set against D96's payout at the best buyer; the item is drained only when its mana is worth more. Each item weighed logs `gear mana: weigh '<name>' 0x<guid>: <m> mana -> <c> in the stone, worth <w> pyreals at 1.8 a point, against a payout of <p>: drain|sell`.

Round 12 left 38 mana stones under the floors (22 Moderate, 12 Mana Stone, 3 Lesser, 1 Minor). The loot rule now keeps a stone, empty or charged, whatever the floors say, while the kit holds fewer than `ItemManaKeeper.StoneTarget` (4: two charged and two to capture with). Such a stone gets the verdict `KitStone` (the decision line says ", for the kit's mana stones") and goes to the kit pack. The excess goes by the value rules, and a stone of the target is never offered to Archmage Cindrue, whose mask buys them.

The activation requirements are read in ACE's order (WorldObject_Use.cs 191-324): Arcane Lore, the item's skill limit (the armour loot names Melee or Missile Defense, LootGenerationFactory_Magic.cs 177-203), UseRequiresSkill, the specialised limits, the level, the attribute and vital limits, then the heritage. Each refusal names retail's line: 0x028B 0x04C9 "Your X is too low to use that item's magic.", 0x04CB, 0x04C6, or the transient "You are not high enough level to use that!". A wield refusal is 0x00A0 SkillTooLow 0x0468 or LevelTooLow 0x0420 (Player_Inventory.cs 1655-1661 and 2126-2229), for which retail prints no line (`WeenieErrorText.RetailShows`).

**Trade notes and coin that stack (D136 point 3, D133; `Scenarios/Journey/ResupplyStation.cs`, `Fighter/StackMerge.cs`; `ResupplyStationTests.Notes.cs`).** Every trade note weenie stacks to 250 (wcids 2621-2627 and 20628-20630, MaxStackSize PropertyInt 11 = 250, StackSize 1, ACE-World-Database v0.9.296) and the coin (273) to 25,000. ACE never joins a new stack to a held one. A buy makes one new stack of up to MaxStackSize a row (`Vendor.cs` 392-424 `ItemProfileToWorldObjects`) and adds it with `TryCreateInInventoryWithNetworking` (`Player_Commerce.cs` 59-102, `Player_Inventory.cs` 90-118, `Container.cs` 499-575, no merge). A sale's payout comes as new coin stacks (`Player_Commerce.cs` 194, 211-218, 302ff `CreatePayoutCoinStacks`). Joining stacks is the player's own GameAction 0x0054 (retail `CM_Inventory::Event_StackableMerge`, 11.6096 0x006ACDD0; ACE `HandleActionStackableMerge`, `Player_Inventory.cs` 2849ff), the `MergeStack` verb the corpse looter already sends for looted coin. Round 12's six single notes were, by this, separate buys (one note a trip), each its own object. After the coin-to-notes buy, the trip now merges the notes into the main pack's stack with the purchase merge, `StackMerge.TryPlanFor(..., mainPackTarget: true)`: only a stack in the main pack itself is a target (D121), so a stack ACE put in a side pack comes home. It logs `resupply: merging a bought Trade Note (250,000) stack 0x<new> into 0x<held>: x<n>` and then `purse: Trade Note (250,000) held in 1 stack(s): 0x<held> x<total> (main pack)`. The coin's stacks are merged the same way after that buy and after the loot sale (`resupply: merging a held Pyreal stack ...`). One buy may take as many notes as the coin pays, up to 250 for each free main-pack slot (`ItemsToReceive.cs` 78-110 asks one slot a stack). A row whose 0062 names no MaxStackSize counts one per slot, as before. Changing a note when the coin is short: ACE sells the whole object it is handed (`Player_Commerce.cs` 199-205 and 232-298; `Vendor.cs` 586-609 pays the stack's whole Value). So a note from a stack of several is first split off into the main pack with GameAction 0x0055 (`SplitToContainer`; ACE `HandleActionStackableSplitToContainer`, `Player_Inventory.cs` 2243ff), logged `purse: split one <note> 0x<one> from its stack 0x<stack> (x<n>) to change it`. That one note is sold; with no free slot it is refused as `pack`. D99's sale reads the main pack and never offers a note, so it is unchanged. `TODO(m5-note-merge)` is closed.

**The purse's follow-up (soak round 13; `Scenarios/Journey/PurseNotes.cs`, `Fighter/StackMerge.cs`).** Two faults in round 13's trip (19:59-20:01 UTC). The trip bought no note and gave no reason: it held 150,021 against the 40,000 floor and wanted a whole 287,500. The coin merge ping-ponged 36 times: the old plan took a full 25,000 stack as the source into a partial one and back.

Now every trip converts the coin above the floor, greedily from the largest note, into the notes of the purse's `min_note` and up (`PurseNotes.Greedy`). For the den `min_note` is 25,000, one coin stack, and it is also the default. A smaller note saves no pack slot and costs 15%, so the 10,000 and smaller stay coin. ACE has no 25,000 note, so the den buys the 250,000, 200,000, 150,000, 100,000 and 50,000. Round 13's 150,021 now buys one 50,000 and keeps 92,521 in coin: four coin stacks and at most five note stacks. The vendor of the purse's largest note is asked for all ten notes, and those under `min_note` are left out. Archmage Cindrue (wcid 2304) lists them all: her CreateList, ACE-World-Database v0.9.296 `weenie_properties_create_list` rows 21060-21069, destination 4. Thelnoth (715) lists only the 100 and the 500 (rows 12597-12598), and Monyra (716) only the 100 to the 1,000 (rows 65467-65469). Each note is priced as ACE does, `max(1, ceil(1.15 x Value - 0.1))` (`Vendor.cs` 577-585): 287,500 down to 115. At the vendor her 0062 decides: a note she does not list is skipped and logged. The coin left is under the smallest offered note's price (57,500 for the den). Each denomination is one buy, merged into its stack before the next.

Every trip logs the decision. For a buy: `purse: coin <c>, floor <f>, above <a>, notes of 25000 and up (a smaller note saves no pack slot and costs 15%): buy <n> x <note> at <price>, ...; <left> stays coin (under 57500, the Trade Note (50,000)'s price)`. Otherwise `... no notes: <why>` (no vendor sells a purse note; no note is of `min_note` or more; the coin above the floor is under the smallest such note's price; the main pack has no free slot). After the buys come one `purse: bought ...` line for each denomination and `purse: done at <vendor>: the coin <c>, <a> above the floor <f>`.

The coin merge (`StackMerge.TryPlanFor`) takes only partial stacks, smallest into the largest other one. A full stack is never a source or a target (`TryPlan` refuses a full source too). Every merge empties its source or fills its target, so the merges end with at most one partial stack. Round 13's three cases, read back from the log, take 2, 1 and 2 merges where the old plan took 12 each (36 in the trip). Tests: `ResupplyStationTests.Notes.cs`. The scripted vendor that lists a trade note lists all ten (`ScriptedShop.Shop.AddTradeNotes`), so the den's forced trip now walks to Cindrue a second time, for the notes.

Nothing in this section was run live or in a loopback: the rehearsal, the soak and the item-end checks are the lead's.

**M6 item 0: the outdoor fight and the death.** The fight's toolbox reads the outdoor fight (section 62). The death handler's trip look-out reads the outdoor ground's band (`FightTargets.Wcids`); a death on an outdoor ground walks its corpse trip (`route=walk`), and a kit-less character rearms from the corpse (`rearm=corpse`), closing `m6-death-outdoor-corpse-walk` and `m6-death-outdoor-kit` (section 63).

## 57. The ladder as data (M6 item 0 a1; D17, D26; DoD 1)

**The ladder and its loader (`Session/Grounds/Ladder.cs`, `LadderLoader.cs`, `ladder/`).** A ladder is one JSON file under `src/Lifestone.Client/Session/Grounds/ladder/`; the csproj embeds every file there (logical name `Lifestone.Client.Session.Grounds.ladder.<file>`). `LadderLoader.Get(key)` reads one once (`LadderLoader.WarMage` is `war-mage`); an unknown key throws `KeyNotFoundException`. A missing, unknown, duplicated or out-of-range field throws `LadderException` naming the file and the field's JSON path, as `GroundCatalog` does for the profiles (section 52).

**A ladder** has a key (the file name), a name, a `top_level` (126 for the war mage, D3), a `sources` object (ladder, top_level, bands, move_on_rule, spell_level, pending, plan_cast_chance) and its rungs in climbing order. The ladder carries `plan_cast_chance` at its top level (0.95, a source value; D4, D41; M6 item 1). The bands run without a gap or an overlap from level 1 to `top_level`. `Ladder.RungFor(level)` returns the rung whose band holds the level and throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` outside 1 to `top_level`.

**A rung** is `kind` ground or quest. It has a band (`from` and `to`, both inclusive: the spec's "10-15" is the band 10-14 with the move-on level 15); a ground key for a ground rung, or quest keys (`academy`, `pathwarden`) for a quest rung, resolved against `QuestCatalog` (section 58); the spec's landblock (or null); alternates (each a ground key, its landblock and its own pending flag); the move-on rule (`level`, `kills_an_hour_floor`, `casts_a_kill_ceiling`; the floor and the ceiling are null only on a quest rung); the war spell level (`min` and `max`, computed by the fizzle rule on the projected base War Magic and pinned by `SpellPlanTests`, section 66; M6 item 1); the element (a damage type, null only on a quest rung); the route key; `pending` with `pending_reason`; and a `sources` object (band, ground, alternates, move_on, spell_level, element, route).

**Pending grounds.** A ground rung or alternate whose profile is not written is `pending: true` with a `pending_reason` of the form "profile due in item N" (optionally "; " and more). The loader fails a non-pending ground that does not resolve through `GroundCatalog.TryGet` (new in a1), a pending ground that does resolve (a stale pending: its flag is cleared when the profile lands), and a non-pending ground whose profile does not hold the named landblock.

**Route keys** are `<kind>:<place>`, the kind one of `start` (where the character is created), `walk` (a walk from the town), `town-network` (one Town Network hop, then a walk) and `water-run` (a surface run with water from the town). Item 4 resolves them (`Ladder.RouteKinds`).

**The move-on rule's values** are plan data owned by the leveling optimizer seat (m6-plan.md section 2.1, `TODO(m6-ladder-move-on)`). Today's floor is half the strategy's modelled kills an hour, rounded down; the ceiling is twice the modelled casts a kill (the band's seconds a kill times 3.4/19.6, M5's measured den kill), rounded to 0.1. What the `level up` job does when a rung falls under the floor or over the ceiling is section 61's.

**The war mage's rungs today** (the island road, D17): 1-4 the Academy and the Pathwarden chest (quest); 5-9 the outskirts rung (a1 first wrote it as `low-b-belt`, the stand-in; section 64's `holtburg-outskirts` replaces it, `TODO(m6-outskirts-profile)` for the Redoubt pass); 10-14 Burrow; 15-21 Lodge; 22-31 Cave (alternate Cavern); 32-44 Temple 20-40; 45-59 Abode (alternate Habitat); 60-74 Quarters (alternates the Temple 40+, which resolves, and Barracks); 75-126 Holding (alternates the Temple 40+ and the den, which resolve, and the Quarters). Every tusker rung is pending on item 3.

**Tests.** `LadderTests` (load, order, contiguity, `RungFor` at every edge and outside, the pending rule both ways, missing and unknown fields by path, the vocabularies) and `HuntingGroundDatTests` over every ground the ladder resolves (the catalog's dungeons and the two named outdoor keys; `LadderTests` asserts the coverage).

## 58. The quest loader (M6 item 0 a2; D26; DoD 7)

**Quest files.** A quest is a file (M6 DoD 7, D26): `Session/Quests/quests/*.json`, embedded by `Lifestone.Client.csproj` and read once by `QuestCatalog` (`All`, `Get(key)`), as strictly as `GroundCatalog`. A missing, unknown or duplicated field, a wrong type, a key that is not the file's name, or a step without its kind's fields fails at load with `QuestFileException`, naming the file and the JSON path.

**`Quest`** is immutable. It holds the key, the name, the giver (or null), the start place, the ordered `QuestStep`s, the done condition (`QuestDone`: a server stamp, a reply or an item; at least one of them), the repeat timer in seconds (null: done once per character) and the sources. `Todos` lists the named TODOs of the sources and the steps.

**The step vocabulary** is `QuestStepKind`. Item 0 implements `go`, `talk`, `use`, `give` and `pick-up`. Item 5 implements `kill`, `hunt-until`, `buy`, `recall`, `confirm` and `wear` (six kinds, each run by the quest station, section 80). `combine` and `apply` still fail at load with "not yet (item 8)" and their `TODO(m6-quest-step-<word>)`. A key on a chest (the ladder note's use-key) is a `use` step with an item.

**The field rules per kind.** `go` needs a place or a target. `talk` needs the NPC and a check. `use` needs the object and a check (a reply, a stamp, an item or an arrival place). `give` needs the NPC, the item and a check. `pick-up` needs the item (its arrival is the check) and may name its container. A null wcid, or a missing check, is allowed only with the step's named `todo`.

**The field rules, item 5 (M6 5 Q1).** `kill` needs the creature (target), `count`, `ground` and `expect.reply`, the kill counter's complete text (`Your task is complete!`); it carries no item and no place. `hunt-until` needs the item, `count` and `ground`, and may name the carrier as its target; no place. `buy` needs the vendor (target), the item and `count`; no place, since a `go` step reaches the vendor. `recall` needs `spell` and the arrival place; no target, no item. `confirm` needs `expect.reply` (a substring of the question's text) and `answer` (`yes` or `no`); no target, item or place. `wear` needs the item; no target, no place.

**The new step fields (M6 5 Q1, F1).** Item 5 adds four optional step fields: `count` (a whole number above 0; kill, hunt-until and buy), `ground` (a ground profile key that `GroundCatalog` knows; kill and hunt-until), `spell` (a spell id above 0; recall) and `answer` (`"yes"` or `"no"`; confirm). Each is refused, by its JSON path, on a kind that does not use it, and a present field must hold a value (leave it out instead of null). An expected item (`expect.item`, `done.item`) means the item arrives: its count in the pack rises over the step, never that it is held (a climber may already hold a gem). The talk step takes two optional fields (F1): `armed_reply`, a task in progress that is accepted as a kill task's arm, and `wait_reply`, the reply on its 20-hour wait, on which the station stops with `talk:on-timer`; both are refused on any other kind. The two kill-task files carry them (San Ming's sets 51756 and 51754; Shoichi's in-progress broadcast and his wait Tell).

**The hunt-until's carriers (M6 14 want loot).** A hunt-until may name `carriers`, each `{"wcid", "shade", "row"}`: a creature of the creature table whose create list can hold the hunted item, the row's shade (its chance a kill: ACE's `CreateListSelect`, `WorldObjects/Creature_Equipment.cs:636-679` @95ef426d, rolls each set of Treasure rows once from `Creature_Death.GenerateTreasure`, `Creature_Death.cs:688-708`) and the `weenie_properties_create_list` row's id; and `kill_rate`, `{"wcid", "kills", "minutes", "source"}`, a carrier's kills measured live. The station passes the carriers to the fight (`carriers=<creature>:<item>:<shade>:<item name>`), which walks to a carrier's corpse beyond the loot radius or with no line, whatever its distance on the ground, under the aggro and walk rules, and walks back to one lost from view with no distance cap; any other corpse keeps the radius. The start line gives the grind as data (the items an hour at the live rate if every corpse is looted, and the hours left), and the fight logs `hunt-until: N of M` after each corpse looted. Both fields are refused on any other kind. TODO(m6-create-list-general-read): the client carries no create lists, so the fact is the quest file's.

**The quest's level and experience (M6 5 Q1).** A quest may name `level` `{min, max}` (min at least 1; max at least min, or null for no top) and `experience` `{amount, kind, max, percent, source}`. A `fixed` award has its amount above 0 and no max or percent (ACE AwardXP and AwardNoShareXP). A `proportional` award has its share above 0 (1.33 is 133 percent of the next level's experience), a cap (max above 0, or null) and a floor (amount, or null): ACE's AwardLevelProportionalXP, `GrantLevelProportionalXp` @95ef426d `WorldObjects/Player_Xp.cs:441-454`. `QuestExperience.At(nextLevelXp)` applies that rule (rounded, capped, then floored), without the server's xp modifiers. Both fields are null when absent; items 6 and 9 read them for the menu and the round.

**The reads (M6 5 Q1, `QuestReads`).** `QuestReads` is pure: it reads only the `ChatLog` and a mark (`ChatLog.Total` before the act) and logs nothing. `Since(chat, mark)` gives the lines added after the mark that the log still keeps. `Replied` and `Said` are the Academy's reply read and its `; said:` fragment, lifted unchanged. `ParseReward` and `Reward` read the system line `You've earned N experience.` (ACE `Player_Xp.cs:114`; N with thousands separators, any one separator between groups of three digits), summed since the mark. `ParseKillCounter` and `KillCounters` read `You have killed N <plural>!` with ` Your task is complete!` or ` You must kill M to complete your task.` (ACE `QuestManager.cs:619-626`), optionally for one plural. `ParseGive` and `Give` read, for a named NPC, `You give <npc> <item>.` (taken), `You allow <npc> to examine your <item>.` (a Refuse emote), and the WeenieErrorWithString refusals that carry the NPC's name: 0x046A doesn't want, 0x04CE busy in an emote, 0x03EF not accepting, 0x058A cowers (ACE `Player_Inventory.cs:3400-3475`). The reward, counter and give-success lines are read only from system chat, never from an NPC's tell.

**The headless Yes/No (M6 5 Q1, `QuestConfirmRule`).** `QuestConfirmRule.Decide(open, step)` decides for each open server question (`GameState.PendingConfirmations`), oldest first. Types 1 (swear allegiance) and 4 (fellowship) are never answered, even when a step names their text: they are left open and logged. A question whose text contains the active confirm step's `expect.reply` (case-sensitive) gets the step's answer. Any other question of a type ACE keeps open until the client answers (2, 3, 5, 6, 7; `GameState.ServerKeepsSlotAfterDone`) gets No. Any other type is left open. Each decision is one line, `confirm: type= text= decision=yes|no|leave why=`. This is the rule half of `TODO(m5-6-headless-confirm-reply)`, closed in item 5: the quest station's confirm step (section 80) and the autopilot's tick (section 83) wire it.

**The station kind (M6 5 Q1).** `StationKinds.Quest` (`quest`) takes `JourneyPlans.QuestArgument` (`quest=<key>`) and `JourneyPlans.FromArgument` (`from=home|ground`, default home); the station kinds number 27. The autopilot's tusk errand lists it (section 83).

**The first two files.** `academy`: the Calling Stone to the greeter 30991, the three leather pieces 13239-13241, the armour-room guard 29322, the Training Master 29320, the Academy Token 12709 looted from a Sparring Golem and given to him, the Central Courtyard portal 31061, the hive's Protection Orb to the Holtburg Sentry 30994, and the exit 29338 to Holtburg. It is done on the exit's congratulations message, since the exit erases the Academy's stamps; section 60 gives the file's 23 steps as they now stand. `pathwarden`: Thorolf 33596, the Pathwarden Token 33613 for the Supply Key 33608, the key on the chest 33609, the robe 40439, the gauntlets 33606, the sollerets 33605 and the trinket 41513. It is done on PathwardenComplete and the trinket (section 59).

**What the client sees of the stamps.** Nothing directly: this server has `quest_info_enabled` false (`/myquests` is off), and the protocol carries no stamp. The runner judges by the NPC's reply, the item arriving and the experience line. On the loopback server the tools' `@lifestone quest has <name>` reads the registry row (held, completions), changes nothing, and gives no time. A verb that reads a stamp's time is proposed, not built (`TODO(m6-quest-stamp-time)`; it is server work, `@lifestone quest when <name> #<id>` replying the registry's completion count and last completion time). With it, `QuestTimers.Observe` can take the server's own completion time instead of the time seen.

**`QuestTimers`** keeps each character's timers by quest key. `Complete(quest, at, how)` records a completion from the done reply (`done-reply`) or the done item (`done-item`), with the next due time `timer_seconds` later (never for a quest done once). `Observe(quest, hasAnswer, seenAt)` records a held done stamp the timers lack (`server-stamp`, timed when seen, so the next due time is never early). `IsDue`, `NextDue` and `Line` (the `quest key=... state=never|due|waiting|done-once` line) read them.

**Persistence (M6 5 Q2; the run folder of review 5-R11).** The timers live in `quests/<checkpoint file name>` (`QuestTimers.FileName`), beside the autopilot's checkpoint folder: the headless host puts the folder in the parent of the checkpoint folder, the Godot host at `user://quests/<file>` (`JourneyLegRunner.BuildParts`, shared by the Godot journeys and the autopilot's legs), through a store (`IAutopilotCheckpointStore`: `UserDataCheckpointStore` or `AutopilotFileCheckpointStore`). `JourneyScenario.NewContext` loads it once into `JourneyContext.Quests` (`QuestStore` beside it; copied by `WithDungeon`). The timers file follows the host's run folder (5-R11): a gate's fresh folder starts with no timers, and the server still gates the tusk's pickup, so a refused pickup stops the step by name (section 81). A file that does not parse, or cannot be read, stops the run with `TODO(m6-quest-timers-unreadable)` naming the file and the JSON path, and is never overwritten. A station records a completion with `JourneyContext.CompleteQuest`: `Complete`, `Save` through the store, then the `quest key=... state=...` line (with `saved=yes|no`). A failed write logs `TODO(m6-quest-timers-save-failed)` and throws (the entry stays in memory). A host with no store (the plain headless `--scenario=journey`, the loopbacks) logs `TODO(m6-quest-timers-no-store)` once per run and keeps the timers in memory for that run.

**Whose records they are (M6 8, the long round's fifth start).** The file is named for the character's name, and a character deleted and created again keeps its name (the climber at each gate, M4 D44). So the file carries the character's guid (`character_guid`, schema 2; `QuestTimers.CharacterGuid`), as the autopilot's checkpoint does. Once the run knows who is in the world it binds the timers (`JourneyContext.BindQuestTimers`, called from `AutopilotScenario.Begin` before any quest rule reads them and from the journey's known state; `QuestTimers.BindTo`): records under another guid are another character's and are dropped, each named in a `quest timers: check before: the file's records are another character's ...` warning, and the file is saved without them; `quest timers: check after: bound to <character> 0x<guid>, <n> record(s)` follows. A schema 1 file names no guid: its records are kept as this character's and logged `TODO(m6-quest-timers-unowned)`. The cause was live: a fresh climber read the last climber's finished errand as `done-once` and never ran it. The menu's read-only load before a run (`AutopilotHost.TimersNow`) does not bind (`TODO(m6-menu-timers-guid)`).

**Tests (M6 5 Q1, Q2, F1).** `QuestProfileTests`: the quest files load; the steps come in order; a missing and an unknown field each fail naming the file and the path; combine and apply fail loud; each item-5 kind loads with its fields and fails by path without each one, or with a field it does not use; the new step fields refuse a bad value and refuse themselves on the other kinds; the level and the experience load, compute ACE's proportional award and are read strictly; the timers' round trip and next due time. `QuestReadsTests`: ACE's exact strings (thousands separators, a plural with spaces, the complete and the not-complete counter, the give lines and the four refusals, an NPC name with a comma); a line before the mark is ignored; a tell is never read as the server's line. `QuestConfirmRuleTests`: the five kept types get No; types 1 and 4 are left even for a step; other types are left; the step's own question gets its answer; the line format. `QuestTimersStoreTests` (Q2): the store's round trip.

## 59. The fresh climber Winnie and the Pathwarden (M6 item 0 a3, f1; D5, D7, D25, D34; DoD 2)

**The creation template** (`MageTemplate.ClimberCreationIntent`). The traditional mage's attributes (Strength, Endurance and Quickness 10; Coordination, Focus and Self 100) with the credits spent from the Aluvian heritage's 52 skill credits (`CharGenData`, `ACCharGenData::GetSkillTrainedCost` and `GetSkillSpecializedCost`, 11.4186 0x005C26D0). War Magic is specialised (28) and Life Magic specialised (20): 48 of the 52, 4 left. Alchemy is not in the template (D34, which amends D6: the Atlan wand's one Alchemy check is a named grant in item 8). Melee Defense is never bought (D5). The unpaid lines, Creature Enchantment (8), Mana Conversion (6) and Item Enchantment (8), are named by `TODO(m6-climber-creation-credits)` and left to item 1's credit plan.

**The fresh character** (`--scenario=climber-create --fresh-character`; the default account is `test` only). `ClimberCreateScenario` is the M4 D44/D45 re-create for Winnie (D7). It is refused without the flag, with `--character` or `--create-character`, and on any other account. The live Winnie is never entered: the retail delete runs, the list shows her pending, the new Winnie is created at level 1, and `MageTemplate.ClimberCheck` checks the template. Only then does the server mod's character purge remove the old copies until it answers unknown-character. Nothing is granted and nobody is placed; the character stays in the Academy. The verdict is `[climber] verdict fresh=recreated|created purged=<n> granted=<n> template=ok|short level=<n>`, where `granted` is the `ModVerbCounter` tally since the session began.

**The purge rule.** The server mod's `CharPurgeRules.Graduated` and `Recreated` (and the stand-in's copies) name Winnie, so the D45 rule applies to her. The installed mod needs `server\setup-server.ps1 -ModOnly` before the first live `climber-create`; that run is the lead's, under the pre-authorisation for leads (M4 D8). `TestAccounts` lists Winnie on `test`.

**The Pathwarden as a journey station.** `--scenario=journey --journey=climber` (Winnie on `test`, one station of kind `pathwarden`, `PathwardenStation`) reads `quests/pathwarden.json`. Its go and use steps carry the cell 0xA9B40022 and the points of Thorolf (97, 27, 94) and of the chest (99, 29.5, 94). The station goes to Thorolf, talks to him (the stamp PathwardenFound1111), gives the token, receives the key, uses the key on the chest, opens it, picks up the robe, gauntlets, sollerets and trinket, and wears them. Every step is check, act, check, with one named recovery (`recovery=talk-again|give-again|unlock-again|wear-again`). The completion goes through `JourneyContext.CompleteQuest` (`PathwardenRun.Timers` is the context's `QuestTimersInUse`): it is recorded, saved through the host's store and logged (M6 5 Q2; `QuestTimersStoreTests`). The chest's reach is `PathwardenRun.UseRange` (1.5 m), proved by item 0's round 9 (the give, the key, the chest opened, 3 of 4 pieces worn), so the reach and the open check carry no TODO now. The file has no talk step (the station's talk branch runs only when a quest file has one), so the talk's reply has no open check (`m6-pathwarden-talk-reply` closed with no test to write). The return pass's unnamed tolerances are `ReturnWalkSlack` (1 m), `ReturnGiveSlack` (3 m) and `ReturnNpcMatchRadius` (40 m) in `ResupplyStation.cs`, their values unchanged (review 2-R9). A station problem is a WARN line `PROBLEM step=...: what; item=... wcid=... container=... location=... server said: ...`, and the live test prints every log line of each phase under a header.

**The wear rule (F1).** ACE refuses a clothing piece while a worn piece's `ClothingPriority` overlaps it (`Creature_Equipment.cs:50-58` and `:93-101` @95ef426d). The pinned world SQL gives the Robe 40439 the priority 0x17F00 (outerwear, head and feet), the Gauntlets 33606 0x8000, the Sollerets 33605 0x10000 (feet), and the Trinket 41513 none (ValidLocations 0x04000000). A new character wears starter shoes (`PlayerFactory.cs:109-130` @95ef426d). So the live round's worn=2/4 is explained by the starter shoes blocking the robe and the sollerets. The station takes off a starter piece in the way (Unwield, then check), wears the robe, gauntlets and trinket, and leaves the sollerets in the pack while the robe covers the feet: the verdict's `blocked=1`, a WARN line, and `TODO(m6-pathwarden-robe-covers-feet)` (the lead or the owner decides robe or sollerets; the robe carries five spells and armour level 50 over the whole body, the sollerets 120 over the feet). `pathwarden_done=yes` needs the stamp, the trinket worn and every piece worn or blocked by name; `trinket_worn` reads the trinket alone. Not established offline: that the starter shoes were the one blocker live; the next round's PROBLEM lines show each piece's coverage, location and the server's reply.

**The bridge and the lane.** Before the Academy station (section 60) existed, `--scenario=academy-exit --character=Winnie` walked her out of the Academy. `AcademyExitScenario` is now a fixture for the other characters' baselines. The live lane is `-GameArgs:'--scenario=climber-create --fresh-character'`, then `--scenario=academy-exit --character=Winnie`, then `--scenario=journey --journey=climber`. The pre-journey recovery place to Holtburg (`JourneyScenario.cs:284-306`) is replaced for the climber by section 60's cheat-free known state.

**M6 item 0, after the review: the climber is never granted or placed (F5).** The player tools' one send path refuses every item, experience, place, spell-learn and corpses-rot request while the character in the world is Winnie (`MageTemplate.ClimberName`). The outcome is Refused, its text starts `TODO(m6-climber-no-grant)`, one WARNING goes to the session log, and nothing is sent or counted. `quest has`, `status`, `where` and the character purge are not refused. The named opt-in is `--allow-climber-grant` (the Session group, default off; `SessionOptions.AllowClimberGrant`, `GameSession.AllowClimberGrant`, `ActionApi.AllowClimberGrant`), kept for item 8's one Alchemy grant (D34). The refusal closes in item 0; the grant itself stays item 8's.

## 60. The Academy by play (M6 item 0 a3b; DoD 2)

**The Academy is a station.** `AcademyExitScenario` stays what it was: a test fixture for the other characters' baselines (a `place` to the exit's wing, the quest stamped by the mod, the way home by place). It is no longer used for Winnie. The climber plays the Academy as a station, `AcademyStation` (`Session/Scenarios/Journey/AcademyStation.cs`), which reads `quests/academy.json` by step kind through `AcademyPlan.Of`. A `go` walks to its place's point for its target; a `talk` uses the NPC and checks its reply; a `give` gives and checks the reply and the stamp (`quest has`, asked once a second for up to 8 s); a `pick-up` with no target is a floor pick-up (worn after it when it has wield locations, by F1's `PathwardenWear.Plan`); a `pick-up` whose target is a creature is a kill with war spells and the loot of its corpse; a `use` inside the Academy is a portal, checked by a teleport away from it; a `use` whose place is outside the Academy's landblock is the exit, checked by the arrival there and its reply.

**The steps.** The file has 23 steps, from the lead's SELECTs (`cache/m6/0/sel-academy-8602.tsv`, `sel-academy.tsv`, `sel-sentry-master.tsv`): the Calling Stone to the Society Greeter 30991; Jonathan's room (0x860201B0) for the Leather Gauntlets 13240; the armour room (0x860201B6) for the Leather Leggings 13241 and the Leather Cap 13239; Samuel 29322 (0x860201B1), talk ("You may now proceed to the Training Area."); the Training Master 29320 (0x8602023A), talk; the Sparring Golem 12698 on its 10-second generator beside him, killed, its Academy Token 12709 looted and given to the Training Master (AwardXP 1,000, `AcademyTokenGiven`); the Central Courtyard portal 31061 (0x86020273), used; the Sentry 30994 (0x860202C2), talk ("You must infiltrate the hive"); the Adolescent Olthoi 29331 (0x86020100), killed, its Protection Orb 29336 looted and given back to the Sentry (his Tell, a level-proportional award, `SentryTaskComplete`); the Exit to Holtburg 29338 (0x86020169), used (Holtburg 0xA9B40019, the congratulations message).

**The fight is a single-target kill**, over the Action API's targeted cast, not the ground fight: the Academy is two named creatures in two named rooms, not a hunting ground, and the token and the orb are looted by weenie class, which the fight's value picker does not promise. Each cast is check, act, check: the target alive and within 15 m (else a walk to it), the mana for the spell (else a rest of up to 90 s), the targeted cast, its outcome, and the target's death within 2 s. A fizzle is cast again, a busy answer waits a second, and a components refusal stops the station by name. The war spell is the spellbook's War Magic projectile of the highest level with the least mana; the pack's caster is wielded first at the held slot (one recovery unwields it first) and the mode is set to magic. Any attacker (GameEvent 0x01B2 and 0x01B4, `CombatEvent`) is fought first, before the next step and inside a kill (M5 D88). The corpse ("Corpse of <name>", within 10 m of where the creature died) is walked to, opened and the item picked up. One recovery: another kill when the corpse lacks the item, another pick-up when the item did not arrive.

**Instancing.** The Academy is instanced: the same layout sits in several landblocks with the same cell low words. The station takes the landblock it starts in and moves each of the file's Academy cells there by its low word (`AcademyPlan.Rebase`); a cell of another landblock, such as the exit's arrival, is kept.

**Measured on the dats** (`AcademyStationTests`): the start's rooms reach Jonathan's room, the armour room, Samuel, the Training Master's room and the Central Courtyard portal's cell by doorways (4, 4, 2, 16 and 20 doorways); the start does not reach the Sentry's room. The Sentry's room (0x860202C2 with the Portal Linkspot 0x860202C3) shares no doorway with the hive's rooms (0x86020100, 0x86020104) nor with the exit's wing (0x86020169, 0x86020148, 0x86020134). The way between them leaves the rooms (the courtyard is outdoors), which the journey runner's indoor-outdoor planner walks and the room planner cannot show (`TODO(m6-academy-hive-layout)`, read on the first live run). The walks inside the Academy go through that planner over its landblock, and the runner's door crossings open the doors. The Training Area door 29329 (0x860201B2) may be locked until Samuel's talk; a failed walk there names the door. If the runner has no nav map for landblock 0x8602's outdoor part, the go step to the hive or the exit fails by name (`travel:run:...`).

**Closed and open names.** Closed here: `m6-academy-token-kill`, `m6-academy-spawns`, `m6-academy-npc-names`, `m6-academy-leather-wcids`, `m6-academy-xp`, `m6-academy-hive-orb` and `m6-academy-sentry-reply`. Open: `m6-academy-courtyard-arrival` (the portal has no destination row; the station logs where it lands); `m6-academy-sentry-percent` (the Sentry's award has only the amount 5,000); `m6-academy-sentry-gift` (the item 49563); `m6-academy-skip`; `m6-academy-hive-layout`; and the loud stops `m6-academy-no-caster` and `m6-academy-war-spell`, not expected. The Sentry's stamp follows his Tells and a GotoSet, so a longer chain shows as a PROBLEM line with the reply seen.

**Experience.** The dat table gives level 2 at 1,000, level 3 at 2,777, level 4 at 5,697 and level 5 at 10,248. The Training Master's 1,000 makes level 2. ACE's level-proportional award is the level's span times the percent, held to the minimum and the maximum: a whole span at level 2 (1,777) lands on 2,777, level 3, and the 5,000 award lands on level 4. So the Academy's fixed awards reach level 3 (4 at most) on this server, with the kills' experience on top (not in the SELECT). DoD 2's "level 5" is not reached by the Academy (`TODO(m6-academy-sentry-percent)`), and the Pathwarden's emotes award none here. The live test reports the level from the character's own property and grants nothing.

**The cheat-free climber.** `JourneyPlans.Climber` is the Academy station, then the Pathwarden station, with `CheatFree = true` (`JourneyPlan.CheatFree`). A cheat-free journey sends no place of any kind. The mod verbs are marked at the journey's start, not after the known state. The known state is where the first station starts (`IKnownStart.Unplayable`: the Academy's start cell, by its low word 0x01AD, in any Academy instance) or, with no such station, the plan's ground. Anywhere else the journey stops by name: `stop=known-state-unplayable:<where>` (`cell-0x...`, `no-position`, or `<ground>:cell-0x...`). The recovery after a failed station never places either (`stop=known-state-unplayable:recover:cell-0x...`). After the done line a cheat-free journey writes `journey climber cheat_free=yes level=<n> granted=<n> place=<n> recovery_place=<n> stop=<name|none>`; the counts are the mod-verb counter's since the journey's start (`ModVerbCounts`). The climber is judged `granted=0 place=0 recovery_place=0`, and the level is the character's own property. `AcademyChestLiveTests` (the lead runs it) does the create, then the climber journey (the Academy by play, then the Pathwarden), prints every log line per phase, and reports `academy_done=yes pathwarden_done=yes trinket_worn=yes granted=0 place=0 recovery_place=0` with `level=<n>`.

**M6 item 0, after the review: the full route and the tutorial's skip (F6, F7, D37).** `quests/academy.json` now has 33 steps. After the Central Courtyard portal it runs: a Thieving Thrungus (0x86020225) killed for its Bellows; the Bellows given to the Academy Blacksmith 30996 for the Academy Library Key 30999 (the key checked in the pack); the key used on the library door 30998 (`AcademyAct.Unlock`, a use with an item, checked by the door's Locked property, one named recovery `unlock-again`); the Senior Guard talked to at 0x8602032C; and the Outer Courtyard portal 29334 used. The library door is locked and ACE opens a locked door only from behind (Door.cs:91-117 @95ef426d), so the walker's two Uses fail and the step fails by name. The full route still cannot finish on this server: the Sentry's rooms and the hive's deepest rooms join the rest of the Academy only by floor portals and steep ramps that the room graph refuses (`TODO(m6-academy-sentry-ramp)`, `TODO(m6-academy-hive-ramp)`, item 4's seam), and its fixed awards reach level 3 or 4 (section 60). So the climber takes the tutorial's own skip (D37): `quests/academy-skip.json`, four steps (the Society Greeter's Calling Stone 30991, Jonathan 29324 talked to for the skip, his Exit Token 29335 given back for the server's teleport to Holtburg). The skip is done on the reply plus the arrival in landblock 0xA9B4, and its verdict reads `academy_done=yes route=skip steps=4/4`. The level is read from the character's own property; the award (level-proportional, up to 11,000) is reported, never assumed. The skip's three leather pickups were dropped in live round 8: the walk to the Leather Cap was refused by the route confirmer's ground probe at the player's own raised floor (z 0.73 in 0x860201B6), `TODO(m6-probe-start-surface)`, item 4's. The full route's code and file stay for item 4.

**M6 item 0, after the review: reach by use, touch portals and the shut door (F4, F4b, F6).** An object within `UseReachMetres` (5.0 m: the use range of 1.5 m plus 3.5 m, Lifestone's own constant, not a rung's) is used where the character stands, and ACE's move-to walks the rest (Player_Use.cs:184-206 and Player_Move.cs:37-96 @95ef426d); beyond it the journey's runner walks.
