Each choice is logged as `reach=use` or `reach=walk`. A walk the wayfinder refuses gets one named recovery: the character steps back to the last point the wayfinder confirmed, at least 1.0 m away (`recovery=step-away`), and plans the same walk again; refused again, the step fails by name. A corpse's loot is checked by its contents, with one `recovery=open-again`. The Central Courtyard portal (31061) takes the player on touch, not on Use: a walk to a portal the next step uses counts as taken only when the client saw an accepted teleport since the walk began (`TouchTeleported`), and a walk that ends short with no teleport fails by name. A walk that lands in another landblock checks the landing before any recovery (22fb6638). A door still shut after two Uses is a closed door for the rest of the walk and fails by name without a replan (`TODO(door-locked-replan)` stays item 8's). `TODO(m6-academy-ground-probe)` (item 4): round 4's standing spot near the Training Master, where the probe found no ground, may recur; the reach rule is the fix for that case.

**M6 item 0, after the review: the m6-climber gate area (F5, D36).** `AcademyChestLiveTests`, DoD 2's check, has its own gate area `m6-climber` in `tools\lib\GateAreas.psd1`. It is selected by changes under `Session/Quests/` and to the Academy, Pathwarden and climber-create files, and `-Loopback m6-climber` runs it. It left the `actions` area, so a `Session/Actions` change no longer selects the ten-minute Academy run. A change under `Session/Scenarios/` still selects every class, the fail-safe as before.

**The shared runner (M6 5 Q3, D56).** The Academy's step runners (talk, give, the floor pick-up, the kill and its loot, the fight-back, the caster and the mode, peace, the walk to an object and its step-away recovery, the stamp check, wear) live in the shared `QuestStepLeg` (`Session/Scenarios/Journey/QuestStepLeg.cs`), which `AcademyRun` and the quest station's `QuestRun` both extend. The Academy keeps its go, its portals, its exit and its rebase (`Cell`, virtual). Every log line and recovery name is unchanged (diffed); `AcademyChestLiveTests` runs again in the gate's m6-climber lane.

## 61. The level up job and the [ladder] line (M6 item 0 a4; D27)

**The job.** `--autopilot-job=level-up` (default `den`, M5's job unchanged) runs the autopilot as the level up job's first form. The ground is the war mage's ladder rung for the character's own level (PropertyInt 25), read at each cycle's start in the known state, after the start-up audit and before the place is classified (`AutopilotScenario.DecideRung`, `AutopilotScenario.Ladder.cs`). The start rule is D7 and D25: the den job plays BSD Mage only, and the level up job plays Winnie only (`AutopilotHostLogic.RequiredCharacter`, `StartRefusal`). The option's help is in `OptionCatalog.Autopilot.cs`.

**The cycle's start** is check, act, check (M5 D141). "ladder: check before" names the level, the rung held and the run's ground. The decision acts. "ladder: check after" names the rung, its band, the move-on level and how many levels are left. The stops are these: a quest rung stops with `stop=rung-quest:<rung>`; a rung whose profile is not written with `stop=rung-pending:<rung>`; a rung whose ground the fight refuses with `stop=rung-unfightable:<rung>` (the rule is the fight's own `FightOptions.GroundError`, so the stop goes away once the fight walks outdoor grounds, section 62); a level past the top with `stop=ladder-top` (ok); an unread level with `stop=failed:rung-level-unknown`. These stops cast no recall first, since nothing was fought.

**The move-on** (`m6-ladder-move-on`). A level that has reached the rung's move-on level (its top plus 1) belongs to the next rung. A next rung on another ground stops the run with `stop=rung-moved:<rung>` (ok), and the host builds the next run on `AutopilotScenario.LadderGroundFor(level)`. The next run's first check, the after-check, stops with `stop=failed:rung-ground-mismatch:<rung>` if its ground is not the rung's. The kills-an-hour floor and the casts-a-kill ceiling are only logged (D27); their values stay `TODO(m6-ladder-move-on)`. The host's restart on the new rung is section 63's.

**Each cycle logs** the bolt: the rung's element's line at the cap of section 66's rule (D41) on the current War Magic, never under the rung's plan, with `plan= live= skill= chance= plan_chance= cap=`. A line the ladder cannot name, or one the fight does not cast, is a loud stop (`stop=failed:rung-bolt-line:<rung>`, `stop=failed:rung-element-line:<rung>`; M6 item 1). It logs the target band (the ground's band with its top lowered to the character's level + 5, `AutopilotScenario.TargetLevelMargin`, with its reason) and the creatures it skips. It logs once each every buff line of which the spellbook holds no level, and `TODO(m6-ladder-buff-profile)` when the character has no buff profile (section 63 gives Winnie's).

**The `[ladder]` line** (report-only, D27) is written once per cycle (`at=cycle`) and once after the done line (`at=done`, the run's totals): `at n level rung ground kills xp_per_h deaths scrolls_bought spent_xp quests_done granted walk_s s move_on_level kills_per_h kills_per_h_floor under_floor casts_a_kill casts_a_kill_ceiling over_ceiling`. `granted` is the session's verb-counter tally, as on the cycle line. `scrolls_bought` and `quests_done` read 0 until item 1 and the quest runner. `casts_a_kill` reads n/a until the fight line carries `casts=` (section 62 adds it). `walk_s` (`m6-walk-cancel-seconds`) is measured from the state: the position one second apart, and a pace of 0.5 to 20 m/s counts the second, so a cancelled leg counts as every other pace does. Section 62 closes that name in the walkers.

**M6 item 0, after the review: the climb driver and the rung's margin (F5).** `tools\climb.ps1` drives the climb from level 1 as three steps. Step 1 creates Winnie (`--scenario=climber-create --account=test --fresh-character`); step 2 runs the climber journey (`--scenario=journey --journey=climber --account=test`); step 3 runs the level up job on the play host to `-TargetLevel` (10) for `-Minutes` (60), with the display held through `tools\lib\GateHost.psm1` and no setting changed. Step 3 is refused unless step 1 read `granted=0` with `template=ok` and step 2 read `cheat_free=yes granted=0 place=0 recovery_place=0`; a count a log does not give is a refusal, never a zero. The script reads each step's log, the headless console's `climber: verdict` line included, and ends with one report-only line (D27): `[climb] verdict level_start= level_end= rung= kills= deaths= granted= place= recovery_place= minutes=`. `granted` sums the three steps, `place` is step 2's plus step 3's `places=`, and `recovery_place` covers steps 1 and 2 only. `-SkipCreate` skips steps 1 and 2 and appends `skipped=create,journey`; `-PlanOnly` prints the commands and starts nothing (the backend stays the lead's: the script reads its state and never starts or stops it). Its pure parts are `tools\lib\Climb.psm1`, tested by `ClimbScriptTests`. Each rung of `ladder/war-mage.json` carries `target_margin`: the outskirts 5, a quest rung and a pending ground rung null. The loader requires it on a ground rung that is not pending, refuses it on a quest rung, and takes 0 to 50. The level up job reads it, logs it in the `ladder: targets:` line and passes it to the fight as the station argument `target-margin` (`FightOptions.TargetMargin`), which replaces `FightTargets.LevelMargin`. A rung with no margin logs `TODO(m6-rung-target-margin)`, and a fight given none logs `TODO(m6-fight-no-target-margin)` once. The `[ladder]` line's `quests_done` counts the quest keys the job knows to be done, by the rule of `reason=quests-done`.

## 62. The outdoor fight (M6 item 0 a5; D33, D47, D88)

**The ground.** `FightOptions.GroundError` lets through a dungeon (as before) or an outdoor ground with `outdoor.cells` (`FightTargets.IsOutdoorFight`). An outdoor ground without cells is still refused, by name. A dungeon fight is unchanged.

**The walk.** `OutdoorFightWalk` (`Session/Scenarios/OutdoorFightWalk.cs`) takes its legs from `OutdoorTour` (`Session/Grounds/OutdoorTour.cs`): the profile's `outdoor.cells` in the file's order, round and round, the player's own cell left out. Its purpose is `Order` (D47: the next cell, to look for targets there). Each leg is a point goal at the cell's `spot` at the terrain height (`HuntGround.SeekHeight`) plus 0.5 m, through the travel seam with `TravelPurpose.Cell`, the request the hunt's next cell makes (a journey's seam runs it on foot; the default seam places). A spot with no height (water, steep, or unread) is skipped by name. With no height anywhere, the walk fails with `TODO(m6-outdoor-height)`.

**Check, act, check (M5 D141).** `outdoor walk: check before leg n` names where the player stands and the goal. The arrival check needs the player on one of the ground's landblocks: a place's Arrived only confirms the place, so the leg waits for the landblock, as the hunt's place does. A failed leg, an arrival off the ground, or a leg over the profile's `walk.leg_s` is abandoned, and the walk goes on to the next cell (`m5-fight-walk-recover`; three in a row fail the walk). There is no physics yet: no line test (`TODO(m6-outdoor-line)`) and no walk to a spot (the loot's walk back keeps `TODO(m5-loot-walk-back-walk)`).

**The targets** (`FightTargets.Of`). A dungeon's profile `targets` are its targets. An outdoor ground with none listed hunts its `outdoor.creatures` within its `level_band`, once per wcid, on the outdoor cells (low word under 0x100) of its landblocks that are not no-go. HostileWatch and the autopilot's vitals guard read the same list, so outdoors they see the ground's creatures.

**The band follows the character.** On an outdoor ground the pick skips a creature above the character's level + 5 (`FightTargets.LevelMargin`, the rule section 61 names as `AutopilotScenario.TargetLevelMargin`). The fight logs the band once per level ("targets: the band follows the character") and each creature skipped in range ("skipped above the band"). An attacker is fought back whatever its level (D88: the self-defence names it from the notices, not from the band). An unread level logs `TODO(m6-outdoor-band-level)` once, and the pick takes the ground's band.

**The bolt cap.** The den fight's spec argument `max-level` (`JourneyPlans.MaxLevelArgument`) sets `FightOptions.MaxLevel` unless the command line gave `--fight-max-level`, so it reaches `FightScenario.PlanCap`. The belt has no plan row, so the argument is the cap. The level up job passes the cycle's `BoltLevel` through it (`AutopilotScenario.LadderFightSpec`, logged as `ladder: the fight's bolt cap: level n`). The element: every rung of the outdoor road is fire, whose line is the fight's own Flame Bolt line. Another element keeps `TODO(m6-ladder-element-line)`, logged once, and the fight casts Flame Bolt.

**The verdict and the kill lines.** The fight's verdict carries `casts= walk_s=` after `openers=`: the casts sent, and the walk's walking seconds (`n/a` for a walk that does not count them). Every kill notice logs `kill n: casts=k (<notice text>)`, the casts counted since the previous kill when the notice arrives; a killing cast whose answer comes after the notice counts on the next kill. The `[ladder]` line's `casts_a_kill` reads these fight lines' `casts=` over their `kills=`, and reads n/a until one carries it.

**Walk seconds.** Every ground walk counts its walking seconds frame by frame (`LegPacing.TotalWalkSeconds`). A leg cancelled before its arrival (`Abandon`, when the fight finds a target) counts as an arrived leg does, and logs `leg n to 0x.. cancelled after walk_s=x (counted in the walk's total y s: m6-walk-cancel-seconds)`. This closes `m6-walk-cancel-seconds` in the walkers (`RunnerLegs`, `OutdoorFightWalk`); the game's `GameFightWalk` exposes `WalkSecondsTotal` for the fight's verdict (F2).

## 63. Winnie's wiring and the way home (M6 item 0 a6, f2, f3; D33)

**The play host.** The play host plays the level up job on the climber plan (`AutopilotHostLogic.PlanFor`): Winnie's checkpoint file (`winnie.json`), the start rule through `StartRefusal`, and the run's ground taken at each fresh start (the first press, or `/auto` from Off or Done) from the ladder's rung for the level (`LevelUpGround`). A level with no run refuses by the ladder's name, and an unattended start exits 1.

**The move-on restart.** On `stop=rung-moved:<rung>` (ok) the dial restarts once by itself on the next rung. Check: the stop and the cycle are logged. Act: the host reads the new level and rung and rebuilds the parts over the new ground, sharing the spell table; if the parts are ready the dial starts at once, otherwise the host presses it when they are read. Check: the next run's first cycle must be on the rung's ground, else `failed:rung-ground-mismatch`. A refusal or a missing hook stops with `failed:rung-restart-refused` (exit 1 when unattended). The lines are `ladder: move-on restart: check before`, then `act` or `REFUSED`.

**The kit-factory seam (M6 item 16 E0b, D139).** The steps of a rung move are client code, one copy for every host: `Session/Autopilot/AutopilotRungKits.cs` holds the first press (`PrepareRung`: the level, the start's ground, the kit over it), `UseRung` (the plan by `PlanFor`, the dial's stock counters, the kit unless it stands over the same ground) and the dial's move-on hook (`MoveOnNext`: go, wait or refused by name), with their log lines word for word, and the carry of a start, a hand-back and a restart (`AutopilotRungKits.Scenario`: the options left, the seed, the hand-over, the totals, the cold-read checkpoint store). Which ground a rung is stays `RungOwner`'s (section 106). A host implements `IAutopilotKitFactory`: `Ready`, `Prepare(ground, plan)`, `PressWhenReady(startedBy, reason)` and `Create(carry)`. The play host's half (`AutopilotHost.RungKitSeam`) keeps what needs the game: the worker loads with the shared spell table, the kit over the game's nodes with the player's own body as the walker, the press that waits for the loads, the files, and the unattended exit on a refused press. The headless half (`Session/Hosting/HeadlessAutopilotKits.cs`) reads nothing on workers, so its kit is ready when asked for and a restart starts in the frame of the stop; `HeadlessClimbScenario` is the dial over it, started once as an unattended run (`started by --scenario=autopilot`), and `HeadlessAutopilotScenario` uses it for `--scenario=autopilot --autopilot-job=level-up` with the journey's own parts built for each run over its rung's ground (the plan is then the job's, the ladder's character). Proved offline by `HeadlessClimbTests` over the scripted world (a level-up in the fight, `rung-moved`, the next scenario travels and fights on the next ground; a kit read on workers waits and is pressed); the headless level up run has never met a server (`TODO(engine-headless-climb-live)`), and the menu's judgement of a quest task is not wired there (`TODO(engine-headless-menu-input)`).

**The buff profile.** Winnie's buff profile (`BuffProfiles.Climber`) is the arena profile's lines, every line learned by play. The cycle casts only the levels her spellbook holds and logs each missing line once, by name. `BuffCycle.PickMana` and the dance levels (`FillDanceLevels`) cast a mana line learned by play (Stamina to Mana Self, Revitalize Self) only at the levels the spellbook holds; a read book with no level of the line logs `<line>: no level is in the spellbook` once per line. That closes `m6-ladder-mana-line-book` (F2). BSD Mage's lines are build-taught and unchanged.

**The gear scenario.** `GearScenario.WrongCharacter` (the journey's grant rule and the cast-facts station's check) accepts BSD Mage and Winnie. `WrongBuildCharacter` (the gear scenario's `RequireCharacter`) stays BSD Mage's alone.

**The way home from an outdoor ground.** Without Lifestone Recall in a read spellbook, the way home from an outdoor ground the profile says is hunted on foot (no portal, cells listed) is a walk to the home's lifestone point through the travel seam: a Bind point goal, its purpose logged and its arrival checked (`recall-home: arrival-off-point`). The verdict adds `home=walk walk_s=`. Any other case is `recall-home: no way home: ... (TODO(m6-first-tie-walk))`. The trip's way home (`JourneyTravel.Start`, the Home case; closes `m6-trip-way-home`, F2) does the same with the journey's ground known: a read book without the recall on an outdoor ground walks to the home's lifestone point as a Bind point goal through the host's runner. It is checked before (`journey travel: home on foot: check before`), skipped when already within 5 m of the point, and checked after (the player must stand in the point's landblock within 5 m, else `travel:home:arrival-off-point`). A dungeon, an unread book or a journey with no ground is as before: the recall is tried, and its failure names `travel:recall:spell`, with a WARN line that carries the rule's reason. BSD Mage is unchanged. Since M6 item 4 t3b, a read book without Lifestone Recall standing in a routed place (the island, a hub, a stop town, a routed ground) goes home by `rung-change` direction=home, by portals (section 76).

**The way back.** `LogisticsStation`'s way back to an outdoor ground is a walk to `outdoor.cells[0]`'s standing point (terrain height from the dats; `TravelPurpose.Cell`; checked before, acted, and checked after within 5 m, else `logistics:way-back:arrival-off-point`). It is skipped when already within 5 m. An outdoor ground whose profile gives no walk, or with no dats, is a loud stop: `logistics:way-back:no-walk`, `no-dats` or `no-height`. BSD Mage's den return (Primary Portal Recall) is unchanged. This closes `m6-trip-way-back` (F3). `JourneyTravel` makes a Ground travel for the climber a walk (point goal, `travel:ground:arrival-off-point` on a miss) on an outdoor ground hunted on foot, and otherwise the loud stop `travel:ground:climber-no-place`. `JourneyScenario.RecoverFallback` never places the climber: her failed way home is `recover:climber-no-place`, with `recovery_place=0`. Other characters are as before.

**The death on an outdoor ground** (F2, F3). `GearKit.BuildFor(spells, account, ground)` returns `GearKit.Bare`, with no lines, for an outdoor ground whose profile lists no vendor kit (`GearKit.HasNoKit`); a dungeon with no kit still fails `ground-plan-gap`. The death, fight and buff stations use it. The outskirts station threw `ground-plan-gap` too, not only the death. A death over a bare kit drops its gear stage, logged. On an outdoor ground hunted on foot, the death handler's corpse trip is `route=walk` (`DeathRoute.Walk`): no recall, and `BeginCorpseLeg` starts the corpse walk (an object goal, `TravelPurpose.Corpse`) from the lifestone. The respawn is Holtburg's lifestone (`ClassifyRespawn`). The rearm for a kit-less character with no caster wielded or held is `rearm=corpse` (`DeathRearm.Corpse`, report-only): no buy and no failure. The rebuff and the heals are skipped until the items are back, the wear step's `WornRestorer` wields the best caster held and wears the remembered set, and the item lines are re-cast after (`relines`). The items-back check reads the worn set as the take-back found it (`DeathHandler.WornSet`) against the state: `gear=wielded|missing worn=<n>`, and `GearBack` is false when a remembered piece is not worn again (WARN names the guid). The death station's walk (`DeathGroundWalk`) is `OutdoorFightWalk` for an outdoor ground, and the trip's look-out reads `FightTargets.Wcids(ground)`. This closes `m6-death-outdoor-corpse-walk` (F2) and `m6-death-outdoor-kit` (F3).

**The foci audit** (F2). `StartupAudit.ReadKit` audits, for a ground with no worn kit, the foci a character's casts assume (`StartupAudit.AssumedFoci`: Winnie's War and Life foci, 15271 and 15270, from the starter pack). `KitReading.FociMissing` names them, and the autopilot's kit audit stops by name, `m6-foci-missing` (`kit: the foci the casts assume are not in the pack`). Planning with the account's full spell formula is not done (`TODO(m6-account-formula-plan)`: `SpellFormulaRules.CustomizeForAccount` at `GearKit.cs:470`, `ComponentFloor.cs:68` and `:106`, `LevelFloor.cs:58`, `FightScenario.WarPick.cs:145`, `GearScenario.cs:1143`). The profile's lines hold both formulas for account `test` (section 64), so the stop is the cautious reading; the lead may relax it to a warning.

**Tools and places.** `-Steps login-check` (or `login`) prints `[slicecheck] steps SKIP backend step <name>`, since slice-check never starts the backend. Place paths the climber's chain could reach were audited in F3: `LogisticsStation.cs`, `JourneyTravel.cs` (the Ground case's place stage) and `JourneyScenario.RecoverFallback` are fixed. The default seams place only when no travel is given, and the journey's stations always pass the context's `JourneyTravel`.

**M6 item 0, after the review: the stations on the run's ground, the vitals guard and the bare kit (F8 and the lead's fixes).** The journey's stations read the run's ground: `JourneyStations.Create(plan, arguments, dats, kitAccount, ground)` sets `FightOptions.Ground` to the ground the level up job's parts are built over (`JourneyLegRunner.BuildParts` passes it). Before, a command line without `--fight-ground` meant the Black Spawn Den, so the buff station's gear stage judged the den's arena kit, and the death, fight and gear stations' fight options read the den's profile. The known-state vitals guard stands down while the hands hold no caster and a pack does (`PackHoldsCaster`, logged once: the state goes on and its caster step wields one first). Before, the guard asked for the magic mode every second, the client refused it by name, and the 90-second known-state watchdog sent the run home before the start-up audit could wield the caster; no bound was scaled, since the login settle took 5 s. An outdoor ground with no vendor kit has the bare kit (`GearKit.Bare`): its gear verdict reads `gear=bare` rather than failed, the buff leg's judge accepts it, and a gear stage over a bare kit judges nothing short, since there is nothing listed to wield or wear there. The buff cycle given no profile takes the climber's own (`BuffProfiles.For`, every line learned by play), so a line she cannot cast is not in it. A line learned by play is wanted only while its school's skill is trained, logged once by name (a Creature Enchantment line failed the cycle while that school was untrained). A fresh climber trains Creature and Item Enchantment from the levels' credits (item 1's plan, `TODO(m6-climber-creation-credits)`).

## 64. The outskirts profile (M6 item 0 belt; D33, D17)

**Why not the belt.** `low-b-belt` (generators 1999 and 2001) sits 4.3 to 8 map units out (1 to 2 km), with band 8-20 and creatures to level 30. The pinned `encounter` table has nearer generators: 2007 "Newbie Aluvian Generator" (355 cells within 5 units, nearest 0.85), 1996 "Low A Aluvian Generator" (218 cells, nearest 2.69, levels 2-15) and 5150 "Harmless Aluvian Generator" (bunnies and chicks, levels 2 and 4). Generator 2007 is the spec's "drudges, mites L8".

**The profile** `profiles/holtburg-outskirts.json` is of kind outdoor. Its creatures from generator 2007 are Drudge Skulker 0.25, Drudge Slinker 0.25, Young Banderling 0.15, Mite Snippet 0.10, Mite Scion 0.10, Young Mosswart 0.05 and Creeper Mosswart 0.05 (all level 8), and Gnawer Shrethlet 0.05 (level 2). Its children have a delay of 300 s, init 1 and max 1.

**The cells.** The cells are the ten nearest 2007 cells whose terrain reads dry (the `HuntingGroundDatTests` rule); eight of the twenty nearest are water, in the lake north of the town. They are 0xA8B50034, 0xA9B30035, 0xAAB30017, 0xA9B30034, 0xAAB30016, 0xA8B30027, 0xA8B3002D, 0xAAB3000B, 0xAAB30036 and 0xA8B3000C, 0.85 to 1.42 map units out (about 200 to 340 m), in landblocks 0xA8B3, 0xA8B5, 0xA9B3 and 0xAAB3. The first cell is north of the lake and the other nine are south of the town; nearest first is the belt's rule, kept.

**Band and damage.** The band is 5-8: the floor is the rung's first level and the ceiling the highest child level. `AutopilotScenario.TargetBand` gives 5-8 for levels 5 and 9. The expected yield per spot is 0.95. Fire damage taken (PropertyFloat 67) is 1.42 for the drudges, 1.0 for the rest and 0.8 for the Gnawer, a mean of 1.22 over the band, so fire is confirmed for the rung.

**Home and the spell plan.** Home is the Holtburg lifestone 0xA9B40019, the den's. The `spell_plan` has one row: levels 1-9, Flame Bolt, spell level 2 (the rung's cap, which section 62's bolt cap reads once the outdoor fight reads the plan: `ChooseLevel` picks the highest level held under the row). Low-b-belt, `HuntGround.LowB`, `BeltKey` and the M4 hunters' tests are untouched. The rung's profile is `holtburg-outskirts`; the belt stays the M4 hunters'. `TODO(m6-outskirts-profile)` stays open for the Redoubt, item 3's pass.

**The formula finding** (`TODO(m6-outskirts-account-formula)`). ACE's spell formula depends on the account name: `SpellTable.GetSpellFormula(table, id, session.Account)` rewrites the taper slots 1, 3 and 6 (RandomizeVersion1) by a hash of the account. For account `test` (read from the dats by the new dat test): Flame Bolt I (27) is Lead Scarab, Hawthorn, Powdered Onyx, Turpeth and Birch Talisman; Flame Bolt II (81) is Iron Scarab, Grey Taper, Hawthorn, Powdered Onyx, Turpeth and Birch Talisman; Armor Self I (24) is Lead, Wormwood, Onyx, Cobalt and Cedar Talisman; Heal Self I (6) is Lead, Hyssop, Powdered Amber, Colcothar and Willow Talisman.

**The foci.** A fresh War Magic character is created with the foci. `starterGear.json` gives each trained magic school a Training Wand, its Foci (War: Foci of Strife 15271; Life: Foci of Verdancy 15270), 5 Lead Scarabs and 25 Prismatic Tapers (`PlayerFactory.cs` 225-300 @95ef426d; stacks merge, so Winnie holds 10 and 50). `Player.HasFoci(school)` (`Player_Spells.cs` 458-488) is true for any foci in the inventory, and then ACE casts the foci formula (a Lead or Iron Scarab with 1 or 2 Prismatic Tapers). So a mage without foci exists only when the foci is lost, by a death or a sale. The profile's lines hold both formulas, so either casts. The audit that stops on missing foci is section 63's.

**Burn.** `Spell.TryBurnComponents` (`Spell.cs` 157-189) burns per slot per cast: ComponentLoss times CDM times min(1, Power/skill). Flame Bolt I has ComponentLoss 0, Flame Bolt II 0.05, Armor Self I 0 and Heal Self I 0.01. Herbs, powders, potions, coloured tapers and the Prismatic Taper have CDM 1; scarabs and talismans 0.1. The worst case is 90 kills an hour at 4.9 casts a kill, 441 casts an hour of Flame Bolt II: 22 of each heavy component an hour (2.2 scarabs or talismans, or 44 Prismatic Tapers on the foci formula).

**Stock lines** (keep, trip under, stop under). Grey Taper, Hawthorn, Powdered Onyx and Turpeth 40, 10, 2; Iron Scarab and Birch Talisman 10, 3, 2; Lead Scarab 20, 5, 2; Wormwood, Cobalt, Cedar Talisman, Hyssop, Powdered Amber, Colcothar and Willow Talisman 6, 3, 2; Prismatic Taper 60, 15, 3; Mana Potion 5, 2, 0. Archmage Cindrue (2304) sells every one except the potion, which Thelnoth (715) sells: her list holds all the herbs (14), powders and potions (7), talismans (7), the 12 coloured tapers (34), the Lead (14), Iron (68), Copper (135) and Silver (338) scarabs, and the Prismatic Taper (30). Renald (718) stays the weapon and armour buyer and sells none of these.

**Purse.** The starter gear gives 10,000 pyreals (the Jump skill's gear in `starterGear.json`). One full restock at the keeps is 6,838 pyreals; the first, after the pack's 10 Lead Scarabs and 50 Tapers, is 5,198. Scrolls for the next spells (Flame Bolt II onward) are not sold in Holtburg: Cindrue sells none, and Thelnoth sells only Other-spell scrolls (Heal Other I, Revitalize Other I and the Other buffs). The full-formula lines are for account `test` (`TODO(m6-outskirts-account-formula)`).

**The starter pack.** A War Magic specialist with Life Magic and Alchemy trained: Training Wand 12748, Foci of Strife 15271, Foci of Verdancy 15270, 10 Lead Scarabs, 50 Prismatic Tapers, 10,000 pyreals, a Sack, a Calling Stone, a Pathwarden Token, Bread, Ust, a Mortar and Pestle and 3 Azurite. Spells: Flame, Force, Frost Bolt I, Shock Wave I, Acid Stream I, Lightning Bolt I and Whirling Blade I (War, specialised); Armor Other and Self I, Heal Other and Self I, and Imperil Other I (Life, trained; Drain Health Other I and Harm Other I are specialised-only). The book has no Stamina to Mana Self or Revitalize Self (the den's mana lines): those are learned by play (section 63).

**M6 item 0, after the review: the burden (F8 and the lead's fixes).** Capacity is `EncumbranceSystem.EncumbranceCapacity`: 150 times Strength, plus 30 times Strength for each carrying augmentation up to 150 (none for the climber). Winnie is created at Strength 10, so her capacity is 1,500 and the outskirts' 90% line is 1,350. The first climb probe read 129% after one restock, with the pack about 872 before it. The starter items sum to 1,250 by the SQL burdens, 378 more than the probe implies, so one of them weighs less than the SQL says (`TODO(m6-starter-burden)`: read `EncumbranceVal` per item live). The Pathwarden station sheds the clothing its pieces replace: every piece the wear plan took off, and every clothing piece in the pack whose coverage overlaps a quest piece now worn, is dropped (GameAction 0x001B) and checked gone, since ACE refuses overlapping clothing (Creature_Equipment.cs:50-58 and 93-101 @95ef426d). The chest's carry gate (`quests/pathwarden.json`, its `carry`: `line_percent` 90 and `reserve_burden` 120) takes the pieces lightest first, only when the burden plus the piece plus the restock's 120 fits the line. The robe and the trinket are the quest's named reward (`always`): taken over the line, with the burden logged. The sollerets (540) and the gauntlets (900) stay in the chest, counted left off by name, and are taken from Strength 14 and Strength 20 respectively. A chest piece whose burden is not read is left, loudly (`TODO(m6-pathwarden-piece-burden)`). So Strength, not the armour, is the binding limit: each rank is 150 of capacity (`TODO(m6-climber-strength)`, item 1's credit plan). The outskirts profile's `burden_trip_percent` is 150, not the section default of 90: the climber's runs loot nothing, so a trip cannot shed burden and a 90% line would call a trip every cycle. At 150% her run is half speed (ACE's burden mod), and the trip is called there, with the run stopped by name if it cannot help. The loader accepts up to 200, ACE's own ceiling. No rule drops what is carried over the line; `TripLoopGuard` is the only stop for a loop.

## 65. Dressed by rule (M6 item 2; DoD 4, D26, D38)

**GearScore** (slice a: `GearScore.cs`, `SelfEquip.cs`, `KeepAsideRule.cs`) scores a candidate or a worn piece for one slot. `GearScore.Of` takes the item and a `GearContext` (the skills, the rung's element, the ground's damage types, the useful cantrips, the spell names, the carried burden, the run's TODO latch) and returns the slot, the total, the named parts, any unmet requirement, and the attuned and bonded flags. Its log line is `gear score: <slot> '<name>' 0x<guid> <total> = <part> <value> (<note>), ...`, ending `; 0: <unmet>`, `; attuned` or `; bonded` when they apply.

**Casters.** A caster scores its war bonus on the rung's element (`WorldObject_Weapon.cs` 382-400), and 0 when a wield requirement is unmet. A tie goes to the mana conversion (only a caster on the rung's element may win one), then to the useful cantrips (`GearScore.CasterBeats`, the M5 7 S2c order). The parts are never summed: a percentage of damage and a percentage of mana conversion are not one coin. A caster out of mana counts no cantrip; its hours of mana are shown, from `ItemCurMana` over the absolute `ManaRate` (Float 5) over 3,600.

**Armour.** Each covered body part (nine parts, `BodyPart.GetCoverageMask`, `Entity/BodyPart.cs` 115-140) scores (AL plus the piece's Impenetrability) times its protection, the protection clamped to [-2, 2] (`Creature_BodyPart.cs` 66-100, `ArmorProfile.cs` 33-58). The ground's damage types are averaged in, but the grounds do not yet carry them, so the score rests on the averaged protections (`TODO(m6-ground-damage-types)`, the armour stub until item 3's ground fields). A body-armour cantrip adds its value to all nine parts unscaled (`GetBodyArmorMod`). A piece's share of the free capacity comes off its total, and a piece that fills the free capacity scores 0. With the Strength unread the burden is not weighed, and the log says so. A piece with neither its armour profile nor the `ArmorModVs` floats scores protection 1 and names the gap (`TODO(m6-armour-profile-unread)`).

**Jewellery** scores its useful cantrips, none when out of mana. The armour cantrips' stat rows that the buff table lacked are a small table in `GearScore.cs`, read from the pinned world SQL's `spell` table: Minor to Legendary Impenetrability (2604, 2592, 4667, 6095) and Armor (2578, 2571, 4911, 6102), values 20, 40, 60 and 80. These are spell facts, not ground facts.

**Replace.** A piece with no useful cantrip replaces the one worn piece in its coverage when it scores `ReplaceMargin` (1.10) higher. The two server actions run with the parts bare between them. `Replace` is not `IsUpgrade`, so the loot's keep-aside is unchanged. A worn piece casting a useful cantrip, and an unappraised worn piece, are never replaced.

**Element and wield types.** `SelfEquipJudge.ElementOf` takes the rung's element first, then the plan's family, then 0 with `TODO(m5-self-equip-element)`. Wield requirement types 3 to 6 are read (`m5-self-equip-wield-type`: 3 and 4 from the attribute, 5 and 6 from the vital maximum; ACE `Player_Inventory.cs` 2147-2178 @95ef426d). Types 9 and up stay loud under the same name, for M7.

**The caster's mana** (slice c: `CasterManaRule.cs`, `ItemManaKeeper.cs`). A caster's spells drop when its mana reaches 0: `Player_Tick.cs` 681-699 removes the item spells and calls `OnSpellsDeactivated`. A mana stone only adds mana (`ManaStone.cs` 119-190 never activates the spells), and the wield re-creates them (`Player_Inventory.cs` 313-315 and 324-366, `OnSpellsActivated` in `WorldObject_Magic.cs` 2191-2196). So a recharge is followed by a re-wield, and the mage half of `m4-gear-mana-reactivate` is closed here. The fighters' line stays M4's (`GearRecharge.cs` 307).

- The "spells dropped" flag is set by the `Your <name> is out of Mana.` chat line in `WornManaWatch.cs` and cleared at each confirmed caster wield of the resupply (`CasterSpellsDropped.Shared`).
- `CasterManaInput` gives `ItemManaKeeper.Next` the held caster, the flag, the pack's spares and every vendor ware as an offer. `KeepItemMana` acts on `step.Caster`: `SwapToSpare` (the spare wielded, checked; a failed wield re-wields the old one, then `RearmHands`), `Rewield`, or `WantStone` (the charge as a floor line). Its line is `caster mana: ...`.
- The Atlan wand's 500 mana drains in about 5.5 h (ManaRate -500 over 5.5 x 3,600 s). That is the spec's figure until item 8 reads the wand's own rows.
- Archmage Cindrue (2304) sells no Mana Stone 2435, Moderate 27330, Greater 2436 or Major 27328. She sells the Minor Mana Stone 27331 (Value 250) and the Lesser 2434 (Value 500), both empty, and the Mana Charges 4612 to 4615 (Values 350, 650, 1,500 and 2,500; ItemCurMana 100, 175, 350 and 500). A stone she sells must be charged, so a want is always a charge. At her 1.35 a High Mana Charge costs 3,375 pyreals; the drain is about 4.4 charges a day, about 14,900 pyreals.
- `m5-stone-field-refill` is M7's. `WornManaWatch` runs in the level-up job (`AutopilotScenario.cs` 408), but the long run's trips came about every 46 minutes against the 5.5 h drain, so the refill on a home trip is enough.

**The gear floor** (slice b: `GearFloor.cs`, `ResupplyStation.Gear.cs`). `GearFloor.Plan` is pure. Below the floor level it buys nothing. The floor level is the rung of level 1's `move_on.level` (the academy-and-chest rung, 5), read from `LadderLoader.WarMage`, with no constant (D26). Two casters are wanted (`CastersWanted`, the owner's rule, not a ground fact). Missing casters come first, each at the cheapest caster a profile vendor sells, then one robe covering the chest when none is worn (the cheapest one), then the charge a `WantStone` asks for. A ware is a caster or a robe by `GearKit.FloorWeenieOf` (the SupplyWeenies table, pinned SQL).

- A missing caster that cannot be bought (no profile vendor sells one, or the purse is short) stops the trip `no-caster` (`m5-no-caster`), with the reason. A robe or charge that cannot be bought is a named note (`TODO(m6-no-robe-vendor)`, `TODO(m6-no-stone-vendor)`), not a stop.
- The floor runs only on loot trips (`Gear` is `--fight-loot`). Its buys go first in the buy list and never enter `supplies.kit`, so `GearKit.HasNoKit(outskirts)` stays true and a kit-less death keeps `rearm=corpse` or `none`. A bought spare is `rearm=pack`.
- Each buy is checked before (open vendor, profile price, coin, held count), acted on, and checked after (held count and spent rose): `gear floor: bought ...: check after: held 0 -> 1, paid 270`. A refusal reads `gear floor: refused: ...`. With no caster held and none buyable the trip ends `gear floor: no-caster: ...`.

**The equip pass** runs after the buys and before the pack sort. It appraises, swaps in a better caster (the other becomes the spare), and judges every held non-caster: `Wear` (check, wield, check) or `Replace` (check the worn piece and a free main-pack slot, take it off, check, wield at its location, check; a refused wield puts the old piece back, checked). The floor's robe is worn in its free slot, since a plain robe scores no armour gain. Its line is `equip pass: worn=<n> replaced=<n> casters=<held> refused=<n> (<names>)`.

**The sale filter** (slice d: `ResupplyStation.cs`) keeps a piece from the sell list when ACE would refuse it or the floor keeps it: a worn piece; a Value-0 piece (`Player_Commerce.cs` 275-280); an attuned piece (PropertyInt 114 above 0, which ACE refuses to drop, `Player_Inventory.cs` 1389-1393 and 866-871, and `Vendor.cs` 626-627 stops the resale); a retained piece (PropertyBool 91 or the Retained description bit, `Player_Commerce.cs` 268); and a caster the floor keeps. The floor keeps two casters held (wielded, main pack and side packs), and the rest of the main pack's casters are kept best first by `GearScore.Caster`, an unappraised one always. One line a trip says what was kept: `sale: kept <n> (<count> <reason>, ...): not offered`. `m4-vendor-issellable-wire` stays M7: the wire is still unread, and the filter drops only the classes known to be refused.

**The returns to Thorolf** (slice d: `GearReturn.cs`, `pathwarden.json`). The quest file's optional `returns` block (giver, rows, reward, emote, source) is read by `GearReturnTable`; `QuestCatalog` lets the key through, one line. Its six rows are Thorolf's (33596) Give emotes 53553 to 53558, read from the pinned SQL's emote and action rows: the Helm 33607 goes back for a Salvage 33620 ("a bag of high quality Granite"), the Gauntlets 33606 and the Sollerets 33605 for a Salvage 33621 (Steel), and the Robe 40439, the Plate Leggings 33601 and the Plate Hauberk 33597 for a Sturdy Iron Key 6876. The Trinket 41513 has no such row and is kept.

- The robe is kept while it is the only chest cover. A piece is returned when a worn piece in its slot scores higher (outgrown) or a worn piece is in its way (blocked, `Creature_Equipment.cs` 50-58 and 93-105). ACE refuses to drop an attuned piece, so the return is the only way out for it. A caster is never returned here.
- The trip checks the plan and Thorolf's place, gives the piece (`Give(npc, piece, 1)`), and checks that the piece is gone and the reward's stack rose. A failure keeps the piece by name, with no retry. Lines: `return: <name> ... goes back to <npc>` and `return pass: given=<n> kept=<n>`. There is no live Give proof yet.

**The notes on the outskirts** (slice d: `holtburg-outskirts.json`). The purse is coin 2,700 with a minimum note of 10,000, and one Trade Note (10,000, wcid 2625, count 1: the loader's minimum, `TODO(m6-purse-note-count)`). The floor is 2,700 because a restock from nothing at the keeps costs 2,270, plus the Wand's 270 and the Faran Robe's 68, rounded up to the hundred. Notes are carried from level 6, since a death takes half the coin and no notes (`Player_Death.cs` 347-360 and 629-663; ladder note section 11.1). A note costs 15% of its face. A 10,000 minimum leaves at most the floor plus the smallest note's price (14,200) exposed, so a death takes at most 7,100. The creation stack of 10,000 is 7,300 over the floor and under the 11,500 a note costs, so it stays coin and pays no premium in levels 1 to 5, where a death takes nothing. The default minimum of 25,000 would leave up to 30,000 exposed. `ResupplyStationTests.Notes` proves it: 40,000 coin buys three notes at 11,500, and 10,000 coin buys none, with the reason logged.

**The outskirts rows** (slices b and d: `holtburg-outskirts.json`). The ladder note and the corpus said Holtburg sells no caster. The pinned world SQL (v0.9.296, create list row 21071) says Archmage Cindrue (2304) sells the Wand 2472 at 270: Value 200 at her 1.35. Ecutha the Tailor (719) sells the Faran Robe with Hood 5851 at 68 (Value 50 at her 1.35), with her buy mask 0x40004 (clothing and notes), the den profile's row verbatim. The outskirts have no `loot` section, so the `MageLootRules` defaults stand, with no measured floor per burden (`TODO(m6-outskirts-loot)`).

**The climber's and the autopilot's lines** (slice e: `AutopilotScenario.cs`, `AutopilotScenario.FullAudit.cs`, `StartupAudit.cs`, `tools/lib/Climb.psm1`).

- The cycle line and the stop line carry ` casters=<n>` between the tally and ` s=`, read from `GearFloor.CastersHeld` (wielded, main pack, side packs) at the line's moment, and `?` while the inventory is unread. The done line has none. It is report-only (D27).
- The audit's caster step stops `no-caster` when under two casters are held and no profile vendor sells one or the purse is short; a short purse that can be refilled is a named line, not a stop. A ground with no vendor (the belt, the forest) is not audited (`TODO(m6-floor-vendorless-ground)`).
- A short floor makes the audit's trip due, and the trip is forced when only the floor is short (`KitReading.FloorShort`, `TripSpec(forced: true)`). The floor is bought only on loot trips, and the audit does not know the fight options. With loot off it makes the trip once and then says `still short ...; TODO(m6-floor-needs-loot)`: one wasted trip per audit until the fix (`LootOn` on the audit, the fix slice's R1).
- The climber loots. `tools/lib/Climb.psm1` appends ` --fight-loot=on` to the level-up job unless `-NoLoot` is given, and `-PlanOnly` prints `loot=on` or `loot=off`. The `[climb] verdict` line gains ` casters=<n>` from the last cycle line when it was read, report-only.
- `WornRestorer.ElementFor` takes the rung's element first, then the family, then the TODO. The audit's pick and the restore's log use it (`gear: restore: element 0x10: <source>`). A confirmed caster wield in the restore clears the spells-dropped flag (ACE gives the spells back with the mana, `Player_Inventory.cs` 313-315).

**The review's fixes (slice f).** GearPhase acts on a `Replace` before the sale (`ReplaceChecked`: take off, wield, check,
put the old piece back on a refusal) and wears through `WearChecked` (the slot read after the wield; `equip pass: wear`), so
a looted upgrade is worn, never sold first; the equip and return passes run on a trip with nothing to buy or sell too. A
caster counts toward two only when it is wielded, its requirements are met, or it is still unread (named): an unwieldable
find neither fills the floor nor is kept by the sale (`GearFloor.CountsAsCaster`). A `Replace` never leaves the chest bare,
and the floor buys no robe that cannot go on (`TODO(m6-robe-coverage)`: the supply table has no coverage column). The
autopilot reads the loot setting (`AutopilotOptions.LootOn`): with loot off a buyable short floor is a note (`floor short,
loot off: no trip`), not a forced trip that cannot buy; an unbuyable one is still the `no-caster` stop. A kit line cannot
carry two wielded casters (`GroundCatalog` refuses a count above 1 outside the pack slot, and `GearKit.Build` wields every
such line), but the kit's pack spare (the re-arm Wand) counts: `BSD Mage`'s built kit reads `casters=2` from its first
cycle (the item's live gate).

## 66. The spell plan by level (M6 item 1 a; D4, D41)

**The rule (`Mage/SpellPlan.cs`, pure).** ACE passes the cast pre-check with `SkillCheck.GetMagicSkillChance(skill, power)` (@95ef426d `WorldObjects/SkillCheck.cs:19-22`, factor 0.07; the difficulty is the spell's power, `Player_Magic.cs:530-536`; a skill more than 50 under the power fails outright). The client keeps one copy of that formula, `GearCasts.Chance`, and `SpellPlan.Chance` calls it. ACE's 95% line is 43 over the power (0.9530); 42 over gives 0.9498, so the spec's "42" was wrong. A level's plan skill is its power + 43: II 93, III 143, IV 193, V 243, VI 293, VII 343. `SpellPlan.LevelAt(skill, chance)` is the highest level of a line whose chance reaches the chance, or 0. The powers come from the profile's Flame Bolt line (the SpellTable's, pinned by `BsdProfileSpellsTests`).

**The plan's chance is a ladder value.** `war-mage.json` carries `plan_cast_chance` 0.95 at its top level, with `sources.plan_cast_chance` (D4, D41). `LadderLoader` requires it (a number from 0.01 to 1; a missing, text or out-of-range value fails naming `$.plan_cast_chance`), and `Ladder.PlanCastChance` carries it. No code holds 0.95.

**The projection.** `SpellPlan.ProjectedWarBase(table, level)` is the climber's base War Magic at a character level: specialised at creation (ACE `InitLevel` 10, `Player.SpecializeSkill`, `Player_Skills.cs:236`), `round((Focus + Self) / 4)` over the creation values 100 and 100 plus the planner's ranks, plus the planner's War Magic ranks. The planner is `MageSpendingPlanner.Compute` at the level's total experience (the dats' XpTable) with `MageBuild.Traditional` and the shares the spender uses at that level (`MageTemplate.SharesAt`). No buff is counted, and every later magic skill counts as trained, so War Magic gets the smallest share the planner gives (D41). Base War Magic is 60 at level 1, 109 at level 10 and 346 at 126. Check: with Creature, Item and Mana Conversion left out, level 6 projects 89, Winnie's base after her one level-6 trip in item 0.

**The rungs' levels are computed.** Each rung's `spell_level` is `SpellPlan.PlanFor`: min is the level at the plan's chance on the projection at the band's first level, max at its last (the top rung at 126). Each rung's `sources.spell_level` names both projected skills. `SpellPlanTests` pins every rung against the computation and its source text.

| Rung | Band | Base War Magic | Plan | Was |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| academy-and-chest | 1-4 | 60-74 | I | I |
| outskirts | 5-9 | 79-103 | I-II | I-II |
| burrow | 10-14 | 109-134 | II | II |
| lodge | 15-21 | 139-171 | II-III | III |
| cave | 22-31 | 175-207 | III-IV | IV |
| temple-20-40 | 32-44 | 210-250 | IV-V | IV-V |
| abode | 45-59 | 253-281 | V | V |
| quarters | 60-74 | 283-302 | V-VI | VI |
| holding | 75-126 | 305-346 | VI-VII | VI-VII |

The strategy's "III at about 10, IV at 20" was on a buffed skill. On the base skill III comes at 21, IV at 31, V at 44, VI at 74 and VII at 126 (346).

**At run time (D41).** In the level up job (`Autopilot/AutopilotScenario.Ladder.cs`, `LadderNotes`), the rung's element names its bolt line. The job reads the current War Magic through `GearCasts.TryCurrentSkill`, the same read the fight's `ChooseLevel` makes. `BoltLevel` takes `live`, the highest level of the line at the plan chance on that skill. The cap is `live`, never under the rung's plan min, and the result is the highest level the spellbook holds at or under the cap. With no skill read, the cap is the rung's plan max and the line says why. The report-only line (D27) reads `ladder: bolt: <element> <line> plan=<min>-<max> live=<level> skill=<current> chance=<the cap level's chance on the current skill> plan_chance=0.95 cap=<level>: <why>`.

**The fight casts at the plan's chance.** `LadderFightSpec` passes the chance to the den-fight station as the argument `cast-chance` (`JourneyStations.CastChanceArgument`), and `JourneyStations.DenFightBuff` sets that fight's `BuffOptions.CastChance` from it. It is a station argument like `max-level`, not an option, so `OptionCatalog` has no new entry, and a command-line `--buff-cast-chance` still wins. The den job never sets the argument, so BSD Mage keeps 0.9 (`BuffOptions.DefaultCastChance`). The buff station outside the fight keeps the journey's chance.

**The bolt line per element (closes `m6-ladder-element-line`).** `SpellPlan.BoltLineNames` maps the seven elements of `Ladder.Elements` to their SpellTable lines, which are ACE's missile categories 117-123 (`ACE.Entity/Enum/SpellCategory.cs:122-128`): fire Flame Bolt, cold Frost Bolt, acid Acid Stream, electric Lightning Bolt, pierce Force Bolt, bludgeon Shock Wave, slash Whirling Blade. `SpellPlan.BoltLine(element, spells)` returns the profile's line when the profile holds one (Flame Bolt I to VIII today). Otherwise it returns the SpellTable's War Magic spells "<line> I" to "<line> VI", taking the lowest power and then the lowest id where names repeat (the SpellTable holds item-proc copies of Flame Bolt I at power 900). A SpellTable line stops at VI (`TODO(m6-bolt-line-vii)`), since each line's VII shares its category with other spells. Two cases stop the job loudly, before any recall: an element with no line the ladder can name (`stop=failed:rung-bolt-line:<rung>`), and a line the fight does not cast, since the fight casts only Flame Bolt (`stop=failed:rung-element-line:<rung>`, `TODO(m6-fight-element-line)`). Every rung is fire today, so neither fires.

**How the two caps relate.** The fight's cap is `FightScenario.PlanCap`: the ground's `spell_plan` row for the character's level, capped by `--fight-max-level`. The level up job's cap reaches it as the station argument `max-level`. On a ladder ground the fight casts at most the smaller of the ground's row and the ladder's rule. The ground's row stays a ceiling (the outskirts' "levels 1-9 Flame Bolt II" still caps at II), so the rule can lower the cap or raise it within that row. `ground-plan-family` (`FightScenario.cs:718`) is not touched here; section 9 re-places it.

**Tests.** `SpellPlanTests` (the chance and its 43- and 42-over lines, `LevelAt` at both edges of each level, the projection, every rung, the seven lines; three read the dats). `LadderTests` (`plan_cast_chance` missing, out of range or text; the computed table and its sources). `LadderLineTests` (the D41 cap, the element's line, the two stops, `DenFightBuff`, and a scripted ACE at level 5 on the outskirts that writes `ladder: bolt: fire Flame Bolt plan=1-2 live=...` and passes `cast-chance=0.95`).

## 67. The skill credits and the spend (M6 item 1 b; D43)

**The dat's credits.** The XpTable's `CharacterLevelSkillCreditList` (retail dats; `SkillCreditTests` prints it) grants one credit at each level 2 to 10, then only at the even levels 12 to 20, then at 23, 26, 29, 32, 35, 40, 45 and 50. ACE grants the new level's credits at the level-up (@95ef426d `WorldObjects/Player_Xp.cs:295-296`). The map's "one a level" did not hold.

**The plan (`Mage/SkillCreditPlan.cs`, pure).** The order is the climber's unpaid trained lines (`MageTemplate.PlanClimberCreation(...).Unpaid`, the costs read from the SkillTable through `ClimberCreateScenario.PlanFromDats`): Creature Enchantment, Item Enchantment, then Mana Conversion. `MageTemplate.ClimberCreationOrder` is Life, Creature, Item, Mana Conversion (D43); slice b first kept the older order, with Mana Conversion at 12 and Item at 32, and h2 changed it. Never Alchemy (D34) or Melee Defense (D5), never a specialisation. The next step is the order's first untrained skill, trained when the credits cover its cost; otherwise the plan waits for the difference and keeps the order. From level 1 the schedule is Creature at 5, Item at 16 (the travel spells) and Mana Conversion at 32, pinned by `SkillCreditTests` and `FreshClimberTests`.

**The train step (`SkillTrainStep`).** Check, act, check. Before: the skill's description read, the skill untrained, and `AvailableSkillCredits` at least the cost. Act: `IActionApi.TrainSkill` for exactly the cost (`ActionSource.Automation`). After: the skill trained and the credits down by the cost, within 5 s of the action's completion. A refusal, a timeout or an unconfirmed after-check is named and never retried.

**The spend (`LevelUpSpend`, `XpSpendRule`).** The job trains, then spends. `XpSpendRule` is called again while a call ends `RaiseCap`, at most three calls, each on one line (`xp: level-up call <n>: ended <end> (spent_xp= raises=)`), then the summary `level-up spend: done: trained=<list> spent_xp= raises= credits= next=<step>`. The level up job runs it at the cycle's start, before the rung is decided, at the run's first check and at each level-up (one spend a level), so a climber at a pending or quest rung still trains and spends. A failed train stops the run `failed:rung-train:<Skill>`; a refused raise stops it `failed:rung-spend`. The `[ladder]` line gains `trained=` after `scrolls_bought=`, and `spent_xp=` now holds the level-up spend with the trips'. The trip's `XpSpendRule` call is unchanged. Both paths read the XpTable through `XpSpendRule.TableOf` (the session's, else the journey's dats); with neither, the trip fails its station by name and the level up job spends nothing that level (`TODO(m5-logistics-xptable)`).

**The Strength floor (`m6-climber-strength`; `StrengthFloor`).** Before the planner's shares, the spend raises Strength until the carried burden (the server's EncumbranceValue, read live) is at or under the line. The line is the ground's `burden_trip_percent`, at most 100: the room under 100 is the ground's loot margin (the den's 90 keeps the burden under 90%, the outskirts' 150 under 100%). The capacity is `EncumbranceSystem.EncumbranceCapacity` of the base Strength with the carrying augmentations: 150 times Strength, plus 30 times Strength per augmentation (ACE `Player.GetEncumbranceCapacity`, `Player_Inventory.cs:46-51`). The base is used, not the buffed value ACE judges, because a buff lapses. The planner lists the floor first (`StatTarget.Floor`), takes its cost before the shares, and never passes the floor over. Its line reads `xp: strength: burden=<b> capacity=<c> want=<s> (base Strength <n>, <p>% now; the line <l>% ...)`. Item 0's 1,700 BU wants Strength 12; the fresh climber's 2,460 BU (before the chest) wants 17, seven ranks, 1,988 XP. With the floor planned, the climber's base War Magic falls by at most 3 at levels 4 to 9 and no rung's `spell_level` moves (`XpSpendRuleDatTests`), so `war-mage.json` is unchanged. BSD Mage's Strength 113 carries about 68%, so its trips see no change.

**The caps and the named list (M6 item 14; D112; `XpSpendRule`, `MageShares.Climber`, `MageTemplate.OnClimberList`).** For the ladder's character the owner's rule is a rule of the spend, not only of the plan: Max Health and Endurance about 5% of the experience earned each, no attribute over 10%, the rest to her magic. The allocation of 2026-11-11 (164,873 at level 22) gave Jump 18 ranks and Magic Defense 14 because the older splits' pool holds every skill the heritage trains at creation; it gave Endurance 12% because the floor's 5% and the pool's share were two accounts and one allocation could catch a stat up to its 10% line. **Her split** (`MageShares.Climber`, in the spend and in `SpellPlan`'s projection): 55% to the magic skills (War Magic, Life Magic, Item Enchantment, and Creature Enchantment once trained), 20% to Focus and Self, 5% to Mana Conversion once trained, 5% to Max Mana, and 5% each to Endurance, Max Health and Max Stamina; what a share cannot spend goes to the magic skills and Max Mana. Strength is bought by its floor alone. Coordination, Quickness, Jump, Run, Magic Defense, Arcane Lore, Loyalty and Salvaging are never raised: the plan does not list them, and the spend checks every raise against the list (`xp: not on the list: <stat>`). **The account.** Every raise of an attribute or Max Health is checked twice: its cost in all against its percent of the experience earned (`StatCap.Limit`: 5% for the two health stats, floor and share together; 10% for the others), and what it has taken of this allocation against the same percent of the allocation. A stat's first rank of an allocation is always allowed, so a rank dearer than the share is still bought. The allocation is the unassigned experience the first call found, and a call that follows a `RaiseCap` end goes on with the same account. A held stat is named once (`xp: held: <stat> a -> b: ...`), and the walk goes on to the stats after it. **Floors against caps: the cap wins.** The Strength floor is cut to the 10% line and the health floor to 5% a stat; a floor the account holds does not make the pool wait; a floor that wants more than its cap allows is said once by a rule, by name (`xp: cap: Strength: ...`, `xp: cap: health: ...`). The one exception is a load she cannot run under: retail's load modifier is 0 from a load of 2, so at 200% of the capacity the run rate is the walk's (`StrengthFloor.CannotRun`). The least Strength that puts the burden under that line (`StrengthFloor.CureWant`) is bought over both checks, and named at every call that buys it (`xp: cure: Strength: ...`; each such raise reads `the Strength floor's run-line cure, over the cap`). **The summary line.** Each call ends with `xp: shares: allocation=<n> spent=<n> banked=<n> earned=<n> caps=health<=5%,attribute<=10% | <stat> <xp> <percent of the allocation> run <percent of the experience earned>[/<cap>%[ over]] | ... | other skills (<names>) ... | groups: attributes ...; listed skills ... | banked <n>: <why>`: each attribute, the three vitals and each listed skill, then the skills off the list as one entry, the two groups, and what stayed unassigned with its reason. `over` marks a stat whose running share is past its cap (a character built before the rule, or the cure). What no rule's next rank takes is banked, never spent on a cheap rank off the plan. The Burrow's `spell_level` moved from II to III (144 at level 16 on her split; 141 before), and every rung's source text carries the new figures. Tests: `XpSpendAccountTests`, and `XpSpendReplayDatTests`, which replays that allocation on the retail XpTable: 156,085 of the 171,369 unassigned (91.1%) to the four magic skills, 8,032 to the Strength floor's one rank, nothing to Jump, Magic Defense, Endurance or Max Health.

**Tests and open names.** `SkillCreditTests`, `XpSpendRuleTests` (at level 10 the spend trains Creature Enchantment, then spends with Strength first; the floor tests; the scripted ACE), `XpSpendRuleDatTests`. Closed: `m6-climber-creation-credits` in behaviour (its text stays in `ClimberCreationPlan.LoudLines` and the `--scenario` help until `FreshClimberTests` and the loopback `FreshClimberOptionsTests` are retired) and `m6-climber-strength`. Open: `m5-logistics-xptable` (the guard), `m5-mage-level-credits` (it names a built mage at `--mage-level`; a climber's credits are `SkillCreditPlan`'s), `m6-credit-plan-dats` (item 1 placed: a level up without the dats trains nothing, loudly) and `m6-strength-burden-unread` (item 1 placed: a floor asked with no burden or Strength read raises nothing that call, loudly).

## 68. The scriveners and the learn trip (M6 item 1 c, d; D40, D41)

**The scrivener catalog (`Grounds/scriveners.json`, `ScrivenerCatalog`).** An embedded, immutable JSON file; a missing or unknown field fails at load with its JSON path. It holds 35 scriveners, 24 lines and 109 spells: the seven war bolt lines, the seven elemental Vulnerability Other lines, Imperil Other, Vulnerability Other and Magic Yield Other (each I to VI), and the seven travel spells of the Journeyman Scriveners of Item Magic. Each spell cites the create-list row of each scrivener who sells it (D28). The data comes from `cache/m6/1/sel-scriveners.tsv`, `sel-scroll-rows.tsv` and the pinned world SQL's landblock_instance rows, read offline. `ScrivenerCatalogTests` pins name, school and power against the dats; two Creature level-I powers are 1 in the dat, and the catalog keeps the dat's value. Left out: the Viamont scriveners (0x31D6), the ACE-added scriveners (0xA25F), whose town the corpus does not name, and the Void scriveners.

**Towns and cells.** A town is named by the landblock a point of interest names. Ayan Baqur (0x1134) is an inference: the points of interest name Ayan Baqur at 0x1133001F, and the Town Network portal stands at 0x11340026. Six rows, 20216 among them, carry the cell 0xA9B30000 (low word 0); the loader resolves each to the outdoor cell under its point with `LandDefs.get_outside_lcoord` (20216: 0xA9B3003C), and `ScrivenerPlace.CellFromPoint` marks it. `ResupplyRun.Meet` reads the scrivener live by guid before the last metres, as before.

**Prices.** A scroll costs its scrivener's SellPrice (50) times its Value (ACE `Vendor.GetSellCost`, `ceil(50 x Value - 0.1)`, `Vendor.cs` 577-585 @95ef426d): I 50, II 250, III 1,000, IV 5,000, V 10,000, VI 50,000 pyreals. This corrects the map's note that Winnie's purse covers every level to VI: her 10,000 covers II to V once each, not VI.

**The vendor view.** `HuntingGround.Scriveners` holds the catalog's scriveners of the home town, merged at load by `GroundCatalog` after the profile's vendors. The merge is additive: a scrivener the profile lists is the profile's. `VendorSelling`, `PriceOf` and `VendorOf` see the merged scriveners; `Vendors`, the loot buyers and the profile checks do not change. Each merged scrivener has mask 0, so no sale goes to one.

**The learn plan (`Mage/ScrivenerLearnPlan.cs`, D41).** The lines are the rung's bolt line (`SpellPlan.BoltLine`), then the element's vulnerability, Imperil Other, Vulnerability Other and Magic Yield Other, each only while its school is trained. A line's target is the highest level whose chance on the current War Magic is at least the ladder's `plan_cast_chance`; the bolt line never goes below the rung's `spell_level.min`; targets stay within I to VI (VII is loot's, section 70). Only the target is bought, and only when the book lacks the target itself: a higher level held (a looted III over a target of II) does not count as Known, so the plan's own level is still bought and the fight's cap casts the highest level the book holds at or under it (M6 1 fix, 1-R3). The character must be able to read it (`CanRead`, ACE `CanReadScroll`). A scroll already in the pack is read, not bought. The plan applies on the ground a rung plays: its own ground when the profile exists, else its first alternate whose profile exists. The den, the Holding rung's second alternate, is not a ladder ground, so BSD Mage's den trips do not change.

**The learn trip (`LogisticsCause.Learn`, trigger `learn:<spell>`).** A Trip after every other trigger. It is due when the target is readable, the home town sells it, and `SaleMemory.Shared` has no refusal for it this session. It is recomputed only when the book, the level, the enchantments or the magic skills and attributes change. A target sold only off the home town (V at Plateau Village, Qalaba'r, Dryreach and Westwatch; VI at the Grand Master Scriveners) is not a trip trigger: it rides on the next trip, whatever triggers it (D40). Since M6 4 t4a the resupply plans it by the Town Network (`TownNetworkTrip.Choose`, `Session/Scenarios/Journey/TownNetworkTrip.cs`, section 78): the candidates are every catalog place of every scrivener who sells the scroll, the towns by name; a candidate is admitted when its town is a travel place, the travel file leads there from the home lifestone's place, the town has its own way back, the way home is Lifestone Recall or the portals, and no walk of the trip passes a lever-only door. The first admitted is chosen and the plan's line names it with every refusal and every other admitted town. With no town admitted the learn stops, logged once a session with `TODO(door-lever)` when a door refused one, else `town-network:no-town`. For the climber: V at Dryreach, VI at Stonehold. The learn itself is the resupply station's (`ResupplyStation.Learn.cs`), and the trip is section 78's.

**The loopback and the line.** `MageBuildScenario` gains `characterName` (default BSD Mage) and `withheldSpells` (arena profile spells the build does not learn), so the Throwaway can be built to the VI band (D39). `ScrivenerLearnLiveTests` is written and compiles; the lead runs it. The `[ladder]` line's `scrolls_bought=` and `learned=` come from the logistics line's fields (section 69).

**Closed and open.** Closed: `m5-learn-spell-data` (`SpellOf` falls back to the catalog, pinned against the dats) and `m5-learn-vendor` (a profile line's vendor is checked at load; its TODO stays as the guard). Open: `m5-scrivener-distance` (no code site; the catalog gives every scrivener's cell and point and the walk reads him live, so it closes if its sense was where he stands) and `m6-scrivener-town-network` (closed by M6 4 t4a: `TownNetworkTrip`, `ResupplyRun.TownLearnTrip`, `ResupplyStationTests`, `TownNetworkTripDatTests`; D40). Open gains `door-lever` and `m6-town-scrivener-stops` (section 78).

## 69. The buy-trip (M6 item 1 d; D12, D40)

**The sellers (`scriveners.json`, `scarab_sellers`; `ScrivenerCatalog.ScarabSellers`).** Eight archmages sell the carried scarabs. Each entry holds the wcid, the name, the SellPrice (the float property 38 of the pinned world SQL), the scarabs it lists (wcid, Value, create-list row) and its places. Zisaha bint Jaidka (2314, Fort Tethana; rate 1.8; rows 70986 Pyreal and 70987 Platinum) comes first, and the trip takes the first seller whose town some ground calls home. The others stand in towns a point of interest names by landblock: Uziz (1824), Sawato (2290), Neydisa (5646, Archmage Philomon, rate 1.7), Linvak Tukal (9414), Timaru (11400), Fiun (30049) and Xarabydun (35730, Pyreal only). Left out: 25 sellers whose town no point of interest names, and Jeeves (6826), the Advocate dungeon's and the only Diamond Scarab seller (D12). Zisaha sells Pyreal at 1,800 and Platinum at 18,000 (ACE `ceil(rate x Value - 0.1)`). Sources: `sel-scarabs.tsv`, `sel-zisaha.tsv` and the pinned world SQL, read offline; each create-list row was checked against `weenie_properties_create_list`.

**The rule (`BuyTripRule`, pure).** A carried stock line (no ground vendor sells it), not floor-only and under its `stop_under`, is due when the plan casts it. The plan's level is the highest war-line level cast at the ladder's 0.95 on the current War Magic (D4). The level must be at least the first spell level whose components burn the line (the ground's `components`: Pyreal VI, Platinum VII), so no constant is used. The want is `keep - held`. The arrival is the lifestone of the ground whose home is the seller's town (Fort Tethana: `tusker-temple-fort-tethana`'s 0x27800006). Outcomes: `plan-unread` is a stop; `no-seller:<line>` is a stop (`TODO(m6-buy-trip-seller)`, unreachable for the Pyreal and Platinum Scarabs); `plan-below:<line>` is not due yet; `unplanned:<line>` is a line whose components the plan never names.

**The station (`StationKinds.BuyTrip`, `buy-trip`).** Check, act, check. A character with no teleport budget (the journey's `TeleportBudget` 0: the climber; the rule, not the name, M6 1 fix 1-R13) away from the seller's town goes by the Town Network (M6 4 t4a, `travel=town-network`): the seller is the first of the catalog's sellers of the scarab that `TownNetworkTrip.Choose` admits (section 68's rule, in the catalog's order). With Lifestone Recall that is Zisaha of Fort Tethana: her walk from the Network drop 0x2681001D (outside the walls) goes round the fort, never nearer than 83 m to its lever gate, and reaches her room 0x24810102 (`TownNetworkTripDatTests`). Without the recall her town is refused (`lever-door:fort-tethana-gate`), and the trip is the catalog's next seller in a travel place: since M6 item 14 (m6-goldscarab) Archmage Sammam al-Ashiz of Uziz, whose walk from the drop and back to Uziz's portal is confirmed (`TownNetworkWalkDatTests`, the town stock cases); before it Archmage Philomon's at Neydisa, whose walk from the drop finds no path in the dats yet (`TODO(m6-neydisa-walk)`). On the climber's grounds from the Cave to the Barracks the Gold and the Pyreal Scarab are no carried lines any more: they are town stock, bought at the same archmage on the way out (`Mage/TownStock.cs`, the profiles' `town_stock`), so no buy-trip is called for them there. The hops are `PortalHopLeg`s (one `buy_trip_hop:` line each), checked after (in the town's place); a failed hop fails the station `buy-trip:hop:<name>` and the way back still runs. No seller admitted is the stop `buy-trip:town-network: <TODO(door-lever)|town-network:no-town>: ...`, logged once a session per town and scarab. The purse must cover the want at the catalog's price before the trip leaves (`purse-short`, never retried; since M6 16 E5b the purse is the coin and the trade notes of the main pack, unless a ground profile's mask says the seller takes no note: the buy is the vendor counter's, `VendorCounter.Buy`, which changes a note at the counter when the coin is short; `m6-buy-trip-notes` is closed, `TODO(m6-buy-trip-note-mask)` stands for a seller no profile lists). A built character goes by the journey's one budgeted teleport (`TravelPurpose.Ground` to the arrival, `travel=budgeted-teleport`; the teleport lands at the seller's own place, M6 1 L2) and then must stand in the town (`TownLandblocks`: every landblock the catalog lists in the town plus the arrival's; Fort Tethana's Zisaha 0x2481, its scrivener 0x2581 and the lifestone 0x2780 are one town); a mage already in the town walks (`travel=none`). It walks to the archmage (`TravelPurpose.Vendor`, reached by live distance), opens the shop, and checks that the scarab is listed and the coin covers it at the wire price (a different wire price is logged and the wire wins). A free slot is needed. `IActionApi.Buy` buys the want. After, the pack must rise by the want and the coin fall, within 5 s, else `after-check`; a refusal is `refused` and never retried. Then Lifestone Recall home (`TravelPurpose.Home`), unless the spec says `no-back`. The way back (M6 4 t4a): by Lifestone Recall when the book holds it, else (a trip by the Town Network) the rung change's `direction=home` by portals; the check after reads the home's landblock (or the travel file's start); a failure is `buy-trip:way-back`.

**The line.** `buy_trip: scarab= town= vendor= want= bought= price= purse_before= purse_after= travel= ok= reason=` is logged once, after the buy or at the end. The logistics stop on a carried line now reads `logistics: stop: <reason>; buy-trip due: <scarab> x<n> at <archmage> (<wcid>) in <town>; the station buy-trip makes it (D12); the autopilot's call makes the station since M6 4 t4b (TODO(m6-buy-trip-autopilot) closed; D44)`, where it said `TODO(m5-platinum-stock)`: it stays a named stop until a plan calls the station (M6 1 fix, 1-R4). A line that is not due reads `buy-trip not due: <why>`.

**The learn hold (`LearnHolds`, `Mage/LogisticsCounters.cs`).** A logistics trip that was due a learn and bought no scroll holds `learn:<spell>`, with its cause (M6 1 fix, 1-R1; `LogisticsStation.LearnHoldCause`). A short purse (the coin under the price) is released by the coin or by a level rise; any other cause (the scrivener not reached or not found in reach, the scroll not listed, no scroll after the walk, a refused buy) leaves the coin covering the price, so only a level rise releases it. It is logged once a session with the cause (`logistics: learn hold: ... cause: ...`). The `[ladder]` line's `scrolls_bought=` and the new `learned=` are summed from the logistics line's fields (`AutopilotTally.ScrollsBought`, `Learned`), not from the cycle line.

**Closed and open.** Closed: `m5-platinum-stock` (the loud stop is the trip: `BuyTripTests`) and `m6-carried-scarab-restock` (`BuyTripStation`; `BuyTripTests`, and `BuyTripLiveTests` for the lead to run). The old tag text remains in `GearKit.cs` (lines 160, 339 and 371, item 2's file); the startup audit's text and the `FightScenario.cs` comment now name `TODO(m6-buy-trip-autopilot)` (M6 1 fix, 1-R4), which is the tag the stop carries until a plan calls the station (item 4's hop). New: `m6-buy-trip-town-network` and `m6-scrivener-town-network` (item 4: the Town Network hop closes both stops), `m6-buy-trip-notes` (item 4 or later) and `m6-buy-trip-seller` (a guard). Closed by M6 4 t4a: `m6-buy-trip-town-network` (the station by the hop; `BuyTripTests`, `TownNetworkTripDatTests`); new open: `m6-neydisa-walk`.

## 70. The scroll keep rule (M6 item 1 e; D4)

**The rule (`Mage/ScrollKeepRule.cs`, pure).** A looted scroll is kept when its spell (`WeenieDesc.SpellId`, on the wire without an appraisal; ACE `WorldObject_Networking.cs:159` @95ef426d) is a level of the rung's bolt line or of a debuff line the plan learns, that the book lacks, that is the plan's NEXT level of the line (the level `ScrivenerLearnPlan` would buy on the current skill: `ScrivenerLearnPlan.TargetLevel`, M6 1 fix 1-R3, DoD 3's "the plan's next level") or a VII, and readable by ACE's rule (`CanReadScroll`, `Player_Skills.cs:458-471`: a power under 50 or from 300 is readable; otherwise the skill must be trained and at least the power less 50). A VII (power 300) is always readable, so a VII of the plan's line is always kept and read (D4). A looted III or IV over a plan target of II is not kept (it would be read and hide II from the buy; the loot rules sell it); the bolt line's VIII is no longer kept by this rule. `PlanLines` gives the lines: the bolt line from `SpellPlan.BoltLine`, and the debuff lines from the catalog I to VI plus FightDebuffs' VII for Fire Vulnerability, Imperil, Vulnerability and Magic Yield. `Evaluate` (with the plan's cast chance) gives a `ScrollKeepVerdict` (NotScroll, NoSpell, SpellbookUnread, NotPlanned, NotAbove (the book holds it), NotNext, Unreadable or Keep). `Hook` is the `MageLootThresholds.KeepScroll` delegate: the rung is read by the character's level at each call, and the book and skills are read at each call. The rule is wired in `FightScenario`, where the session is, not in `FightOptions.EffectiveLootThresholds`, which has no session.

**The read (`ResupplyStation.Learn.cs`).** After the walk, the trip reads each Writable in the main pack and in every side pack (a kept scroll parked in a review pack is read: M6 1 fix, 1-R2). A kept scroll is read; the rest are logged `learn: held scroll ...` with their kind (NotPlanned, NotAbove, Unreadable and so on). Each read is check (held, the rule on the live book and skills), act (Use), check (the book gains the spell: "You learn the X spell."). A refusal is named by `RefuseLearn` and not tried again in the session. A held scroll does not start a trip on its own; it is read on the next trip whatever its cause (`m6-held-scroll-trip`).

**Open for the sale (1-R2's other half).** `ResupplyStation.SaleItems` (item 2's part of `ResupplyStation.cs`) must skip a scroll `ScrollKeepRule` keeps; the lead lands it after item 2's merge.

**Closed and open.** Closed: `m6-vii-loot-rule` (`ScrollKeepRuleTests`: a VII Flame Bolt is kept at war ranks 0, 56 and 400) and the learn half of `m6-scroll-read` (`ScrivenerLearnTests`, `A_looted_VII_Flame_Bolt_in_the_pack...`: a looted scroll the rule keeps is read). The bought half stays open: a bought scroll that no learn line names still logs `TODO(m6-scroll-read)` at `ResupplyStation.cs:1276`, item 2's file. Open: `m6-debuff-line-vii` (item 4 or later: a debuff line of an element other than fire has no VII in FightDebuffs, so its VII is not kept) and `m6-held-scroll-trip` (item 4, with the long-run trips).

## 71. The picker by band and the debuffs below VI (M6 item 1 f)

**The levels.** The picker scores the debuffs at the level of the bolt's own cap at that moment (`LevelCapFor`, I to VII; the ladder sets the cap, the fight reads it). VI and VII are `FightDebuffs.Spells`, as before. Levels I to V are `DebuffRows.FromSpellTable`, built once a fight from the client's SpellTable: the spell named "<the VI row's line> <numeral>" in the VI row's school (the lowest id when the dat holds several) gives the id, name, base mana, power and duration. `FightDebuffs.LowerLevelEffects` gives the effect the dat does not hold, from the pinned world SQL (v0.9.296): the attribute and skill debuffs at -10 to -30, Fire Vulnerability Other at x1.1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75 and 2.0, Imperil Other at -20 to -150 armour, and the drains' proportion, loss and cap. A level the table lacks is named once and not scored. A debuff is scored only when the spellbook holds its spell at that level and its school is trained; one it lacks is skipped by name, once (`pick: Fire Vulnerability Other III is skipped: the spellbook does not hold it ...`). The drains as attacks stay at VI and VII (`FillDrainOffer`).

**The vulnerability's effect.** ACE multiplies the target's fire resistance by the enchantment's value (`GetVulnerabilityResistanceMod`, `EnchantmentManager.cs:925-939` @95ef426d, read by `Creature_Properties.GetResistanceMod`, :100-152), and a war bolt's damage is multiplied by that resistance (`SpellProjectile.cs:486-488`). Its landing is a resist: `TryResistSpell` rolls the caster's Life Magic against the target's effective Magic Defense with `SkillCheck.GetSkillChance` (`WorldObject_Magic.cs:104-113`, 119-168), the chance `FightDebuffs.Chance` already models. The debuff's cast seconds are the measured mean of the opener's landed or resisted casts (`MeasuredHeals`, key "debuff cast at another"); the bolt's gesture and overhead stand in until one is measured, and that is logged once.

**The target's health outdoors.** An outdoor ground's creatures carry no health row (the outskirts' and the belt's `targets` are empty), which is why item 0's climb wrote `TODO(f10-picker-data)` on 130 lines. The fight now appraises the first creature of each class once (GameAction 0x00C8 on the Query lane, with no hold: check, act with one Identify, then check on a later decision) and reads ACE's creature profile, which carries health and maximum health on any roll (`CreatureProfile.cs:47-53`, `AppraiseInfo.cs:568` @95ef426d; a class's weenie fixes its maximum health): `pick: Banderling Scout (class 6) has a maximum health of 60 by its appraisal`. A class whose answer holds no health is named once (`TODO(f10-picker-data)`) and never asked again; the picker weighs that class by the bolt. With no war option built, the bolt's numbers come from the bolt the fight casts (`FightPicker.FillBolt`: the SpellTable's mana and power, the projectile row's damage, the gesture, overhead and flight).

**The bolt rows.** Every element's bolt line I to VIII has its projectile row (`WarSpellData`: the seven lines share the Flame Bolt's damage level by level, with a speed of 15; the world SQL's `spell` and `weenie_properties_float` type 26 rows), so a rung of another element builds its war options. A spell outside every bolt line still stubs, by id.
