**Closed.** `f10-debuff-levels` (`DebuffRows.FromSpellTable`, `LowerLevelEffects`; the picker scores I to VII), `f10-picker-data` (one appraisal per class; the name stays for a class answered with no health), `m5-war-pick-data` (every element's bolt rows), `f11-unknown-kind` (every kind has its rule, and a value outside the enum fails), `f10-debuff-gesture` (measured cast seconds), `opener-unknown-line` (every ground's opener is an arena Debuff line). `f10-stamina-drain-row` was closed by slice h1: `TryStaminaDrain` reads the picker's rows. Evidence: `FightDebuffsTests`, `FightPickerTests` (`A_band_mage_scores_and_picks_the_vulnerability_at_its_own_level...`, `A_vulnerability_the_book_lacks_is_skipped_by_name_once...`), `FightScenarioTests` (the appraisal on the belt, the no-health class named once, the measured seconds) and `FightDebuffsDatTests` (Exhaustive, over the dats). The band-only rows are re-placed on items 3, 6 and 11 (section 9).

## 72. The account formula and the long run's constants (M6 item 1 g, h1, h2, w)

**The formula (`Mage/AccountFormula.cs`, pure).** One place chooses a line's components: the foci formula when the school's focus item is in the pack, else the account's full formula (the account name lower-cased). ACE's spell formula depends on the account (`SpellTable.GetSpellFormula(table, id, session.Account)` rewrites the taper slots by a hash of it; section 64 gives the examples). `LevelFloor.HeldForAccount` and `LevelFloor.ShortOf(..., accountName)` read it, and `ComponentFloor.FloorOnly` and `NeedsLineAtFloor` take the account name and a `holdsFocus` flag. Without an account they behave as before.

**The account name is the login.** The formula needs the LOGIN name the server stores (the kit's `kitAccount`, the account entry in the secrets file), never the secrets key. For the four test accounts the key and the login differ; slice h1's note said they were equal, and that was wrong. `JourneyContext.Account` is the key, and `JourneyStations.AccountNameFor(factory, log)` is the one place the autopilot reads the login; a host that gave none returns null (the foci rule applies) with one `TODO(j4-kit-account)` warning, never the key (M6 1 fix, 1-R9). `BuffOptions.AccountName` carries it to each host; it is init-only and never printed.

**The callers (`m6-account-formula-callers`).** Closed in three slices. The fight's floors (h1; `FightAccountFormulaTests`); the vitals, heal and logistics floors (h2: `PackFloor`, `VitalsKeeper.AccountName`, `HarmHealScript.AccountName`, `VitalsMeans.Pick`, `LogisticsStation(forced, resupply, accountName)`; `HarmHealScriptTests.AccountFloor`); and every host that builds a floor (w: the journey keeper, the stations, the Game's leg runners and the play host; `AccountFormulaHostsTests`). Left, named for item 2: `GearKit.CastBurns` (item 2's file). `BuildVerifyStation` now takes the login (`accountName`, `KitAccountOf`) for the mage build's kit and the fighter components (M6 1 fix, 1-R9); `TODO(j4-kit-account)` is narrowed to a host that gave no login. The cast-facts station's burn-roll flag stays on `LevelFloor.HeldFor`: it is a focus-held flag, not a floor.

**The foci at start (`m6-account-formula-start-foci`).** The two floor-only plans made before the pack is read cannot ask the pack which foci it holds, so they ask `HoldsFocusAtStart`: War and Life always (the climber's starter foci), the others only when the kit lists them (BSD Mage's four). The autopilot's twin uses `MageTemplate.ClimberName`. Open for item 2.

**The constants (`m5-batch-figures`, `m5-leave-refresh-bound`).** Measured in the long run (`cache/m6/longrun-measures/SUMMARY.md`): `FightScenario.BatchLineSeconds` 1.5 to 2.0 (`FightScenario.Refresh.cs:51`; a whole batch's median 1.94 s a line, p90 2.13, max 2.40); `LeaveRefreshBoundSeconds` 120 to 45 (`:61`; the worst leave 17.7 s, the bound never hit); `TripSeedSeconds` 120 to 85 (`AutopilotScenario.cs:218`; sell trips' median 83 s). `AccountFormulaTests.The_constants_carry_the_long_runs_measures` pins them. The leave warning keeps `TODO(m5-leave-refresh-bound)`: it names the fallback, which never fired. M6 1 fix (1-R6): the bound is the larger of 45 s and the batch's own plan (`FightScenario.LeaveBoundFor`: lines x `BatchLineSeconds` plus `BuffOptions.LookaheadMarginSeconds`), so a full same-age batch of 25 lines is never cut; the long run's measure stays the floor.

**The stagger (`m6-buff-recovery-batch`).** `FightScenario.StaggerSameAge` (`FightScenario.Refresh.cs`): when 10 or more active lines read with the same time left (within one `BatchLineSeconds`), line k in recast order is scheduled (n-1-k) x 2 s earlier, so the first recast is the most urgent and the lines are one pass apart. It logs one `buff refresh: stagger:` line per group. The honest limit: the batch still takes about 50 s. The stagger makes the order explicit and does not shorten it; shortening needs early recasts, which cost casts and buff life, and is `m6-buff-batch-split` (the owner's decision). The first live pass should show a stagger line and a 25-line batch at about 50 s; with no stagger line, the lines were not read as ties and the premise is re-measured.

**Tests and open names.** `AccountFormulaTests` (the constants and the formula), `AccountFormulaHostsTests`, `FightAccountFormulaTests` and `HarmHealScriptTests.AccountFloor`. Open: `m6-foci-augmentation` (M7). `AccountFormula` holds a focus only as the item in the pack, while ACE's `HasFoci` is also true with the school's infusion augmentation; no test character has one.

## 73. The grounds (M6 item 3; D48, D49)

**The profile's new fields (`Grounds/HuntingGround.cs`, `Grounds/GroundDraft.cs`).** Every field is optional, so a profile without one loads as before. `entry` (`GroundEntry`) is the entry portal: its wcid, guid, cell, origin, front point, `min_level` and `max_level` (PropertyInt 86 and 87, a number or null), and `tieable`, which is false when the portal's PortalBitmask carries NoRecall (0x20; ACE's `Portal.NoTie` is `NoRecall`, Portal_Properties.cs:14-16 @95ef426d). `HuntingGround.AdmitsLevel` reads it purely and is true without an entry. `exit` (`GroundExitSection`) is how the ground is left: `kind` is portal, recall or walk, with a required `source`. A portal exit names its cell (one of the ground's cells) and a straight-line `from_arrival_m` hint; the walk over the room graph is item 4's. A dungeon is not left by walk, and an outdoor ground has no exit portal. The ladder's own fields load in `Grounds/LadderLoader.cs`.

**The kill-first role.** A target's `role` may be `kill-first`. It loads as `GroundRole.Target` with `GroundTarget.KillFirst`, so every existing `Role == Target` check holds and the enum gained no value. `HuntingGround.IsKillFirst` allocates nothing and is false for an avoided creature. The draft proposes only target or avoid, so the role is set by hand. Only the Temple 20-40 marks one: the Minion 22512, which casts Acid Stream III.

**The target stats.** `max_health` is ACE's `CreatureVital.MaxValue`, the maximum ACE spawns a creature at whatever the row's `current_Level` says (Creature.cs:132-135 @95ef426d). `magic_defence` is ACE's `CreatureSkill.Current`. A profile may also carry `attributes` (the six), `damage_types` (the OR of the body parts' damage types) and `swing_s`; no profile carries `swing_s` yet (TODO(f11-swing-seconds)). M6 14 drain resistance: any creature entry (a target, an approach hostile, an outdoor creature) may carry `resist_health_drain`, the weenie's `ResistHealthDrain` (weenie_properties_float 125), written only where it is not 1; `Vitals/DrainResist.cs` reads it by kind across the profiles for every heal pick and life cast (0, as an Armored Tusker's: a drain or a Harm Other takes nothing, so Heal Self heals), and a landed drain that gives 0 where the model expected a real heal sets its kind to 0 for the rest of the process. The readers are `FightPicker.FillTargetStats` (`Mage/FightPicker.cs`, which fills the fight's target stats from the profile), `KillFirstPick` (`Mage/FightPicker.cs`, which orders the main pick; the defend and ring picks do not), and `SelfEquipJudge.DamageTypesOf` (the gear score's damage types). A value the profile does not give reads as none, and the reader names it (TODO(f10-target-attributes), TODO(m6-ground-damage-types)).

**The ten tusker profiles.** Seven are the spine (the rungs of `ladder/war-mage.json`); three are alternates of those rungs. Each is `profiles/tusker-*.json`, drafted by `GroundDraft` from the pinned world SQL v0.9.296 and checked by `HuntingGroundDatTests` and `HuntingGroundTests.The_seven_spine_tusker_profiles_hold_the_W0_counts_gates_and_target_stats`.

The entry portal's MaxLevel is 40, and ACE refuses a player above a portal's MaxLevel while `use_portal_max_level_requirement` is true (Portal.cs:172-176 @95ef426d; the default at PropertyManager.cs:608; a read-only SELECT in M6 3 found it true on this shard). The Abode's rung takes its margin of 20 from its first level, 41 (41 + 19 = 60).

The profile is not written (TODO(m6-hills-citadel)), and its element, lightning, is TODO(m6-fight-element-line).

**The target margin does not band a dungeon (3-R5).** The margin reaches only the outdoor band (`FightScenario.Outdoor.cs`). On a dungeon rung the pick takes every target at any character level, so the margin is a named but inert value there (TODO(m6-dungeon-band)); the seven dungeon rungs' texts say so.

**The account formula beside the foci formula (3-R10, F3).** The climber's nine dungeon profiles carry the account test's lines (components, stock lines and Cindrue's wares, destination 4) beside the foci formula's, so a Winnie without her Foci of Strife finds herbs, powders, talismans and tapers in stock. `HuntingGroundDatTests.ClimberAccountKeys` allows the account lines on those keys, and the theory `A_climbers_dungeon_carries_the_account_test_formula_beside_the_foci_formula` pins them. The Gold and Pyreal Scarabs appear in no Holtburg create list: carried, TODO(m6-island-vendors). `TODO(m6-kit-account-formula)` stays open, narrowed to the callers that pass no `holdsFocus`.

**The gap skips (`Grounds/DynamicSkip.cs`, 3-R4).** A dat check on a ground whose walk has a gap reports a skip with its TODO name and its numbers, not a silent pass. A gap that then passes is a "stale skip" failure, so the fix that closes a gap also removes its skip. The skipped checks are the body run of `IndoorRunThroughDatTests` and the room-graph slot checks of `DenRoomGraphTests`, each skipped by name. M6 4 r1 renamed the skips. The body runs of the Burrow, Lodge, Quarters, Abode and Holding skipped as `m6-dungeon-run-share` (the walked share was over the bound: Burrow 0.189, Abode 0.171, Holding 0.176), and the Cave, Cavern and Habitat as `m6-cave-ground-probe-021E`, `m6-cavern-ground-probe-0209` and `m6-habitat-ground-probe-011A`. ## 74. The travel file (M6 item 4 t1, t3a, t4b, f2; D50, D51; DoD 5)

**The file (`Session/Travel/travel-routes.json`, embedded; `TravelRoutes.cs`).** The travel between the rungs is data (D50, D26): 28 portal edges (each with its wcid, guid, cell, origin, destination, MinLevel, MaxLevel, PortalBitmask, its SQL rows and the placement's rotation, `facing`); the places they join (each with a `source`, checked by its test, D28); the routes of 13 grounds in order of preference (a start place, the portal steps each with its straight-line walk, and the run to the entry portal), each route admitted by the highest gate on it; the ways home (the hop back to a Network portal); the gems; and the lever-only doors (`lever-doors.json`, section 78). `TravelRoutes` loads it strictly, a bad field failing at load with its path: `RoutesFor`, `FirstAdmitted`, `WayHomeFrom`, `Gems`, `GemInto`. A ground with no route is the named stop `TODO(m6-ground-route)`, not an exception; a place with no way home is `TODO(m6-way-home)`. The ladder's `route` string stays a label (`war-mage.json`, item 3's file); a test checks that every rung's ground and alternates have a route. Two grounds have an empty-step route: the outskirts (`on-foot`) and the den (`recall-or-tie`, handed to den-travel).

**Facts** (each with its SELECT; `TravelRoutesSqlTests`, Exhaustive, reads the pinned world SQL).
- The Facility Hub holds no portal into the Town Network. Its way home is the Eastham Portal 42815 (guid 0x78A020BC, no gate), then Eastham's Portal to Town Network 43065 (guid 0x7CE95089, in landblock 0xCE95, 196 m from the Eastham arrival), then 42820. The hub's portals to the island dungeons (the eight tusker portals 42175 to 42182) open by level: the Burrow, Lodge, Cave and Cavern from 15, the Abode from 20, the Habitat from 25, the Quarters from 30, the Barracks from 40.
- The returns to the Network are not in every arrival landblock: Fort Tethana's is 43065 guid 0x7258104B in 0x2581 (135 m from the 0x2681 arrival); Plateau Village's is 43065 guid 0x749B6043 in 0x49B6 (103 m); Qalaba'r's is wcid 43066 (it drops at hub cell 0x00070133). Stonehold, Dryreach and Eastham: 43065.
- The island drops have no portal home. From a hub drop the way home is the walk to the Refuge's portal 42852 (0x7F682018): Burrow 590.1 m, Lodge 805.8, Cave 642.0, Cavern 450.7, Habitat 673.8, Quarters 1,103.0, Abode 1,328.0, Barracks 1,296.2 (the file's `island-drops` walk hints, recomputed from the SQL rows by the test). Lifestone Recall is the other way home, not in this file.
- The Holding: by the Barracks drop (the hub's Barracks portal, gate 40; run 1,506.5 m), or by the Refuge (gate 10; run 2,796.3 m). The Holding's entry 22680 is gate 60 at the walk in.
- The Temple 20-40 is reached by New Colier first: the walk of 592 m from Holtburg's lifestone to the New Colier Portal 12527 (0xABB1, no gate), then the run of 734.1 m to the entry 22698. By Neydisa's castle it is 3,450.5 m (second, not first).
- The island's entries are NoRecall (PortalBitmask 49), so none can be tied; the Temples' entries are bitmask 1 and tieable. The first-visit tie is therefore the Temples' (D51). The Holding's entry 22680 is NoRecall too: every Holding trip is a recall or the hop home, the hop, and the 2.8 km island run (D51, `m6-holding-tie-first-visit`).
- The Aphus Lassel Portal Gem 22729 (spell 2936, "Entrance to Tusker Island", to 0xF6820033, the Refuge) is in the file as `gems`, with `replaces_hops_into` the island (section 75). Its source is item 5's (Brighteyes's tusk turn-ins), so `gem=held` is rig-only until item 5 (F2).
- Places added for the buy-trip and the learn trips: the island exits (the Surface portals 22664, 22689, 22662 and 22681, to 0xF9820039, 0xFA7F0006, 0xF07F0039 and 0xEA7B0001), and Fort Tethana's lifestone 0x2780 (guid 0x72780000, the Temple 40+ profile's home) and Zisaha's room 0x2481 (guid 0x72481001). Every other profile's home lifestone is Holtburg (0xA9B4).

The ways home are `shoushi` and `lin`. The ground route `cave-of-alabree` has no portal step: the run of 354.5 m to the entry.

**The Cave of Alabree's way home (M6 5 W).** The exit 4938 "Surface" drops at 0xA7B3001E (92.3, 136.1, 30.0), outside the cave's mouth, in a landblock no place holds. The run from there to Holtburg's lifestone point is 387.2 m, planned whole and confirmed on the dats (`TownNetworkWalkDatTests.The_cave_of_alabrees_surface_exit_runs_home_to_holtburgs_lifestone`). The file's ways home are portal hops only, so the run home is not data yet: `TODO(m6-alabree-way-home)`, placed item 9 (D60, D62).

**The Alabree entry walk (M6 5 Q6b, W, W2).** The walk from Holtburg's outdoors to the entry 4937 is planned whole, and the confirmer refuses it at the cave's ramp (`TODO(m6-ramp-step-down)`, a physics ground probe; wayfinding.md, open TODOs). It is pinned by `TownNetworkWalkDatTests` (`alabree`) and stays `TODO(m6-alabree-entry-walk)` until the pin passes. Shoichi's walk in Lin was refused by the room graph as a pit edge, its steps being the room's statics; since M6 14 (the guard task) the route planner reads a doorway's static steps and the walk there and back is proved on the dats (`m6-lin-shoichi-walk` closed; the in-room half of `room-steps` stays).

## 75. The portal hop leg and the rung-change station (M6 4 t2, t3a, w6a, f2; D50, D51; DoD 5)

**The rung change** takes the climber from where it stands to its rung's ground, or home from it, by play. `RungRoute.Decide` is a pure rule over the travel file (section 74): at the ground already, nothing; the ground known tied (`JourneyFacts.PortalTieOf`) with Primary Portal Recall in the book, the recall alone, from anywhere; elsewhere, home first; then the first route the level passes (`TravelRoutes.FirstAdmitted`, the entry's own gate added): its portals as hops, then the run to the entry's front point, the entry's gate read again, the tie when the entry is tieable and Primary Portal Tie 47 is known and the ground is not known tied (read before the Use), and the Use of the entry. A level no route passes is refused by name before any walk (`gate:network-to-refuge:9<10`). A ground with no route is `TODO(m6-ground-route)`. A route with no portal and no run (the outskirts, the den) hands over to `den-travel`. A pending profile with no entry passes the portals' gate alone; the entry's gate is then the server's, read from its refusal at the Use. Home is Lifestone Recall when the book holds it (the climber learns it with Item Enchantment at 16, D43); else, from inside the ground, its exit portal (the profile's `exit`) or the walk home of an outdoor ground, then `TravelRoutes.WayHomeFrom` by portals (the Refuge's 42852, the hub's 42820); nothing known is `TODO(m6-way-home)`. The way home is planned from the ground that holds the body (`RungRouteInput.BodyGround`, F1). NoRecall entries are never tied (`tied=untieable`, D51). Portal Recall 2645 is not used: any later portal (the Town Network's) overwrites the last portal, so the tie's recall is Primary Portal Recall 48.

**The hop leg** (`PortalHopLeg`, `TravelLeg.HopThrough`; run as its own leg so that a station sees its failure). Check: present, standing in the portal's From place, the level inside the portal's gate, else `gate:<edge>:<level><<min>`, before any walk. Act: on foot to the front point, 3 m in front of the portal, with `WalkToPoint` (`TravelPurpose.Cell`), over the hub's rooms indoors; the portal by its guid, else its weenie nearest its origin; `Seek` within 2 m; peace; `Use`. Check: a teleport began, present, in the destination landblock, else `hop:<edge>:no-teleport`, `:not-present` or `:wrong-landblock`. One named recovery, `recovery=use-again` (after ACE's 0x04A7, 4 s first). The server's level refusal is read by its code or text (WeenieError 0x04AB, "You are not powerful enough to interact with that portal!", and 0x04AC above MaxLevel: ACE `Portal.CheckUseRequirements`, WorldObjects/Portal.cs:166-176 @95ef426d) and is never retried. A portal that takes the body on touch during the walk (`OnCollideObject`, Portal.cs:103-106) is `taken=yes`, and no Use is sent. A walk to the front point, or a seek, that the server ends by a teleport (`travel:run:moved`, or any teleport seen during the walk) is checked at once: present in the edge's destination landblock is the hop taken on touch (`taken=touch`, logged, no Use, the check after as for a Use); present elsewhere is the named failure `hop:<edge>:moved-elsewhere:<landblock>`, and a teleport is never answered by a front-wall recovery (M6 4 F5; ACE Portal.OnCollideObject @95ef426d). The destination check is the landblock only: an arrival radius needs the edge's destination origin on `RungPortal`, not built.

**The front point** is 3 m from the portal on the side it faces (`PortalFacing.Forward`: local +Y turned by the rotation, retail's forward axis, `CellFrame.HeadingDegrees`). The facing side is not the approach side: over the 42 distinct route transitions the facing is opposite the approach in 30, so every portal edge and route entry carries its rotation (T3a). Without a facing the front is the approach-side point. The hop logs `hop <edge>: front point <cell> (<x>, <y>) front=facing|approach`. When the walk to a facing front fails (a front inside a wall of a Network room), the hop walks once to the approach-side point, logged `front=approach recovery=front-wall`; when that walk fails too, the hop fails `<key>:front-wall` with both walks' failures (W6a, `HopOutcome.FrontWall`). Nothing else is retried. Indoors the point is planned in the room that holds it: 3 m from a Town Network portal it is out of the portal's alcove, so it moves to the nearest point a room holds within 3 m (`front-room`, logged with the metres moved); a facing point in no room goes to the approach side at once (`front=facing in-no-room`, M6 4 f3). The facing side's front point is used only when it is on the walker's side of the portal's plane: when the start lies past the portal from it (the dot of the start-minus-origin and the facing is negative), the approach side is walked first, logged `front=approach why=facing-past-portal` (M6 4 F5). Every hop of the travel file is walked on the dats from every start of its place by `TownNetworkWalkDatTests` (48 of 60 cases; 12 pinned by `TODO(m6-facility-hub-rooms)`, `TODO(m6-network-qalabar-step)` and `TODO(m6-neydisa-network-front)`).

**The gem** (`TravelGem`, the file's `gems`): when a hop into the island fails by name and the Aphus Lassel Portal Gem is held, the gem replaces the hops from here up to and including the one into the island (Use; arrival in 0xF682; `gem=used`), and the legs go on from its drop. A gate refusal is not replaced (F2, 4-R6).

**The station** (`RungChangeStation`, `StationKinds.RungChange`, `rung-change`): one station per leg, its legs the hop legs and the walks between them. Each leg names its failure, so `fail=` is never empty: the hop's name, else the step, `<edge>:walk|find|seek|use`; a seam leg's unnamed failure reads "no reason given" (the tag in `Scenarios/GroundExit.cs:212` stays). A successful tie forgets every other ground known tied (section 77). The station is called by the factory (`rung-change`, spec argument `direction=out|home`), by the autopilot's Travel state (section 76) and by the journey's own travel (section 76). The live loopback test `RungChangeLiveTests` runs on the real profiles `tusker-burrow` and `tusker-holding` (no stand-in grounds), its journey built on the ground object as `--fight-ground` would pick it (M6 4 r2); its Throwaway is built as a viable mage (Strength, Endurance and Quickness 10; Coordination, Focus and Self 100), granted the ground's supplies, bound at Holtburg's lifestone and buffed before the rung change (case (a) still withholds Lifestone Recall; M6 4 F6).

**Lines.** `rung_change_leg: n= kind= edge= from= to= metres= ms= ok=` for each leg (with `taken=yes`, `recovery=use-again`, `gem=used` and `tied=` when they apply); the plan line `rung_change plan: direction= ground= where= place= cell= level= book: ... route= legs=[...] tied= gate=; why: ...`; and the verdict `rung_change: ground= level= route= hops= walked_m= gem= tied= gate= ok= fail= direction=` (report-only in its first gate, D27); the station's verdict fields are the same.

**The pit.** The planner refuses an edge over a pit (the Abode and the Holding, section 73). `CellRoutePlanner.NotePitEdge` logs one `TODO(m6-abode-pits)` line a run, through `CellRoutePlanner.PitLog` (static; `JourneyScenario.BindPitLog` sets it at the headless journey's first step, and the Godot host sets it in `JourneyLegRunner.BuildParts`, so the line reaches the session log once a run, M6 4 r2; standard error stays for a host that sets none), and counts `PitEdgesRefused`. The far half needs a jump leg, which is not built (section 77's notes; `m6-abode-pits`).

**Open names.** `TODO(m6-rung-leg-kind)`: a leg kind with no runner is a loud stub (none today). `TODO(m6-network-direct)`: from the Network the out route goes home first (network-to-holtburg, then holtburg-to-network) before its own hops, two extra hops, correct and not short. `m6-portal-front-facing`'s live check of the Network rooms' fronts is now the dat walk (most Network portals' facing side is in no room; the approach side, moved into the corridor, is the one walked). Placed by M6 4 f3: `TODO(m6-facility-hub-rooms)` (a static ramp in floorless cells, docs/wayfinding.md), `TODO(m6-network-qalabar-step)` and `TODO(m6-neydisa-network-front)`. Placed by M6 4 F6 as `TODO(m6-fight-back-war-spell)` (a book with no War Magic projectile cannot fight back), closed by M6 6 R1F as the rule `fight-back:<leg>:no-war-spell`. The retreat is section 85's (M6 6 E, F1, F2); the corpse run from an island leg's death and the journey's recover after a `died:` failure are section 84's (M6 6 C2, D).

**A death on a leg is named, and the run fights back (M6 4 F6).** The rung change's walking legs read the character's life with check, act, check (M5 D141): before each walk (the run, the walk home and every hop's walk to the front) one line `life check before <leg>: health= alive= deaths= vitae= cell=`, and a body at health 0 does not walk (`dead:<leg>:before-walk`). When the server moves the body during a walk, the death evidence is read before any move rule: the death notice (GameEvent 0x01AC, or the 0x019E broadcast: `PlayerDied`), NumDeaths (PropertyInt 43) risen, a vitae new or deeper, or the health at 0 (ACE's `Player_Death.cs` Die, @95ef426d). Any of them ends the station `fail=died:<leg>:respawned=<cell>`, never `travel:run:moved`, with one line `died on <leg>: death_cell= killer= attackers_heard= evidence= respawned= corpse=at-death-cell`. A move with no death evidence keeps its rule (F5's `taken=touch` or `hop:<edge>:moved-elsewhere:<landblock>`, or a run's `travel:run:moved`). A held portal gem never replaces a death. The run fights back (M5 D88): while a run or the walk home goes on, a creature heard attacking the player within 10 s that stands within 40 m (`HostileReach`, the hunt's and the harm-heal station's rule and reach) stops the walk; the leg goes to the magic mode and casts at the attacker, each cast checked (the attacker alive and within the 15 m cast range; the War Magic projectile that `WarBoltPick.ChooseCastable` picks (section 85); the mana; the cast through `TravelLeg.Cast`), then peace, and the walk is planned again from where the body stands (`fight-back <n> on the run leg ended`). Named stops: `fight-back:<leg>:no-war-spell` (a rule since M6 6 R1F), `:no-mana`, `:timeout` (180 s), `:cap` (8 per walk); an attacker left beyond the cast range for 10 s is left, and the walk goes on. The leg's line gains `fought_back=<n> kills=<n>`. The retreat is section 85's (M6 6 E).

## 76. The autopilot's travel rule and the way home below 16 (M6 4 t3b, f1; D43, D50)

**The rule** (`Session/Autopilot/AutopilotTravelRule.cs`, pure; `AutopilotTravelRule.Out`, logged `autopilot travel: direction=out way=<den-travel|rung-change|gap> ground= place= where= level= tie= lifestone_recall= portal_recall= route=; why: ...`). The Travel state picks its station by one rule, in order: an outdoor ground walks (`den-travel`); a ground with a tie record known tied recalls by `den-travel`'s Primary Portal Recall; a tie record whose tie is unknown, with a tieable entry and the recall spell in a read book (or an unread book), tries the recall by `den-travel`, and ACE's 0x04A3 turns the travel to the rung change (the rule is read again); otherwise `RungRoute.Decide` plans, and a plan with legs (a routed ground: the island's, a Temple untied) or with a named stop (a gate, `TODO(m6-ground-route)`) runs `rung-change direction=out` (`AutopilotScenario.RungOutSpec`). A plan with neither is the ground's own station, except when the tie is known untied: then no route reaches the portal and the run stops by `failed:audit:portal-untied` (the den's case only, `TODO(m5-portal-retie-route)`). A rung change that fails stops by its own name, `failed:travel:rung-change:<fail>`: at once for a gate refusal, a plan's `TODO(...)` or the station's precondition, else through the station failure's recovery. Check, act, check: after a rung change that ended well the body must be present in the ground's landblocks before the fight starts, else `failed:travel:rung-change:not-in-ground`. A rung change that moves at least 10 m (or changes landblock) counts as the Travel state's progress (`NoteTravelProgress`), so the island's long runs do not trip its 900 s watchdog; a stalled one does. The start-up audit reads the same rule: a ground known untied that a route reaches logs `portal_tie=route` and goes on.

**The way home** (`AutopilotTravelRule.Home`), wherever the autopilot recalls home (the known state's "elsewhere", a recovery, the recall before a stop, the final attempt): Lifestone Recall when the book holds it, or when the book is unread (an empty book is unread, since ACE's description always carries a mage's spells, so no absence is guessed); else, when `RungRoute.Decide` finds a way home by portals from where the body stands (the island, a hub, a stop town, a routed ground's exit portal), `rung-change direction=home` (`AutopilotScenario.RungHomeSpec`, the station's name `rung-change-home`); else the recall as before, whose refusal names itself. A failed way home is a recall home's failure, and no recall is tried after it (`failed:travel:rung-change-home`). So a climber below 16 without the recall walks home by the rung change.

**The journey's travel** (F1). `JourneyTravel` asks the same rule first for a Ground travel into a dungeon ground and for a Home travel: where the rule says `rung-change`, the leg is the station over the journey's context (`JourneyContext.WithDungeon`), its verdict logged, its `fail=` the leg's failure `travel:rung-change:<fail>`. The logistics trip's ways home and back to an island ground go this way, and the death's corpse trip too (`DeathRoute.RungChange`, `route=rung-change`, `DeathHandler.RungChangeStep`, item 6's file). A journey travel with no context, or to a tied ground, keeps the recall.

**Inputs** (F1, 4-R3). `RungRouteInput.BodyGround` is the ground whose landblocks hold the body (`RungRoute.BodyGroundOf` over `JourneyContext.Grounds`), so a way home from the Burrow runs from the Burrow's exit, not from the journey's ground.

## 77. The tie memory and the one slot (M6 4 t3b, f1, f2; D50)

**The memory** (`m6-tie-memory`, closed for the autopilot). The checkpoint writes `portalTied`: the grounds the journey knows tied (a tie the rung change made at a tieable entry, or a recall that landed), as the one slot below. At the next start, before the checkpoint is loaded (a finished run's file, or another run tag's, still gives it), `AutopilotCheckpoint.ReadTieMemory` reads it for the same character only (the name and both guids known and equal: a re-created character has no tie) and puts each ground in the journey's facts unless this session knows it already, logged `checkpoint: tie memory: <grounds> tied (...); carried into the journey's facts: ...`. So the next trip to a tied Temple recalls instead of walking the route; a stale entry costs one refused recall (0x04A3 sets it untied, and the rule sends the rung change). Godot runs with `-IsolateUserData` start with no checkpoint file, so the memory carries only within one user-data folder. A plain journey with no checkpoint has no memory; its station's log line says so.

**The one slot** (F1, 4-R2). Primary Portal Tie is one slot in the client (`LinkedPortalOneDID`). `JourneyFacts.SetPrimaryPortalTie(A)` keeps the one slot (`PrimaryPortalSlot`) and marks every other ground with a tie record known Untied; `JourneyFacts.TieOf(HuntingGround)` also derives Untied for a ground with a tie record or a tieable entry while the slot holds another. A recall that lands in another known ground's arrival fails `recall:portal:slot-holds:<ground>` (the rung change) or `travel:recall:portal:slot-holds:<ground>` (the journey's recall), and moves the slot. The checkpoint stores the slot (`AutopilotScenario.TieSlot`); a file naming more than one carries none, named on the checkpoint line.

**Done since M6 4 r2.** `DenTravelStation`'s landed recall and its tie both set the one slot (`SetPrimaryPortalTie`), so a den-travel moves the slot as the rung change's tie does and every other ground with a tie record is untied (the F1 gap is closed). The pit log is wired by both hosts (section 75).

## 78. The learn trip and the buy-trip by the Town Network (M6 4 t4a; D40)

**The choice** (`TownNetworkTrip.Choose`, `Session/Scenarios/Journey/TownNetworkTrip.cs`, pure). The candidates are every catalog place of every scrivener who sells the scroll (or the scarab), the towns by name. A candidate is admitted when its town is a travel place (the place holding his landblock, else the place named as the town; else `off-network`); the travel file leads there from the home lifestone's place, reached directly or by the start's way home up to the Network (else `no-route`), every portal's gate passing (else the gate's refusal); the town has its own way back (`no-way-back`); the way home is Lifestone Recall when the book holds it, else the portals, which lead to the travel file's start (`no-way-home` for a ground whose home is another town); and no walk of the trip passes a lever-only door (`lever-door:<key>`: the vendor, a portal out, or, home by portals, the way back's first portal). The first admitted is chosen and the plan's line names it with every refusal and every other admitted town (`learn: plan: ... off-home (...): by the Town Network to Dryreach (travel=town-network), <price> pyreals at <scrivener> (<guid>); chose ...`). For the climber: V at Dryreach (its Master Scriveners of War and Life walk whole from the drop; the Master of Creature Magic needs a catalog stop), VI at Stonehold (Fort Tethana's three Grand Masters stand behind its lever gate; Stonehold's Grand Master of War walks whole).

**The lever-only doors** (`lever-doors.json`, `LeverDoors`, `TODO(door-lever)`). A door that opens only by its linked lever. The only one known is Fort Tethana's gate: door 0x72581042 (weenie 2179, at (173.712, 83.9432) in 0x2581), lever 0x72581044 (weenie 2609; landblock_instance_link 298488). Each door lists the instances a walk from the town's Network drop reaches only through it (the three Grand Master Scriveners, the town's Portal to Town Network); `TownNetworkTripDatTests` proves each finds no path from the drop. No trip plans a walk to them: `TODO(door-lever)` is the stop (use the lever, then the door, is not built).

**The learn trip** (`ResupplyRun.TownLearnTrip`). After the home walk's reads, one town a trip (a line of another town waits for the next, logged). Check, act, check: before, the coin covers the scrolls at the catalog's price (else `purse-short`, nothing remembered) and the body stands in the first portal's place (else the walk to the home lifestone's point, then the check again); the hops, each a `PortalHopLeg` with its `learn_trip_hop:` line; at each scrivener the resupply's own walk (`Meet`: the goal-tile horizon, the NPC bodies), his shop open, the scroll bought (`BuyLine`: `scrolls_bought=`); the reads (`learned=`); then home by Lifestone Recall (`TravelPurpose.Home`), else the rung change's `direction=home` by portals, and the check after (present in the home's landblock, or the travel file's start), off the lifestone. A hop, walk or shop that fails refuses the trip's lines by name (`LearnReason.TownTrip`, `town-trip`) for the session (no loop), and the way home still runs; a failed way home fails the resupply by name. One line: `learn_trip: town= vendors= spells= hops= travel=town-network bought= learned= home= ok= reason=`.

**The buy-trip** (`BuyTripStation`, section 69). A character with no teleport budget goes by the Town Network. The seller is the first of the catalog's sellers of the scarab that `TownNetworkTrip.Choose` admits: with Lifestone Recall, Zisaha of Fort Tethana (her walk from the drop round the fort, `TownNetworkTripDatTests`); without it, since M6 item 14 (m6-goldscarab) Archmage Sammam al-Ashiz at Uziz (a travel place for the town stock's stop; his walk is confirmed, `TownNetworkWalkDatTests`), where it was Archmage Philomon at Neydisa, whose walk from the drop finds no path in the dats yet (`TODO(m6-neydisa-walk)`).

**Open.** `door-lever` (item 4's later slice or M7: it blocks Fort Tethana's three Grand Masters, a Fort Tethana home's trips by the Network (the town's own Network portal is inside the walls), and Zisaha's way back by portals, which the recall serves); `m6-town-scrivener-stops`, narrowed by M6 4 r2 to one vendor: the town Scriveners' stops are catalog stops (`scriveners.json`) each passing the stop-ring check, Dryreach's Master of Creature Magic 0x7DA75030 (stop 0xDA75016D (159.94, 81.17, 18.005)), Stonehold's Grand Master of Life 0x764D503B (stop 0x64D50133 (107.5, 61.0, 78.005)) and Fort Tethana's Grand Master of Creature Magic 0x72581033 (stop 0x25810170 (107.3, 84.9, 220.0)). Stonehold's Grand Master of Creature Magic 0x764D503E has none yet: his candidate (105.0, 57.0, 78.005) confirms from the walk, but its ring point (105.5, 57.0) finds a floor at 78.82, outside 77.805 to 78.105; a point whose ring stands is the fix (item 4 or M7). The other two Fort Tethana Grand Masters (0x72581032, 0x72581035) stay open; `m6-neydisa-walk` (M7, unless a live window needs it: only a character without Lifestone Recall goes there).

## 79. The autopilot's buy-trip call (M6 4 t4b, f1; D44)

`AutopilotBuyTripRule.Call` (`Session/Autopilot/AutopilotBuyTripRule.cs`) queues the buy-trip station at the trip point (once a run) when a carried stock line (the Pyreal Scarab from VI, the Platinum Scarab from VII) is due and the station can reach its seller. The call asks `TownNetworkTrip.Choose` over the catalog's sellers with the station's own inputs (`AutopilotBuyTripRule.TownInput`, a copy of the station's private `TownInput`; `LeverDoors.Default`), and its refusals are on the call's line; no `"town-network"` literal is written there (`TownNetworkTrip.TravelWord`). The scenario passes `_context.Routes` (F1, 4-R4). The start-up audit reads the pack again after the station and stops by the audit's own name (`logistics-stop:...`) only when the station is not due or not reachable (no town in reach, no teleport budget, no Town Network hop), fails, or leaves the stack short. The fight-start stop for a carried line is `m5-carried-stock`. The island exits' landblocks and Fort Tethana's 0x2780 and 0x2481 are travel places (section 74). `m6-buy-trip-autopilot` (D44) is closed: `AutopilotBuyTripTests` (the call rule; queue with a full stack goes on to the fight; a failure stops by name; a short stack after it is not tried twice), `BuyTripCallFor`, `BuyTripEnded`. The texts that said "no plan runs the station yet" are reworded (`BuyTripStation.cs`, `LogisticsStation.cs:18`, `BuyTripTests.cs`; F1 and F2, 4-R10). The station's own limit is 3,000 s (`JourneyScenario.StationLimitFactor`), past the Trip state's 900 s watchdog, which notes the station's progress (section 76).

## 80. The quest station (M6 5 Q3, F1, F2; D54, D56, D58)

The quest station (`J/QuestStation.cs`, kind `quest`, `StationKinds.Quest`) runs one quest file step by step. Its spec names the file (`quest=<key>`) and where the run starts: `from=home` (the default), or `from=ground`, the climber's own ground, the trophy errand on the way home (D58). `steps=<from>-<to>` runs a range of the file's steps, the resume of a cut quest (F2, D62). A quest its timers say is not due is refused before any walk (`start:not-due`).

Each step is check, act, check (M5 D141) with one named recovery, and one line, `quest_step: n= kind= what= ok= ms= <the read>`. A failure is named on the line (`fail=`), with the recovery on it (`recovery=`); the station's PROBLEM line is the Academy's. The run ends with `quest: key= from= steps= done= xp=+<n> reward_line=<n> timer= ok= fail=`.

The kinds at run time:
- **go**: in the place's travel place, the walk for the step's purpose (the shared step-away recovery). From a ground, the exit hop alone when `from=ground` and `RungRoute.Decide`'s home plan from the ground starts with the exit portal into the giver's place (the island's Refuge below Lifestone Recall, D58); else the rung change home. From a town to another, the Town Network trip (`TownNetworkTrip.Choose` over the step's NPC at the step's place; each hop a `PortalHopLeg` with its `quest_hop:` line), as the buy-trip goes. No new walk where item 4 has a station.
- **talk**: the Academy's talk (the use, the reply, the stamp, the gift), and the reward line read for up to 2 s after it. `armed_reply` (a kill task's arm, the counter at 0) and `wait_reply` (the 20-hour wait, `talk:on-timer`) are read as the step's reply. A talk's expected item arrives (`GiftArrived`). A talk followed by a kill step is logged as the kill task's arm.
- **give**: the item held and the NPC in reach before; one Give; after, ACE's give line (`QuestReads.Give`), the item gone, the reply, the stamp, the reward line, the experience before and after, and the expected item arriving; the check logs `give: <gift> arrived: held N -> M`. The NPC's busy refusal (0x04CE, `AiRefuseItemDuringEmote`, Player_Inventory.cs:3405-3409 @95ef426d) waits 2 s and gives once more (`recovery=give-after-busy`). Any other refusal stops by name (`give:refused:not-wanted`, `...:not-accepting`, `...:cowers`, `...:examined`).
- **use, pick-up, wear**: the shared runners (a use's check is its reply, its expected item arriving or its arrival; `recovery=use-again`). Wear is the Academy's shared Wear. A pick-up from a container that is not a creature stops `TODO(m6-quest-pick-up-container)`.
- **buy**: the vendor met and the shop open; `CheckedBuy.Judge` (the buy-trip's checks as one pure rule: the shop is the vendor's, the row by weenie class, the stock, the wire price, the coin, a free slot); one Buy; the count risen by the step's count and the coin down. Refusals are named and never retried. Since M6 16 E5b the buy is the vendor counter's (`VendorCounter.Buy`, docs/automation-engine.md): the purse is the coin and the trade notes of the main pack at a shop whose mask takes a note, and a note is changed at the counter when the coin is short (the town trip's rule, D99), so `buy:purse-short` is left for a purse that is short with its notes.
- **recall**: the spell in the book, then a `TravelLeg` sub-run (the magic mode, `Cast` with the travel cast rules, `ArriveIn` the place's landblock, peace).
- **confirm**: the step's question waited for; `QuestConfirmRule.Decide` over every open question, each answer sent with `IActionApi.RespondToConfirmation` and its `confirm:` line; the step's question is closed after.
- **kill**: the talk before it in the file is the arm (a kill step with none is refused before anything runs: `kill:unarmed`). The body is on the step's ground, else the rung change takes it out. The ground fight is a sub-run: the factory's `den-fight` with `ground=`, `until=chat:Your task is complete!` and `open-ended=yes` (section 81). After it, ACE's counter lines since the step's mark (`QuestReads.KillCounters`: the last count and whether it is complete), with the fight's `until=met` read beside them. A fight that ends without the complete line is `kill:not-complete:<n>/<count>`.
- **hunt-until**: a count already held is done at once and logged (`held=n/count hunted=no`), so the autopilot's errand runs the same file. Else the ground fight with `want=<wcid>` and `until=item:<wcid>x<count>`; after, the count held has reached and risen. A pick-up the server refused ends the step `hunt-until:refused:<wcid>` (F1).

The done check reads `Quest.Done`: the done reply, latched over the steps and waited for up to 8 s after the last one (San Ming's last Tell follows the reward by 1 s); the done item arrived; the stamp by `quest has` where the server answers it, else the reply and the item decide. Then `Context.CompleteQuest` records, saves and logs the timer (`timer=saved`, or `memory` with no store).

**A range of steps** (M6 5 F2, D62). The spec argument `steps=<from>-<to>` (0-based, inclusive) runs only those steps of the file; a malformed or out-of-range value stops at the start (`steps:malformed`, `steps:out-of-range`). The done check and the completion run only when the range ends at the last step; a partial range that ends well reads `done=partial ok=yes`, records nothing, and the verdict ends `steps=<from>-<to>`. A range that starts past the arm takes the last earlier talk as the arm. It is the resume of a cut quest, and the loopbacks' split around a counted setup place (D62).

## 81. The fight's ground, want and until (M6 5 Q4, F1; D58)

The `den-fight` station takes three spec arguments, which the quest station's sub-run calls (`JourneyStations.DenFightOptions`):
- `ground=<key>`: a `GroundCatalog` key, the fight's ground for this station only, overriding `--fight-ground`. The station starts over `context.WithDungeon(ground)` (`JourneyStations.GroundContextStation`), so the precondition's den, the walk (`fight.GroundProfile`) and the context's dungeon all name it. The travel object is the journey's own, shared; a travel to another ground's landblock finds its dungeon by `JourneyGrounds.DungeonOf(cell, journeyGround)`.
- `want=<wcid>[,<wcid>]`: `FightOptions.Want`. The loot's `KeepScroll` hook is composed with it (`FightScenario.WantHook`): an item of a wanted wcid is kept aside with the verdict `quest: want <wcid>` under every value floor and the heavy rule (`MageLootRules.QuestWantPrefix`, `IsQuestWant`); the slots and the load line still bound it. It is noted in `SaleMemory.Shared.KeptAside` and is never judged for wear. A want turns the fight's loot on (F1). A tusk (burden 100) still obeys the free slots and the load line; only the heavy rule and the value floors are lifted.
- `until=item:<wcid>x<n>` or `until=chat:<text to the end>`: `FightOptions.Until` (`FightUntil`). Checked beside the clean minutes, at the external stop's safe point (no loot in flight, kill notices settled): the pack, side packs included with stacks summed, holds at least n; or a system chat line since the fight's start (a mark at the first fight tick) contains the text (case-sensitive; system chat only, F1). The fight ends cleanly through `EndFight` with the line `fight: until met: <what> after kills=<n> s=<n>`; the verdict gains `until=met|not-met` (only with an until), and `until=refused` when the server refused the pick-up (F1). `FightStopReason.UntilMet` ("until-met") names the stop for a caller that wants it; the fight itself ends without a stop request.
- A malformed argument (`ground=` not a profile, `want=` not wcids, `until=` neither form, an empty `chat:`, or `until=item:` with loot off) sets `FightOptions.SpecError` (`TODO(m6-fight-spec-argument)`) and the fight fails at its first step before anything is sent. The options line gains ` want=`, ` until=` and ` spec_error=`.

**The server's refusal of a wanted pick-up.** ACE's `QuestManager.HandleSolveError` (@95ef426d `Managers/QuestManager.cs:558-578`, reached through `Player_Inventory.cs:1257-1259`) answers a solved quest's pick-up with a system chat line, "You have solved this quest too recently!" or "... too many times!". The loot step reads the chat since its pick-ups began (`FightScenario.RefusedWants`). Each planned want not held after the loop is logged `loot: want <wcid> refused by the server: <text>; the item is left and not tried again in this fight`, and the wcid joins a per-fight refused set that the hook honours: no later corpse plans it, so there is no loop.

**The sale's keep rule (Q4, D57).** `ResupplyRun.QuestKeepReason` (logged `sale: '<name>' ... is kept aside (<why>), worth a look: not offered`) keeps a quest file's hunt-until, expected and done items (`ResupplyRun.QuestItemWcids`, read once from `QuestCatalog.All`, so it needs no memory across a restart). The bond alone no longer keeps an item (review 5-R13). `TODO(m6-sale-keep-scroll-restart)` stays for the scrolls.
