**Open.** `m6-outskirts-damage-types` (M7). The optimizer owns the rung's move-on as plan data (`TODO(m6-ladder-move-on)` in the ladder's source texts). **Superseded later the same night (D89, D92):** the bands became outskirts 5 to 15, the Burrow at 16 and the Lodge from 17 behind its gate (sections 106 and 107).

## 101. The skills row (M6 7 S)

**The cause.** A press on a skill row ran `UiListBox.SelectUnderMouse` twice: the list's own mouse-down, and the mouse-down message bubbling from the row. The second run saw the row selected and broadcast a reselect. `GameSkillsTab` toggles on a reselect (`SetSelection` 0x0049B2B0), so the selection was cleared at once. The attributes tab selects on mouse-down alone, so it always worked. The effects page has the same toggle and may have the same fault, not proven and not touched (`effects-page-click-select`, M7).

**The fix.** `GameSkillsTab` ignores a reselect within 20 ms of its selection (the same press). `UiListBox` is unchanged; `UiWidgetTests` pins the double message. The raise buttons had been unreachable through the mouse, so M3 D29's "works" is proven through the mouse path offline, and live as below.

**The proof.** `GameSkillsTabTests.A_mouse_click_on_a_skill_row_selects_it_and_a_second_click_clears_it`; play-checks `skills-tab-row-click-selects-the-skill` and `attributes-tab-row-click-selects-the-attribute`. The live raise on the Throwaway at 09:54: `raise_check skill=36 ranks_before=5 ranks_after=6 ok=yes` (`--live-raise-check`, with `ListPressGuard`). Closed.

## 102. The dress after a death: rewear and replace (M6 7 AE, AF, AH; section 7 D81, D82, D83)

**The order (AE).** The death handler's steps are respawn, rearm, rewear, replace, rebuff, heal, topup, route, trip, items back, relines, fight. `rewear` puts the pack's worn pieces back on right after the respawn, before the rebuff: report-only `rewear=<worn>of<held>|none|n/a` on the death line (D27's pattern; a new field is report-only in its first gate). A real death is a logged no-op where nothing worn dropped.

**Gauntlets (AF).** `GearCoverage` (`Mage/GearFloorCoverage.cs`) reads the body mask 0x1FF00, the gaps in it, and whether a piece closes a gap with no overlap and an armour level above 0. The Pathwarden Robe's priority 0x17F00 leaves the hands (0x8000) bare. `PathwardenStation.CoverageClosed` lets the burden gate take an over-the-line piece that closes a gap while the burden it leaves, less the pieces the plan sheds, is under twice the capacity (retail's load modifier is 0 from 200%). `GearFloor` buys the cheapest hand armour a profile vendor sells when no worn piece covers the hands (`GearFloorKind.Gauntlets`, `HandsCovered`); Renald's `sells` lists Leather Gauntlets 56 at 1,485 on every ladder ground (AH). Nothing in ACE refuses a wield for load: only a buy that would pass three times the capacity (`Player_Inventory.cs:56-76`, `Vendor.cs:496` @95ef426d), so the Strength floor reads the measured burden at the next spend and nothing stalls.

**The replace step (AH).** `Mage/DeathReplace.cs` (pure): `Missing` (a caster when none is held, the robe when no chest piece is worn, gauntlets when no worn piece covers the hands; nothing under the floor's level), `Plan` (the floor's plan, a caster counted as one wanted, never a mana charge), `LeftOnCorpse` (robe and gauntlets only: a caster is never left, the original is the spare). `DeathHandler.Replace.cs` runs one `ResupplyRun` with `ResupplyOptions(Replace: true)` (floor lines only: the walk, `FloorBuy`, `EquipPass`, a `ShopSeconds` limit), once a death (`_replaceTried` clears on a restart). The result is `replace=none|<kinds>|short|failed` on the handler's `Fields` and never a stop; `equip pass: check after: the hands are covered` or `gauntlets-not-worn` names the check. `rearm=corpse` buys the floor's Wand and wields it (`rearm=bought`) so the rebuff runs before the trip, else `replace: fallback by name` takes the old corpse-first path. The take-back leaves a replaced piece (`LootDecision.Replaced`, log `take-back: left '<name>' 0x..: replaced at the vendor`).

## 103. The corpse trip's budget and the death watchdog (M6 7 AG; D84)

**The trip's fights have a budget.** `DeathHandler.TripFightBudgetSeconds` is 300 s (Lifestone's own, a third of the death watchdog). Within it the trip stops for any creature within the aggro reach of its path (M5 D92). Past it the trip stops only for an attacker: a hit, an evade or a spell on the mage within `TripAttackQuietSeconds` (10 s, `RebuffDriver.FightQuietSeconds`), read from the tally's `FightTally` each frame; it fights back (M5 D88) and walks on. Lines: `handler: trip-fight: the trip's fights spent <s> s of their 300 s (<k> kills, <f> fights) and a creature is still near the path: ...` once; each resume carries `trip_fight_s= of 300, kills=`. A new death's trip has its own budget. The looting past the budget does not wait for a clear reach either.

**The death state's watchdog reads the body.** `AutopilotScenario` calls `NoteTravelProgress` in the Death state too: 10 m of the body restarts the state's clock, as for the Trip state (M6 4 F1). So the 900 s is for a body that stands still, not for the sum of the handler's fights, walks and rung changes.

**A cut's second entry.** `DeathScenario.BeginAfterRespawn`: a living, present body more than `LifestoneRadiusMetres` from the tally's arrival means this death's respawn is over: `death: entered again after a cut: ...`, no arrival wait, no vitals wait, no classification (`DeathHandler.Begin(respawnRead:)`, `handler: respawn=read at the station's first entry`). No death is counted: `DeathHandler.Deaths` is the tally's deaths of the handling (at least 1), so a second death before a cut stays counted and the third still stops the run (M5 D92). `DeathScenario.Dispose` no longer stops an observed tally: it is the autopilot's.

## 104. A walk keeps clear of the portals it is not using (M6 7 AI; D86)

`PortalKeepOff` gives `RoomGraph.KeepOff` the portals the travel data knows: they are walls to a plan, no step meets one, and a walk with no way round ends `no path: portal-keep-off:<name>`. The clearance is 3.14 m from the plan's whole line: the touch (1.357 m sphere plus the body's 0.48 m, 1.84 m, from the portal setups 0x020001B3, 0x020005D2, 0x020005D3, 0x020005D5 and 0x020005D6) plus 1.3 m a running body overruns a corner (measured: 1.08 to 1.25 m off the line at Run skill 230 to 450). The hub's eight portals and the Refuge's Network portal are scaled 0.8 (PropertyFloat 39), so their touch is 1.57 m. The walk's own destination is left out of the list. Only walks to a portal carry a list (`m6-keep-off-all-walks`). A body moved anyway keeps today's named failure and fallback. Lines: `the leg keeps clear of portals leg= portals= of= clearance_m= near=`; `the plan keeps clear of the portals name= portals= clearance_m= nearest_m= nearest=`; `the body came inside a portal's clearance (report-only) ...`; `keep_off_nearest_m=` on the run's fields; a hop's failure `<key>:portal-keep-off`. Plan time is unchanged (hub walks about 0.7 s either way). The hall is octagonal, 30 m across, a 3 by 3 grid of 10 m cells with seven portals 10 to 12 m round the Barracks portal at its centre, entered from the north at (80, -25); a portal counts within 3 m of its height.

## 105. The body and the server (M6 7 AJ; D87, D88)

**The cause.** On arrival the body is constrained to the server's position (start 10 m, maximum 50 m outdoors; 5 m and 20 m in a room; `ServerPositionPolicy`, retail `CPhysicsObj::ConstrainTo` 0x00510FF0). Every server echo moves the anchor. `ConstraintManager.AdjustOffset` (retail `adjust_offset` 0x00556DA0) adds the length of every move to one number whatever its direction and zeroes each step on the ground once it reaches the maximum, so with no echo the keys, side-steps and the walk back all give 0 and jumps are refused from 90%. The echo stops because ACE removed the player from a landblock it unloaded: a block unloads 5 minutes after its last `SetActive`, `Unload` removes every object and sets `CurrentLandblock` to null, and a teleport into a block does not call `SetActive` (`Landblock.cs:532-549, 969, 1130-1147`, `LandblockManager.cs:442-459` @95ef426d). Four things on the block's tick stop together: the position echo, the five-minute save, vitals and the worn items' mana. The session stays alive (Identify answered in 32 ms). The arrivals that fell were 300.9 s and 301.1 s after the block was last kept; the cleanest others were 255, 279 and 329 s. Proved live by `where` answering `not-in-world`, and replayed on the dats (`IslandDungeonWalkDatTests.The_Lodge_ramp_stick_is_the_constraint_with_no_echoes_and_no_body_in_the_way`: with echoes she runs past, with none she stops 0.4 m from the live stop).

**The server guard.** `ArrivalGuard` and `Core/ArrivalKeepRules.cs` in the mod: a zero-delay `DelayAction` that re-arms each pass of ACE's loop (ActionQueue, DelayManager, then the landblock tick and unloads, `WorldManager.cs:367-378`, `LandblockManager.cs:265-284`) and calls `Landblock.SetActive` once when a player first appears in a block. Public API only, no package, no patch (the M2 rule, `Nothing_in_the_mod_patches_ACE`). Closed: portals, death's respawn, logins (which also closes `ToolTracker`'s login race). Not closed: a recall cast from a chain on the player (`WorldObject_Magic.cs:1175, 1333, 1386`) lands inside a block's tick, so the guard sees it one pass late: the race shrinks from 5 s to one tick. Default on; `LIFESTONE_ACE_UNLOAD_RACE=ace` in the server's environment restores ACE's timing. Logs: `Lifestone arrival guard: on`, `<name> arrived in 0x<block>: kept active`, `<name> is on no landblock`.

**The client rule.** `BodyApartWatch` and `AutopilotScenario.BodyApart`: one read a second in the states the watchdogs cover (alive, present, placed). A gap past `Limit` (10 m outdoors, 5 m in a room) with no new server position for `HoldSeconds` 15 is a finding; one `where`. `not-in-world` re-logs in at once by the orphan's machine (one log-off, 10 s, the reconnect's tries, the probe after); anything else is named and the run goes on, and a second finding with no closing between makes the same re-login (`body apart`). The gap closing clears the count, with a line. A finding within `BodyApartForgetSeconds` 300 of a re-login stops `failed:body-server-apart`, as does a gap with no host to log in again; the orphan's own rule still stops `failed:known-state:orphaned-login`. Lines: `autopilot: body apart: ... (m6-body-apart)`, `check after the re-login: the body and the server agree`. The rule cuts the station 15 s into a run, before the runner calls it stuck.

## 106. The gates and the one owner of the rung (M6 7 AK, AO, AR, AV, AW, AX, AY; D89, D92, D93, D100 to D103)

**The ladder file's gates.** `rung_gates` lists the gates that chain (the Burrow, then the Lodge; the Cave has its own). A gate is conditions, not a level: level, skills trained, scrolls learned at the gate's level or higher, those lines up on every worn piece, the bootstrap. `RungGateRule` reads them: `BookKnows` (the book holds n or any higher level), `LineOf` (a line's name resolves by the profile's name or the dat's, "Bludgeon Protection Self" and "Bludgeoning Protection Self"; any other name throws `TODO(rung-gate-line)`), `Walk` (the chain), `AtStart` (a restart counts the lines "up" as not met, by name, except the gate of the rung she stands on), `Standing` (the foci's own condition). On a gate's own ground that gate is not read. Past the Lodge's last level (22) the Cave's gate holds her, Armor Self V and Bludgeoning Protection V with the Lodge's lines; the Temple's band has none (`m6-gate-past-the-cave`).

**One owner.** `RungOwner.Decide` takes a `RungAsk` (who asks: the start, the move-on, the cycle's check, the fight's read, the way out, a corpse run; `TrophyDue` for the tusk job) and answers a rung and a reason: `band`, `gate-held:<rung>`, `gate-open:<rung>`, `stands-on:<ground>`, `stop-named:<rung>`, `job:tusk-female`, `quests-done`. Unknown buffs never open a gate. One line: `ladder: rung: asked by <path>: ...`. A run's own gate is read each time she leaves for the ground (`ladder: way out:`); a shut gate stops `rung-moved:<lower>`, ok, no walk. A repository test holds that nothing else picks a rung. `GroundOf`, `CorpseRun` and `CorpseRunAnswer` (AY) answer a corpse run: a shut gate means no fetch.

**The corpse fetch for coin.** `corpse_coin` in the ladder file (`coin_on_corpse` false): a corpse is fetched for coin alone at 2,000 or more from a safe cell, but ACE destroys a dead player's coin while `corpse_destroy_pyreals` is on, so a coin-only death logs `no-fetch:coin-destroyed` (D102).

**The pack.** `health.pack` on seven rungs: want = hit x (N + (pack - 1) x (N - 1)). `big_pack` in the ladder file and `AutopilotCheckpoint.PackHold`: two deaths with five or more awake within 24 m hold her to the Lodge's first three slots until her base mana grows by 20; the checkpoint field is additive (an older file reads null). The pay limit (30%) stays and blocks the want from the Burrow to the Cave (D101).

## 107. Buffs: the bar, the order, the pass (M6 7 AK, AN, AO, AT, AZ; D90, D91, D96, D97)

The bar while buffing is 0.75 (`plan_buff_chance`, read on the live skill, buffed and under vitae, again after each landed step); combat keeps 0.95 (D4, D41 changed for buffs only). The order: the bootstrap (Focus, Willpower, Creature Mastery), the regeneration lines (D96), the masteries, the armor lines, the attributes, Invulnerability (pinned by the climber's buff-order test at the sixteen lines). The catalog carries Armor Self and Bludgeoning Protection to IV, Impenetrability and Bludgeon Bane, the foci and the drains (V and VI are `m6-self-buff-lines-v-vi`). ACE reads the buffed skill for a scroll, so a III needs 50 and a IV 100 (`Player_Skills.cs:458-471` @95ef426d).

**The pass cannot stall (AN).** A climber's pass waits lying down, presses and drinks to `buff_pass_wait_seconds` (900), then ends done with what stands, names what is missing, and those lines are not due again for as long (`start_only_lines`, default empty, is the owner's to fill). `AutopilotState.Buff`'s watchdog reads that limit (AO). Its line: `buff: pass: casts= mana_base= ...` with seconds, potions, rests, presses and what stands. **A learned pass (AO).** `LearnedPassRule`: on a rung, in the ground, a whole start pass is owed on the run's first run and when the book's size differs from the last pass's, after the attacker and the cut trip, before the audit's own buff arrow (`ladder: pass: check before:` and `check after:`). **The pass's place (AW).** A full pass runs at home or where nothing attackable is within 24 m; more than `pass_home_over_lines` (4) lines due with a creature near walks home first, once a pass (`ladder: pass: place:`); a pass in the ground that a creature keeps standing is cut, once, and the creature shot first (AT, `BuffOptions.ShootFirstMetres`, `RestBlockerRule`). **A refresh (AZ).** The lookahead horizon is the margin alone (60 s); the fight's mean is read and logged only. `FightScenario.RefreshPassWatch` ends a soft pass when she was attacked since it began, a hostile is in reach, or a creature that can attack is awake in reach; a hard pass (a line under the floor) still casts under fire and ends only when it must wait for mana or change mode. `refresh_mana_reserve` is 60 in the ladder file; no lookahead chains beside an awake creature. Line: `buff refresh: the pass for X is ended: the fight's order comes first: ...`; `RefreshAborts` is report-only.

## 108. Rest, drain and the mana loop on every ground (M6 7 AN, AO, AW; D94, D95)

**Lying down.** She lies down to recharge where nothing attackable is awake within reach (`NearestAttackableCreature`: the flag 0x10, `WorldObject_Networking.cs:864` @95ef426d; a town NPC no longer holds her up) and stands at the first hit. `Vitals/RestEcho.cs` reads the server's motion for the player (low word 0x0014 sitting, 0x0013 lying): `vitals: check after: the server's motion shows the posture`, `failed=no-echo` after 3 s (Lifestone's own), `failed=posture-lost` (`MaxPostureLost` 2), `vitals: rest ended: posture <what the server showed> ...` with ACE's rate beside the measured one, `rest: stretch:`; the same checks serve `buff: pass: check after:` and `enter_recharge: check after:`. `vitals: rest ended:` reports what it gained (presses added back), what it spent and the net. **Full bars (AN).** In the Lodge `fight.pull_full_percent` is 100: a named check before the entry and before every pull, a standing rest and a hold, never a pull; `rest_s_per_kill=` lets the lead measure a fuller line outdoors. The Lodge entry check runs on the RungChange `enter` leg only (`m6-enter-check-tied-recall`).

**Drain.** `vitals.drain_under_percent` (50): at or below it she drains from the fullest target in reach, level by best heal, on every ground; an out-of-band outdoor attacker is a candidate and an outdoor class carries its max health in the drain pick. ACE sends a creature's stamina only on a successful appraisal (`CreatureProfile.cs:47-66`), so the fight identifies creatures in reach at most once each 5 s while the loop wants them, and a target with none is passed over by name. **The mana loop.** With no Mana Conversion: mana under 30 (the loop starts at 45, the lead's eb5bf070) and stamina at least half presses Stamina to Mana I; under half, Drain Stamina Other from the creature holding the most, where one cast gives at least 30 and needs 20 mana. Costs: Drain Health I power 38, II 88; Drain Stamina I power 38 (proportion 0.1, cap 60); Heal Self 1, 50; Regeneration and Rejuvenation 1, 50, 100, 150 at x1.1, 1.25, 1.4, 1.55. Rates (`Creature_Vitals.cs:102-150, 210-236`): stamina 0.6 a second standing, 1.8 lying, 1.5 sitting, 0.3 in combat; Rejuvenation III 2.5, IV 2.8; mana 0.2, 0.25 under Mana Renewal II, no stance factor. A press from S nets 0.45 S - 10.

## 109. Logistics at her level: components, sale, foci, notes (M6 7 AR, AT, AU, AX; D98, D99, D105, D106)

**Loot at her level (AR).** The rule is 10 Value a burden unit, `loot.radius_m` 60 outdoors and 25 in a dungeon, the load line 125% outdoors and 110% in a dungeon, sold every trip. The sell price is `max(1, floor(rate x Value + 0.1))`, rate 0.9 at every Holtburg vendor (`Vendor.cs:591-598` @95ef426d); Renald's mask has no jewellery or gem, Monyra's (716, mask 0x40808) buys them. Gate A's sample: 12 corpses opened of 457, 445 beyond the radius; expected coin about 60,000 an hour. Copper and Silver Scarab keep 3 with a trip at none; no trip for one Mana Potion.

**Components, sale, learn (AT).** `BuffCycle.NoteComponent` tells `ComponentNeeds.Shared` of a component a pass lacked; `LogisticsCounters.ApplyNeeds` raises its keep and trip_under to two passes (`PassesKept`): trigger `stock:<name>`. `LogisticsCause.Sale` (trigger `sale`): `loot.sale_trip_value` (`GroundLoot.SaleTripValue`, 15,000; 100,000 from a dungeon), after learn in the check order, needs a held-back stock line or an unpaid due scroll (`_learnCoinShort`). `purse.learn_trip_coin` (`GroundPurse.LearnTripCoin`, 15,000), `LogisticsCounters.LearnBatch` 2. **The recall (AS, AV).** Lifestone Recall then Tie in the coin order after the first scrolls, at the 0.75 bar; the tie at Holtburg's lifestone once both are learned. A restart plans `AutopilotTravelRule.Home` without the recall first; legs with no portal and no stop go on foot whatever the ground's kind; a recall refused 0x0400 sets `JourneyFacts.LifestoneRecallUnavailable` (`recall-unavailable:components`) for the run.

**The foci (AU, AX).** `scriveners.json` `foci` (Foci of Enchantment 15268, of Artifice 15269; create-list rows 76977 and 77964; Value 500, burden 400): the price is `max(1, ceil(SellPrice x Value - 0.1))` with SellPrice 50 on scriveners 20205 and 20215, 25,000 each (`Vendor.cs:577-585`). `Mage/FociPlan.cs` picks the next one once the Burrow gate's own conditions are met, the school is trained and a home scrivener sells it; `LogisticsCause.Foci` (trigger `foci:<name>`, the climber only) is checked before the learn trips; `PlanFoci` is first in the trip's buy list, paid from the whole purse, with `foci: check after:`. A focus arrives as ContainerType 2 (`WorldObject.cs:453-462`), so the check and the counters read every place a ware is held (`GearInventory.CountOf`, type-2 entries), `BoughtArrivalSeconds` is 10, and a ware not seen at the limit logs `TODO(m6-bought-unseen)` and holds its line out of the next plan once. The spare Foci of Enchantment stays (a sale and a drop leave it alone).

**Notes and coin (AU and the lead).** `purse.min_note` and the floor: on the Burrow and the Lodge she keeps 30,000 loose and buys notes from 10,000 above that (a death halves loose coin and no note, `Player_Death.cs`); a note costs 15% to buy. `NextNote` reads all ten of ACE's notes (`PurseNotes.All`); any Holtburg scrivener pays a note at its face (`VerifySellItems` does not read `MerchandiseMaxValue`, `Vendor.GetBuyCost`). A Pyreal stack is 25,000 (weenie 273), so 100,000 of coin takes 4 slots; three free slots stay free on the climb's grounds. Health Draught 2457 and Mana Draught 2460 are unsellable: `IsUsableConsumable` keeps them and `VitalsMeans.FindManaPotions` falls back to the Mana Draught.

## 110. The tusk pull and the outdoor wall (M6 7 AX, AM; D100, D104)

**The pull.** `FightScenario.Pull.cs`, started when `RungOwner` answers `job:tusk-female`: walk (3 legs) to `hunt.pulls[0].stand` of `tusker-burrow.json` (`GroundPull.Stand`, `PullStand`), find the holder by weenie and cell, wait up to 420 s for it to be sent, count one try (two a session, `TrophyPullMemory` on the session's state), lift the keep-out, cast at the named holder, fight the pack by the ordinary fight and loot the tusk by the ordinary loot. A kill on the way to the stand starts the walk count again (the lead's 0609af70). Ends: `pull: done`, `pull: failed:<stand-unreachable|stand-no-walk|holder-absent|no-tusk|shot-blocked>`. The shot does not read the sweep (it is logged): the server sending the holder is the check; a bolt on the ledge ends `failed:shot-blocked`. The Burrow's `retreat_health_percent` is 40 now that she holds Lifestone Recall.

**The outdoor wall (AM).** A bolt that stops short outdoors keeps the fight on its target: the mage closes toward it to a better line (twice, the second also to the side) and after 3 wall hits on one target blocks it 120 s; the outdoor walk's line test reads the terrain (the pick no longer takes a target behind a hill that grazes the line by under 0.5 m). Dungeons keep the tour's next cell (F23's rule). A fallback to the old rule is logged by name (`m6-wall-stay-no-spot`, `-no-leg`, `-no-position`).

## 111. The corpse trip, the bind and the keeper that fights back (M6 7 BB, BC, BD; D107, D108)

**The corpse trip (BB).** The keeper no longer stands before a fight under fire (`autopilot fight-back:`). A corpse trip is for need and safety (`handler: corpse trip:`; `trip_abort=cell-unsafe` is new): coin on a corpse is destroyed, so there is no walk for coin. `corpse_coin.min_item_value` (default 20,000 Value) sits next to `min_coin`; ACE's drop line carries no Value, so `TODO(corpse-item-value)` (open the corpse or read the item table) and `TODO(corpse-quest-item)` (no quest item list yet) are named.

**The bind (BC).** `TravelLeg.RestForSpell(spell, seconds)` (`SpellManaSeconds` 120, `SpellManaMet`) checks the mana against `GearCasts.ManaCeiling`, rests in place and checks again, one line each side; `BindStation` calls it before the tie and `RecallHomeStation` before the recall. A tie whose mana does not come back, or that does not link, is a logged `TODO(m6-bind-tie-mana)`; the station stays ok (`tied=no`, `bound=yes`). The climb uses the tie only for Lifestone Recall (ACE `LinkedLifestone`, `WorldObject_Magic.cs:966-976` @95ef426d). `AutopilotTravelRule.Home` answers `TravelWay.AtHome` when the body is at home. With all four foci held, the recall costs the foci formula's Copper Scarab and Prismatic Tapers (both outskirts stock lines); the full formula's Comfrey and Powdered Malachite have no stock line (`TODO(m6-recall-components-stock)`).

**The keeper rule (BD).** `AutopilotScenario.KeeperFight.cs`: with a hostile on her in any state's keeper phase or any station's wait on a ground, `VitalsKeeper.Halt` stops the keeper at once, she fights back until nothing hostile is in reach (stop reason `keeper-fight-back`), and the state resumes from its start. A trip waits for the lull; a stop line with a hostile on her takes Lifestone Recall by name when payable; a leave refresh ended by an attack is dropped. Log lines: `autopilot keeper: check before:`, `vitals: pass halted:`, `autopilot keeper: the fight-back is over after`, `autopilot fight: the trip waits for the lull:`, `autopilot fight: urgent-trip:`, `buff refresh: leave: dropped:`; the cycle line gains `why=keeper-fight-back:<n>`. Stand-downs, each by design: the retreat's way home, the urgent recall, the recall before a stop, a death not yet handled, a scripted death, the heal in place under the ground's retreat line, a one-shot task. Open: `TODO(keeper-fight-fix-phase)`, `TODO(keeper-fight-awake-read)`. The tusk cannot reach a corpse: it is Bonded and Attuned, and ACE takes Bonded items out of the death items (`Player_Death.cs:502` @95ef426d).

**The trophy turn-in (D107).** A trophy held to its count is turned in wherever it was hunted, not only on the rung's own ground.

## 112. The way out: a retreat for mana (M6 7 BE; D109, D110)

On the ladder's job with Lifestone Recall ready, attackers on her and the mana at or under the line (the recall's need plus one Drain Health Other I, read from the spell table and the live pool), she leaves by the retreat's stop and Lifestone Recall by name. No bolt or buff takes the mana under the line while attackers are on her, unless it is the bolt that kills the last attacker; the emergency's heal may spend into it while the recall stays paid or when the next hit kills. `retreat: mana:` lines are the way out: `decide` (each change of the rule's mind), `check before the recall`, `check after`; the cycle line says `why=retreat-mana:<n>`; the fight's own lines are `way out:` (armed, off, a bolt or a heal refused, a line waiting, a press before the line). The retreat counts in `retreats=` and never toward `retreat:again`. The pure rule is `ManaWayOut`; with no Drain Health Other I in the spell table it stays off and says so (`TODO(m6-way-out-drain-row)`). Numbers: Lifestone Recall 50, the station's share 20% (`RecallHomeStation.MinManaPercent`), Drain Health Other I 10, bolts III 15 and IV 20.

## 113. Life Magic through an obstacle (M6 item 14; `m6-life-through`)

**The fact.** ACE asks no line of sight of a spell that has no projectile. A targeted spell's range is checked in two dimensions and nothing else (`Player.VerifySpellRange`, `Player_Magic.cs:481-506` @95ef426d, before and after the wind-up), and the spell is resolved at once on its target (`CreatePlayerSpell`, `:1098-1135`); only a projectile is tested against the world (`IsProjectileVisible`, `WorldObject_Magic.cs:1835`, and the flight in `SpellProjectile.cs`). So Drain Health Other and Harm Other land on a creature in range whatever stands between. Live 2026-11-12 13:00 to 13:09 UTC, the Tusker Cave: a Tusker Crimsonback stood behind a torch 2.5 m from the mage; its blows reached her, every Flame Bolt met the torch, and the fight could only walk.

**The rule (`FightScenario.LifeThrough.cs`, `LifeThroughRule`; `--fight-life-through`, default on).** When self-defence has an attacker no bolt can be cast at from where she stands (no clear line and no struck proof, past the bolt's range, in a no-go cell with no line, or dropped by the shot rule after wasted casts) and it stands within the range of a life spell she can cast, she casts at it where she stands, in place of the walk toward it, the sidestep, the tour's leg, the step and the hold. It is asked again at every pick: it ends when the attacker is dead, gone, out of range, or castable with a bolt again (a clear line with no drop standing).

**Which spell.** Drain Health Other takes a share of the target's current health and gives it to her, scaled to the health she is missing (`HandleCastSpell_Transfer`, `WorldObject_Magic.cs:697-760`): it takes nothing while she is unhurt and can never finish a creature. Harm Other takes a fixed amount: a whole number from `boost` to `boost + boost_Variance` of the world's `spell` row (I -4 and -2, II -7 and -5, III -10 and -9, IV -16 and -17, V -24 and -23, VI -33 and -30, VII -42 and -37), times the target's health-drain resistance (`HandleCastSpell_Boost`, `:474-601`); the caster's damage rating, skill and wand do not enter. The drain goes while the drain pick finds a level worth a cast and it is expected to take at least what Harm Other would; from there Harm Other, at the highest level the book holds, her Life Magic casts at the fight's cast chance and the pack pays. On a Tusker Crimsonback (110 health, Magic Defense 94, resistance 1.0) Harm Other IV takes 16 to 33, 24.5 on average, and at Life Magic 267 lands 99 casts in 100: four to seven landed casts for the kill. With no Harm Other known and no drain worth a cast, the walk and the sidestep stand as before, and one line says why.

**Its place.** In the pick's order: the retreat's drink for the recall, the emergency, the mana reserve and the buff refresh come first; then self-defence. An attacker with a line is the bolt's. With none, Heal Self goes first while the health is under the drain line, then this rule, then the walk. Before each cast the way out is asked as for a bolt (`way out: the life cast is refused` and its press or potion) and the mana order runs as before a bolt. A cast the server refuses for mana (0x0401) is no miss: the next waits for its whole cost.

**The bounds.** Three casts in a row at one attacker that do not land (resisted, fizzled, out of range, unproven) set it aside for 120 s (`m6-life-through-aside`), and so do 40 casts that leave it alive (`m6-life-through-bound`); while it is aside the walk stands as before, and nothing takes the stop back. The loop of 2026-11-12 13:00 UTC (48 casts at one unreachable tusker) is two wasted bolts and three life casts under these bounds.

**The kill and the lines.** ACE writes "With <spell> you drain N points of health from <name>." for a landed Harm Other, the killing one too, and sends the kill notice as for any kill. The line proves the cast, N comes off the creature's modelled health and counts in `damage_dealt=`; the kill is counted and settled as a bolt's. Each decision is one `m6-life-through:` line with the attacker, why the bolt cannot reach it, the spell, the modelled health and what each spell was expected to take. The verdict line carries `life_casts= life_drains= life_harms= life_kills= life_misses= life_asides=` once the rule has cast (report-only).

**Learning it.** Harm Other I to VI are in the scrivener catalog (kind `attack`; scrolls 1554, 2687 to 2691). The plan buys one level: the highest her standing Life Magic casts at the plan's chance that a scrivener of the ground's home town sells (Holtburg sells I to IV); a higher level sold only off home is the Town Network's once the home's is in the book. On the account formula Harm Other I to IV burn Mandrake and Hemlock Talisman, which the outskirts, the Lodge and the Burrow stock from Archmage Cindrue.

## 114. Every armour line on her armour (M6 item 14; `m6-banes`)

**The order.** The owner, 2026-11-12: before a run through the Direlands at level 40 she has every armour protection on her armour, not only the tuskers' two. Her plan learned and her pass cast Impenetrability and Bludgeon Bane; that morning a creature with piercing and electric attacks killed her in 50 seconds.

**The lines (`Mage/ArmourBanes.cs`).** Six more lines of her profile alone (BSD Mage's profile, build and kit are unchanged), each learned by play: Piercing Bane 1569 to 1574, Blade Bane 37 and 1558 to 1562, Lightning Bane 1535 to 1540, Flame Bane 1547 to 1552, Frost Bane 1523 to 1528, Acid Bane 1493 to 1498 (I to VI; VII 2113, 2094, 2110, 2102, 2104, 2092; VIII 4412, 4393, 4409, 4401, 4403, 4391). Each is Bludgeon Bane's pattern in the SpellTable (`ArmourBanesDatTests`): powers 1 to 400, 1,800 s to level V, base mana 10 to 80 and mana mod 2 to 14, target type Vestements. A bane adds the world's `stat_Mod_Val` (0.111, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5 at I to VI) to each piece's protection against one damage type (`Creature.GetArmorMod`, `Creature_BodyPart.cs:65-100` @95ef426d). It cuts a creature's body-part and weapon hits; a spell projectile reads resistance and absorb only, never armour (`SpellProjectile.cs:486-557`).

**How a bane reaches the pieces.** A player casts it on herself: ACE accepts a creature as the target of a Vestements spell (`Player_Magic.cs:1391-1393`) and gives a self-targeted impen or bane to every equipped object that is Clothing or a shield and enchantable (`WorldObject_Magic.cs:2096-2122`); cast on one piece it lands on that piece only (`:2101-2105`). So the cycle casts each of the eight once, at her own guid, as it always cast her two, reads the pieces from the "You cast ... on ..." lines and keeps each piece's time in the armour memory (seeded by appraisal after a login). The pass casts the eight together, after the life protections: Impenetrability, Bludgeon Bane, Piercing, Blade, Lightning, Flame, Frost, Acid.

**Mana and time.** One cast pays the base mana and the mana mod for each such piece (`Creature_Magic.cs:22-31`) before Mana Conversion: 40 + 8 x 10 = 120 at level IV on the ten pieces she wears, 960 for the eight (V: 150 and 1,200). The live log of 2026-11-12 (levels 35 to 37, Mana Conversion 206, pool 323) reads 3.05 s a cast and 1 to 90 mana (nine casts, mean 25): a pass of the eight is about 25 s and 200 mana.

**Where they are kept up.** The pass at home, after the buff bot's stop and before she leaves, casts all eight. In the field (the fight's refresh and top-up, a pass in the ground, the upkeep's pass) one of the six is wanted only where the ground's targets deal its damage type (`BuffOptions.FieldDamageTypes`, the profiles' `damage_types`: the tusker grounds name bludgeon alone, the Crater cold and fire); her two lines are kept as before, and the rung gates name them alone. The reason is the batch: eight lines cast together come due together, and under the fight's hard floor that would be 25 s with no bolt and most of a pool every half hour, for lines that cut nothing a tusker deals. A bane left to the home pass is not recast, not due and not counted as run out in the ground; it is cast again at each trip home. One log line for each of the six when the place changes: `<line>: <spell> (<id>) is in the spellbook; in the field (...) it is not cast and not kept up: the pass at home casts it (m6-banes)`.

**Learning them.** The catalog holds the six I to VI and her two to VI (kind `item_armor`), with the Master Scriveners of Item Magic (20211, 30027) and the Grand Masters (20212, 30028) and their places; the walks from the Network drops to the Master at Dryreach and the Grand Master at Stonehold are confirmed on the dats (`m6-item-master-stops` for the eight others). The plan reads each line at the buff bar on her standing skill and buys the home's level first when the bar's level is sold only in another town (Harm Other's rule). A level is planned only when a vendor of the ground's trips sells its scarab (`ScrivenerLearnPlan.ArmorLevelInReach`): level V burns a Gold Scarab, which no vendor in Holtburg sells, so on the Holtburg grounds her level is IV (Holtburg's Scrivener of Item Magic, 5,000 pyreals a scroll; a Silver Scarab and three Prismatic Tapers a cast) whatever her skill (`m6-armor-scarab-reach`). The six are planned from level 32 (`from_level` in the catalog: the first level of the rung whose band ends at the level the order names); under it each answers `later` and the low rungs' coin and pass are as before.

**Lines to look for.** `learn: plan: rung <key> level <n>: <Line> IV (<id>): due: ... level V burns a Gold Scarab 687 no vendor of this ground's trips sells ...`; at home the buff station's verdict with the six after her two (`levels=...,Impen:IV,BludB:IV,PierceB:IV,BladeB:IV,LightB:IV,FlameB:IV,FrostB:IV,AcidB:IV`) and `<Line>: 10 pieces enchanted, each ends 1800 s after the cast's UseDone`; in the ground the six `the pass at home casts it (m6-banes)` lines, then `buff refresh: hard:` for Impenetrability and Bludgeon Bane alone.

## 115. The quest selection and the Tusker Guard Kill Task (M6 item 14; the guard task)

**The option.** `--autopilot-ladder-quests` takes `on` (the default: every ladder errand and trophy turn-in, no kill task), `off`
(the sprint) or a list of the quest catalog's keys and the group `tusks` (every `tusk-*` turn-in at Brighteyes): only the named
quests run, each other one is skipped by name once a run, and a kill task named in the list is run by the level up job
(`LadderQuestSelection`, `LadderKillTask`). `climb.ps1 -Quests tusks,tusker-guard-kill-task` passes it; `-Quests` and `-NoQuests`
together are refused.

**The task.** Every step is read from the server's own lines (`ladder: kill task: key=... phase=... counter=N/500 read=...`): the
talk to Shoichi in Lin is an errand from home while the counter is unread and the 20 h timer allows (the quest station's steps
0-1: his start arms the counter at 0, his count "You've killed N out of 500 Tusker Guards." reads it, his done reply means it
was complete and that talk was the turn-in, his wait reply records the timer); while it is armed the rung choice takes the
Tusker Barracks in place of her rung's ground (`kill-task:<key>`, her own rung's plan and margin, the Abode's gate read at
each way out); every "You have killed N Tusker Guards!" line moves the counter; the complete line ends the fight in a lull
(`kill-task-done`, the cycle closed `state=kill-task`) and the turn-in (steps 3-4) starts from there; after each talk the
rung is read again, so she moves to the Barracks or back to her own ground by a normal rung change. Supply trips, the bot's
trips and deaths are the loop's own; a gate read shut at a way out holds the task until the next stop at the bot. With
`tusks` selected the fight on the Barracks keeps the Guard Tusk (22425) and the next way home turns it in at Brighteyes.

**The walk to Lin.** Shoichi's street door 0xDA3B0109 opens with its sill 1.2 m over the entry's floor; its three static
steps are now read at a doorway (the route planner's steps down past a doorway), and the walk there and back is proved on
the dats (`TownNetworkWalkDatTests`).

## 116. Housing: the guardian, the house, the window and the house actions (M6 villa)

**The read model.** `GameState.Guardian` (`HouseGuardian`) is the last HouseProfile (GE 0x021D): the dwelling's type, owner, MinLevel, the
purchase price and the rent lines with what is paid (`IsRentPaid` is ACE's `SlumLord.IsRentPaid`). It opens on the first profile
(`GuardianOpened`), refreshes on a later one for the same guardian (`GuardianProfileChanged`) and closes by the vendor's rule (out of the
guardian's use radius plus 1 m, another guardian, the object deleted, the world left; `GuardianClosed`). `GameState.HouseStatus` is
Unknown until HouseData (Owned, `GameState.House`) or HouseStatus (None) arrives; `OwnedHouse.RentDue` is the rent time plus ACE's period
(30 days, 90 for an apartment). `HouseInfoRevision` rises with each. A storage chest needs nothing new: it is a chest, its contents are
`GameState.Containers.Viewed` once opened (section 36), and the ordinary moves put an item in (`MoveToPack(item, chest)`) and take it out
(`PickUp`).

**The window model.** `GameSession.GuardianWindow` (`GuardianWindowModel`) is the guardian window's state, shared by the drawn
`gmSlumlordUI` and the autopilot so that both go the player's way: `Place(pane, item)` drags a held, unworn stack into the purchase or the
rent pane when it pays a line still owed; `FillFromPacks(pane)` drags in, line by line, the stacks a player would pick (coins largest
first, then trade notes smallest first) and names the first line short; `PressBuy` and `PressPay` check before they send (a guardian
open; for Buy the dwelling unowned, no house owned, the pane covering the price; for Pay rent owed and a pane not empty) and leave
`ErrorLine` when a check refuses. The panes empty when another guardian opens.

**The actions.** `BuyHouse` and `PayRent` (lane Use, 10 s, never retried) are confirmed by ACE's lines and refused by name (protocol.md
5.6); ACE's silent refusals time out with a warning that names them. `RecallHouse` (lane Magic, the lifestone recall's limit) is confirmed
by the teleport, refused by WeenieError (YouMustOwnHouseToUseCommand 0x047F and the recalls' others). `QueryHouse` (lane Query, 5 s) is
confirmed by the HouseData or HouseStatus that answers it. `/house recall` sends the recall; the other `/house` subcommands say they are
not built (`TODO(villa-house-subcommands)`).

**The live proof.** `--scenario=villa-proof` (test-tools account, Lifestone Throwaway only) grants what the test needs by the mod's verbs
(M6 D10), buys apartment 4051 through the window, pays its rent, recalls home from Holtburg and moves a Handy Healing Kit into the storage
chest and back, each step checked before and after, and ends with `[villa] verdict villa=proved ...`.

## 117. The villa's steps (M6 villa)

The pieces the climb calls to buy and keep a villa, each an `IStation` in `Session/Housing/` (wired into the level up job by section 118), each check, act, check with a named recovery and one line, the way a player does it (the guardian window `GuardianWindowModel`, Use, Give, MoveToPack, `/house recall`). Facts: `VillaFacts.cs` (the block slumlordvilla1401-1440's two dwellings at 0x9DAF with their guardians, house portals, basements 0x038B/0x038C and storage chests; the price on the block; the climber's account opening `ClimberAccountOpensVillas`), `LockpickFacts` (Merchant 1387 at 0xABB30102, 233 pyreals), `WritFacts` (the four stone caves, Holtburg's Agent of the Arcanum 0x7A9B4038 and his two lines), all checked by `VillaFactsSqlTests`; research in `cache/m6/villa/writ-caves.md`. The rules are pure (`VillaRules.cs`, `VillaRulesTests`): `WritRule` (Need, PlanHandIn, NextFetch), `LockpickRule`, `VillaPurchaseRule`, `StorageRule`, `RentRule`.
- **The stone fetches**: quest files `minor-shivering-stone`, `minor-stinging-stone`, `minor-sparking-stone` beside `minor-smoldering-stone` (go, pick-up; the hour's timer; no ladder), run by the quest station. The travel file gains `holtburg-to-wilderness`, `facility-hub-to-blackmire`, `network-to-mayoi` and `mayoi-to-west-villas` with their four places. On the dats (`TownNetworkWalkDatTests.Villa.cs` and the hop theory) Sparking's whole route walks; Shivering's run stops at the igloo's door (`TODO(villa-shivering-igloo-walk)`), Stinging's at the Blackmire Temple portal in the hub (`TODO(villa-blackmire-portal-ground)`) and at the cave's way in (`TODO(villa-stinging-cave-walk)`); `WritRule.NextFetch` passes those caves by name.
- **`writ-hand-in`** (`WritHandInStation`): stones to the Agent in pairs; after each give the Agent's line (first stone, or the writ line and the writ count up by one); busy is `recovery=give-after-busy`; a half pair left is `half_pending=yes`.
- **`lockpick-buy`** (`LockpickBuyStation`): refused with one held; the Merchant's shop, `CheckedBuy.Judge`, one Buy, the count and the coin after; home by Lifestone Recall. Since M6 16 E5b the buy is the vendor counter's (`VendorCounter.Buy`): a short coin that the main pack's trade notes cover goes on, and a note is changed at his counter when his mask takes one (`TODO(m6-lockpick-note-mask)`: his mask is not in the notes; the villa schedule's own weighing still reads the coin alone).
- **`villa-purchase`** (`VillaPurchaseStation(block, opensAt)`): refused before the account's opening, with a house owned, below the block's level, or with the price not all in the packs (each short line named); the dwellings of the block in order (an owned one `recovery=next-house`), the guardian's Use, `FillFromPacks(Buy)`, `PressBuy`, then the HouseData (`recovery=query-after-buy`) owned, of the block's kind, at the dwelling, the writs and the lockpick spent.
- **`villa-storage`** (`StorageTripStation(items)`): attuned, worn and unheld items stay; `/house recall` (`recovery=recall-again`), the house portal (fails `storage:house-portal-walk` until `TODO(villa-house-portal-walk)`), each chest opened, each move checked in the chest's view (`recovery=move-refused`, `recovery=next-chest`), closed, home (`recovery=recall-home-again`).
- **`villa-rent`** (`RentStation(margin)`): a HouseQuery, then due inside the margin (late is due at once); `/house recall`, the guardian, `FillFromPacks(Rent)`, `PressPay`, "Maintenance paid." and a paid HouseData (`recovery=query-after-pay`).

## 118. The villa in the climb (M6 villa; `--autopilot-villa`)

**The switch.** `--autopilot-villa` (default on) runs the villa schedule in the level up job's own loop (not a task, not the den run). Every
`autopilot cycle` line ends `villa=off` or `villa=on,<phase>,writs:<held>/<wanted>,stones:<n>,half:yes|no,pyreals:<held>/<price>,per_h:<trend>`:
the phase (`unread`, `gather` before the account's opening, `buy` after it, `owned`), the writs against their goal, the minor stones held, the half
pair at the Agent, the coins and notes against the price (the rent's money line once a house is owned), and the money's change an hour over the run
(`n/a` for its first 15 minutes).

**When.** At the logistics trip's end (a town trip), after a ladder errand that waited for the sale, `VillaSchedule.Decide` weighs, in order, each
step once a boundary and never again in a run after it failed: the rent (`RentRule`, 3 days' margin, a late rent at once); the purchase
(`VillaPurchaseRule`: no house, the price in the packs; open at once unless `--autopilot-villa-account-age=ace`); the Crude Lockpick (`LockpickRule`, while no
house is owned and none is held); the hand-in (two stones, or one with the half pair); one stone fetch; the storage trip. Each weighed step is one
line `villa: weigh <step>: <token>: <why>`; the step that runs, `villa: <who>: step <step> (<token>): ...`. After a step ends well the schedule is
asked again (the lockpick, then the purchase; a fetch, then its hand-in). Nothing is weighed while `GameState.HouseStatus` is unread: one
HouseQuery a session is sent by the first tick of the job (`villa: check before: the house status is unread`).

**The writ pace.** `VillaSchedule.Pace`: the writs wanted (no house: the price's 5 and the first period's 2; a house with rent
owed: the writs owed, by the period's end; rent paid: one period's writs by the next end) and the stones to fetch (`WritRule.Need`). By default
the purchase is open at once (the owner, 2026-11-16: a house needs no account age; the server mod sets ACE's `house_15day_account` false and
`VillaFacts.ClimberAccountOpensVillas` is `DateTimeOffset.MinValue`), so with no house the pace is `open`: the writs are wanted now, and each
town trip fetches a stone from every walkable cave its hour's timer allows (one fetch a cave a boundary, the schedule asked again after each),
which is the fastest the two caves allow (`ceil(stones / 2)` hours). Under the retail flag (`--autopilot-villa-account-age=ace`, to match a server
started with `LIFESTONE_ACE_HOUSE_ACCOUNT_AGE=ace`; the opening `VillaFacts.ClimberAccountOpensVillasRetail`, 2026-11-24 22:51:38 UTC, which the
purchase spec carries as `opens-at=`) and for the rent, the pace is spread: the window (the hours to the deadline less a day), the fastest (each
walkable cave one stone a timer), the spacing (the window over the stones); a fetch is due when none is recorded (`first`), when the spacing has
passed since the last stone fetch the timers recorded (`on-pace`), or at every boundary once the window is no more than the fastest (`behind`);
else `ahead`. The fetch is a ladder errand of the quest station on the cave's file (`StartErrand`, from home, ready and buffed), the first
walkable cave its timer allows (`WritRule.NextFetch`; Shivering and Stinging are passed by their TODOs); it counts as `VillaFetches`, not
`errands=`.

**The steps.** The other steps run in the Trip state as station kind `villa` (`VillaStations`, arg `step=`); `villa: ended step= ok= reason=`
reads the station's line. A failure is `failed:villa:<step>:<reason>`, remembered for the run, and she goes home by the recovery's way (as after a
failed ladder errand); a cut step waits for the next boundary; a death or the survival layer's leave out of a step remembers it for the run. The
hand-in's `half_pending=` is kept for the session (`VillaMemory`). The storage trip's items are the held, unworn great-cantrip pieces and kept-aside
finds (no pack, focus or rotation gear); it is held by name (`walk-missing`) while `StorageTripStation.HousePortalWalkEstablished` is false
(`TODO(villa-house-portal-walk)`). The sale never offers a Writ of Refuge or a Crude Lockpick (`ResupplyRun.QuestItemWcids`).

## 119. The fight's fills: what pays (M6 heal spend)

**The finding.** The simulator plays her fight by the client's own rules (`tools\fight-sim.ps1 matchup`, [fight-sim.md](fight-sim.md),
"With her heals"). Against the Tusker Retreat's six (`--pack "11x3,22510x2,236x1"`) at run 5's level-10 bars, the vitals policy's fills
cost her 387 mana and 60.5 s a fight, against 166 mana and 27.9 s with only the emergency's heals (the means of four runs of 2,000 fights).
The trace (`--trace`) showed three causes. With six on her the policy topped up every vital whose whole give fitted (13 presses, 13 stamina
drains and 7 health drains in the first fight), every second of it under all six, and the health those seconds cost came back as more
drains. Drain Health Other IV, which Winnie's Life Magic casts at 14% (the simulator's `her means` line), was priced as if it always landed,
and the health top-up chose it because its small give fitted first (five fizzles in a row in one traced fight). And at a bar of 63 stamina
with no Mana Conversion, a stamina drain was valued at a full bar's press rate, so under the mana floor it ran a loop that gave nothing: a
drain and two presses cost 40 mana and gave 41.

**The rule** (`Vitals/VitalsPolicy.cs`; the order of the decision is unchanged, so `FightScenario` calls it as before and the simulator's
`InFightRules` only fills the new facts):

1. **Each level at its expected give and cost.** `FillLevel.Chance` is the cast chance on her live Life Magic (`GearCasts.Chance`), and
   `FillLevel.Lands` a drain's share past its source's resist (`ManaConversionModel.SkillChance` on the source's Magic Defense, as the bolt's
   land is read). A fizzle gives nothing and costs 5 (ACE `Player_Magic.cs` `CalculateManaUsage`, 566-572 @95ef426d); a resist gives nothing
   and costs the cast.
2. **A mana fill pays only over the mana its seconds cost in health.** `PressPays`: the press's expected give, less its expected cost, less
   `IncomingMana` (the recent incoming, `RecentHits`, times the cast's seconds, times `VitalsPrices.HealMana`, the mana a health point of the
   drain the policy prices best) is over 0. `StaminaDrainNet`: the presses the drain feeds, walked down the bar from where it leaves her (a
   press takes its share of the bar it is cast from, `BuffStatMods.Transfer`), less the presses without it, less the drain's own cost and its
   own seconds' `IncomingMana`. The floors read the same test: under the mana floor a press that does not pay is not cast, nor a stamina
   drain, and the mana order decides. The upkeep's fill still reads `StaminaDrainNets`, the full bar's rate.
3. **A health top-up waits for the best-priced level to fit** (at its whole give, as `press_waits_for_best` makes the press wait): a level that
   fits sooner only because it gives less is dearer a point.
4. **With more than one creature on her** (`VitalsPolicyFacts.Attackers`), a health top-up waits for the next kill (`HealthTopUpWaits`): its
   seconds are the same after it, the kill takes its share out of the incoming, and another creature stays as the drain's source; the health
   floor and the emergency stand guard meanwhile. A drain whose damage pays for its seconds (`TransferPick.KillSeconds` at or under 0) does
   not wait.
5. **Unchanged:** the floors fill at once; a bolt that likely kills goes first; the upkeep; the emergency and its lines (M5 D91); every
   decision with one creature on her or none read; a mana top-up that pays.

**Measured and dropped: a mana top-up that waits while her mana covers the kills.** A sixth rule held a press or stamina drain above the
floor while her mana, with what she regenerates, paid for the bolts that kill every creature on her and the heals that clear needs. It cut
the Retreat's mana no further, and it ran her dry more often where the fills carry her: the Tusker Cave's five Crimsonbacks
(`matchup --pack "1627x5" --her Qwinnie`, seven runs of each, back to back on one save against the tool at `5a8cdee8`)
went from 0.46% out of mana to 0.71%; with the wait taken out (four runs) it read 0.50%. On the lead's big-pack rows, where the fills carry her (the Retreat's ring of eight and its
corners of nine and ten), it did no better than the rules above.

**What the fight reads** (`FightScenario.VitalsPolicy.cs` `TryPolicyFacts`): `Attackers` is self-defence's list (`AttackersNow`); each
level's chance and a drain's share past its source's resist (`CastChanceOf`, `LandsOn`). The `vitals policy:` line adds `heal mana a point`
and `attackers`.

**The evidence** (`tools\fight-sim.ps1` on `m6/heal-spend` against the same tool at `5a8cdee8`, 2026-11-19; each row the mean of the runs
named, 2,000 fights a run; ACE's own rolls are unseeded, so every run's blows differ, and each run's "no fills" row plays the same blows with
the policy's fills left out: the paired column is each run's deaths with the fills less its deaths without, meaned, the fair read of whether
the fills cost or save lives when two runs' blows differ):

Reading the table:

- **Winnie's own bars.** The deaths' mean moves with each run's blows (the "no fills" rows of the same runs read 2.5% before and 2.8%
  after); against its own blows each run's fills save 1.30 points of deaths now and 0.78 before. Out of mana is still most fights: 39 health
  and 160 mana do not clear six level-20 tuskers, so this is a pull she should not take, not a fill to tune.
- **The corner of ten.** One death in 16,000 fights before, two in 16,000 after, inside the run-to-run band (the "no fills" rows of the same
  runs read 0.0 to 0.2% a run); paired, the fills save 0.06 points before and 0.03 after. Out of mana fell from 1.83% to 0.45%.
- **The ring and the Kin (14 at once).** A flee moment both ways, as the lead read it: out of mana 100.00% to 91.25%. She spends more mana
  there (771.4 to 1,182.1) because she lasts longer before the mana runs out.
- **The Holding.** No press or stamina drain fires (`BSD Mage` at level 127 holds 457 mana with Mana Conversion); its fills are the health
  floor's drains, which this change leaves as they were, so its rows differ by their blows: paired, the fills save 6.68 and 5.20 points of
  deaths against 6.31 and 3.14 before. A floor at her whole health giving way to the kill was weighed and is refuted here (those
  drains save the deaths) and in the Cave below, where the fills carry her: the floor is kept.
- **Won fights end fuller.** A won fight ends this far under the mana it began with, before and after: the Retreat's six at level 10 64.2
  and 63.0, at level 14 71.8 and 63.2, the Burrow's three 52.5 and 52.1, the Lodge's six 86.3 and 61.1, its nine 138.7 and 64.7, the ring of
  eight 80.4 and 62.9, the corners 80.8 and 64.1, 87.6 and 66.2. Winnie's own bars are the exception (133.5 and 146.0).
- **The Cave** (`matchup 1627 --her Qwinnie`, `--pack "1627x5"`). Her save moved while this ran (she climbs live): the first baseline read
  level 6, health 60, stamina 115, mana 115 and Force Bolt I and died in every fight of five; the final runs read level 9, health 87,
  stamina 156, mana 166 and Flame Bolt III. So the Cave is four pairs run back to back on the level-9 save. Five at once: deaths 0.08% to
  0.05%, out of mana 0.40% to 0.45% (32 against 36 fights in 8,000), mana 359.3 to 357.3, 53.2 to 52.9 s. One kind, one to six on her:
  six on her out of mana 14.0% to 9.7%, deaths 0.45% to 0.40%; one to five within 0.2 points.
- **The rank** (`rank --her Winnie --min-level 5 --max-level 40 --bars "health=84,stamina=154,mana=161"`, its healed columns, 300 fights at
  each of the two sizes around the census's pack): the Tusker Retreat 0x5C49 (pack 6.3) dies 0.1% to 0.0%, out of mana 0.0% to 0.0%; the
  Tusker Lodge 0x5749 (pack 8.9) 0.0% and 0.0% both; the Tusker Burrow 0x5748 (pack 3.3) 0.0% and 0.0% both.

**What is assumed, named.** The simulator ends a fight at its last kill, so the time between pulls, where the pull's rest and dance pay back
what a fight ended without (`PolicyPullRule`, section 92), is not played (`TODO(fight-sim-between-pulls)`, fight-sim.md "What is not
played"); on every row but Winnie's own bars the won fights end as near their starting mana or nearer than before, so these
rows add no rest. A level's chances are read from her live skill and the source's Magic Defense in the creature tables; one not read is
taken as sure, as before.
